sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: For which two legal purposes does Arizona MVD collect your Social Security number, and does it print as your license number?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Your Social Security number is used to verify your identity and to comply with child support laws, and it is not used as your driver license number.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: Which driving roles match Arizona's Class G, Class D, Class M, and Classes A, B, and C licenses?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Arizona issues licenses by class: Class G for graduated, Class D for operator, Class M for motorcycle, and Classes A, B and C for commercial drivers.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: Where does Arizona place your Class M privilege when you combine motorcycle riding with another license class?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: When a Class M license is combined with another class, the motorcycle privilege is added as an endorsement on the back of the current license.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.front: What vehicles may you drive on a Class D operator license, and what is the minimum age to apply?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.expected_back: A Class D operator license lets you drive any vehicle that does not require a motorcycle or commercial license, and you must be at least eighteen to apply for one.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.front: Which license or endorsement is required for a motorcycle or motor-driven cycle, and how young may you apply?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.expected_back: Riding a motorcycle or motor driven cycle requires a Class M license or endorsement, which you can apply for from age sixteen.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.front: Between Arizona's Class D operator license and Class M motorcycle license, which opens at sixteen and which waits for eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.expected_back: A Class D operator license needs age eighteen, while a Class M motorcycle license can be applied for at sixteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.front: What permit hold time—and which two training or practice options—must an under-eighteen Class M applicant complete?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.expected_back: An under-eighteen motorcycle applicant needs at least six months holding an Arizona motorcycle permit, plus either an MVD-approved motorcycle course or a parent certifying thirty hours of supervised riding.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.front: Which license classes cover commercial motor vehicles, and where are their testing rules published?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.expected_back: A commercial driver license in Class A, B or C is required for commercial motor vehicles, and its requirements are covered in the separate CDL manual rather than this one.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: How old must you be for a graduated or motorcycle instruction permit compared with an operator instruction permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: You may get a graduated and or or motorcycle instruction permit once you are at least fifteen years and six months old, but an operator permit requires age eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: Which Arizona instruction permit waits until age eighteen while the other two open at fifteen years and six months?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Permit ages split by permit type: fifteen years and six months for a graduated or motorcycle permit, but eighteen for an operator permit.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: Who must sit right beside a graduated or operator permit holder whenever the car is moving?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: A graduated or operator permit holder must drive with a Class A, B, C or D licensed driver who is at least twenty-one and sits in the seat beside them.
pills: CLASS A B C OR D

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: For how many months do Arizona graduated and operator instruction permits stay valid?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Graduated and operator instruction permits are valid for twelve months.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: Which passenger, highway, and lighting restrictions bind an Arizona motorcycle instruction-permit rider?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: A motorcycle permit holder may not carry passengers, may not ride on freeways or interstate highways, and may not ride between sunset and sunrise or whenever light is too poor to see people or vehicles five hundred feet away.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: How long does an Arizona motorcycle permit last, and what cap limits renewing it?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: A motorcycle permit is valid for seven months and can be renewed only once within a twenty-four-month period.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: How does the lifespan of a graduated or operator permit compare with a motorcycle permit?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: Permit lengths differ by type: a graduated or operator permit lasts twelve months, while a motorcycle permit lasts seven months with one renewal allowed in twenty-four months.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: Where online does Arizona MVD host practice material for the written permit check?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: MVD offers practice for the written test on its website, azdot.gov slash mvd.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: What check must you pass before MVD issues an Arizona instruction permit—and which commercial permit is excluded?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: You must pass the Division written test before MVD will issue an Arizona instruction permit, though this rule does not cover Commercial Learner's Permits.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: Does the standard rule requiring the Division written check before an instruction permit cover Commercial Learner's Permits?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: The written test is required before an Arizona instruction permit, but the rule does not apply to a Commercial Learner's Permit.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: If you held a learner's permit in another state before moving, how does Arizona treat those months?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Arizona credits applicants for the time they held an instruction permit in another state.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Which age bracket receives an Arizona Class G graduated license, and what vehicles does it cover?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: A graduated license goes to applicants who are at least sixteen but under eighteen and lets them drive any vehicle that needs no motorcycle or commercial license.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: During the first six months on Class G, which overnight hours are off-limits—and who in the front seat lifts curfew?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: During the first six months, a graduated license holder must stay off the road from midnight to five a.m., except when the front passenger seat is occupied by a parent or legal guardian holding a valid Class A, B, C or D license.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: What exact clock window and how many initial months define Arizona's Class G nighttime restriction?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: The graduated night limit runs from midnight to five a.m. and lasts only for the first six months of the license.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: Which four solo trip purposes let a first-six-months Class G teen drive legally between midnight and five a.m.?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: The night limit also does not apply when the teen is driving directly to or from a sanctioned school-sponsored activity, a job, a sanctioned religious activity or a family emergency.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: How does who may supervise an instruction permit differ from who lifts the Class G night restriction?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: The permit supervisor must be at least twenty-one and hold a Class A, B, C or D license, while the adult who lifts the graduated night limit must be the teen's parent or legal guardian.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: During the first six Class G months, how many non-sibling passengers under eighteen may ride without a licensed parent up front?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: During the first six months, a graduated license holder may not drive with more than one passenger under age eighteen, unless those passengers are the teen's siblings or a licensed parent or legal guardian rides in the front passenger seat.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: Do your own brothers and sisters under eighteen count against Arizona's one-teen Class G passenger cap?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: Siblings never count against the graduated passenger limit, but a non-sibling passenger under eighteen does, and only one is allowed without a licensed parent or guardian up front.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: How long must you hold an Arizona instruction permit before applying for Class G, and what status must it have?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: To get a graduated license you must have held an Arizona instruction permit for at least six months, and the permit must still be valid when you apply.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: How do the two separate six-month periods in Arizona's teen licensing timeline differ?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: The permit must be held at least six months before a graduated license, which is a different six-month period from the restricted first months of the graduated license itself.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: Alongside six permit months, which two training alternatives qualify a teen for a Class G license?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: A graduated-license applicant must also finish an MVD-approved Arizona driver education program, or a parent or guardian must certify the required supervised practice in writing.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: How many total and night supervised hours must a parent certify—and what reduced option exists after specific safety courses?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: The certified practice is at least thirty hours of supervised driving with at least ten at night, or twenty hours with at least six at night when the minor completed a Traffic Survival School or Defensive Driving course.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: Which two specific courses reduce supervised Arizona teen practice from thirty-and-ten hours down to twenty-and-six?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Supervised practice is thirty hours with ten at night in the normal case, but drops to twenty hours with six at night only for a minor who completed Traffic Survival School or a Defensive Driving course.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: Who may MVD excuse from Arizona's six-month permit, driver ed, and practice-hour requirements?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: Someone already holding a current and valid license from another state may be excused from the permit, driver education and practice-hour requirements.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: Does Arizona force a Class G driver to swap for a Class D operator card upon turning eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: A graduated license holder does not have to switch to an operator license at age eighteen but may choose to.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: Why should you read the fine print included with an Arizona traffic citation right away?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: If you get a citation you may be eligible for the Arizona Supreme Court's Defensive Driving Program, so read the information that comes with the citation carefully.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: What mandatory consequence hits an under-eighteen Class G driver after a first traffic-violation conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: For a driver under eighteen with a graduated license, a first traffic-violation conviction means mandatory Traffic Survival School and the violation goes on the driving record.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: What suspension lengths hit an under-eighteen Class G driver on a second traffic conviction and on a third?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: A second conviction brings a three-month suspension of the driving privilege, and a third brings a six-month suspension, each also recorded on the driving record.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: At which conviction number do license suspensions start for an under-eighteen Class G driver?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: For a graduated driver under eighteen, the first conviction means Traffic Survival School, not a suspension; suspensions start at the second conviction with three months and rise to six months at the third.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: What happens when a Class G teen gets caught breaking the midnight curfew or one-friend passenger rule?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: Breaking the curfew or passenger restrictions brings extra penalties, including fines and a mandatory extension of the six-month restricted period.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: How many curfew or passenger convictions trigger suspension—and what else suspends a teen's privilege?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: A third conviction for curfew or passenger violations results in suspension, and so do convictions for other violations, including alcohol-related ones.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: Who must sign an Arizona instruction permit or license application when the applicant is under eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: If you are under eighteen, at least one adult must sign your instruction permit or driver license application.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: What legal responsibility does an adult accept by signing a minor's permit or license application?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: The adult who signs for a minor becomes responsible for any negligence or willful misconduct while the minor drives.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: How many parents sign when parents are married, unmarried with joint custody, or holding sole custody?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: The signer is one natural or adoptive parent when the parents are married to each other, both parents when unmarried with joint custody, or the one parent with sole custody.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: Why must unmarried parents with joint custody bring two signatures when married parents need only one?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: Married parents need only one parent's signature, while unmarried parents sharing joint custody must both sign.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: When parents do not sign, which three documented adults—including an employer—may sign for a minor?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: Other permitted signers are a legal guardian or a foster parent living with the minor (each with proof), or the minor's employer if the parents' death certificates are shown.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: Who must witness adult signatures for a minor, and does signing the permit cover the later license?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: The signatures must be witnessed by an MVD agent or a notary public, and signatures given for the instruction permit must be given again for the driver license.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: Which three identifying facts must appear on a request to cancel a minor's driver license?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: A cancellation request must state the license number, full name and date of birth of the person whose license is being canceled.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: Who does federal law require to register with Selective Service, and within what window around age eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: Federal law requires male United States citizens and male aliens living in the country to register with the Selective Service System within thirty days of turning eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.front: For a male applicant under twenty-six, which three MVD transactions carry automatic Selective Service consent—and which stays optional?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.expected_back: By applying for an original, renewal or reinstatement license or ID, a male applicant under twenty-six consents to Selective Service registration, while for a duplicate the consent is optional.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.front: Which single MVD card request lets a male under twenty-six treat Selective Service registration as optional?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.expected_back: Selective Service consent is automatic for a male under twenty-six applying for an original, renewal or reinstatement credential, but optional when he applies only for a duplicate.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.front: How does MVD handle Selective Service data for eighteen-to-twenty-five-year-olds versus teens under eighteen—and does it enlist you?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.expected_back: Applicants aged eighteen to twenty-five have their registration information sent to Selective Service immediately, while for those under eighteen it is held and sent automatically at eighteen; registering does not mean joining the military.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: Where must you position your car if forced to leave it along an uncurbed highway versus a curbed street?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: If you must leave your vehicle on a highway or street, pull onto the shoulder as far from traffic as you can, or as close to the curb as possible where there is one.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: Which three brake, transmission, and ignition steps secure a vehicle before you step out?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Before leaving it, set the parking brake, shift into park or leave a manual transmission in gear, and switch off the engine.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: After securing a disabled car roadside, what should you place outside and where should you wait if safe?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Put out proper emergency signals and, if possible, stay with the vehicle until help arrives.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: What simple security step belongs whenever you have no choice except walking away from your stopped vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: If you have to walk away from the vehicle, lock it.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: Name three everyday access or crossing zones where parking is always illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Parking is illegal on a sidewalk, in front of any public or private driveway, and inside the boundaries of an intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: Besides parking directly on a crosswalk, within how many feet of an intersection crosswalk is parking banned?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Parking is illegal on a crosswalk, and also anywhere closer than twenty feet to a crosswalk at an intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Under what sole circumstance is parking permitted along a freeway or interstate highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Parking on any freeway or interstate highway is illegal except in an emergency.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: When a genuine breakdown forces a freeway stop, which four securing and warning steps still apply?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Freeway parking is banned except for emergencies, and an emergency stop still calls for the shoulder, the brake, the engine off and warning signals.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: Even away from hydrants or crosswalks, what two broad conditions make parking unlawful anywhere?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: You may not park where signs prohibit it or in any way that creates a hazard for other vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: Within how many feet of a fire hydrant is parking prohibited in Arizona?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Parking within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant is illegal.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: Within how many feet of a railroad crossing is parking illegal in Arizona?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Parking within fifty feet of a railroad crossing is illegal.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: Line up Arizona's three no-parking distances from shortest to longest — hydrant, crosswalk, and railroad?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: The no-parking distances differ by object: fifteen feet from a fire hydrant, twenty feet from a crosswalk at an intersection, and fifty feet from a railroad crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: May a driver park on a bridge span or inside a highway tunnel?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: You may not park on a bridge or inside a tunnel.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: What traffic mission are freeways and interstate highways engineered to handle?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Freeways and interstate highways are built to carry higher-speed traffic safely.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: Between drivers already cruising on the freeway and drivers entering from an on-ramp, who must yield?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Drivers entering a freeway must yield to the traffic already on it and are responsible for merging safely.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Walk through the speed, signal, check, and merge sequence for joining a freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: To merge, match your speed to the traffic in the freeway's right lane, signal, check the traffic around you and merge carefully once it is clear.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: Which painted stripe and ramp zone must you never cut across while entering a freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: While entering a freeway, do not cross a solid line or drive through a gore area.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: How do solid white lines and gore areas restrict both freeway entries and freeway exits?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: A solid line is off-limits both when entering and when exiting a freeway, and so is the gore area on entry.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: What communication step is mandatory before peeling off onto a freeway exit?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Signal before you exit a freeway.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: What dedicated lane helps you leave most freeways without slowing main traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Most freeways have deceleration lanes to help you exit, and proper braking gives a smooth exit.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: Contrast how you manage speed on a freeway entrance ramp versus a freeway exit lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: On entry you match the speed of the freeway right lane, while on exit most freeways give you a deceleration lane in which to brake smoothly.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: Which two habits prevent crashes when queueing onto a busy, backed-up freeway exit?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: When exiting in heavy traffic, keep a space cushion behind the vehicle ahead and do not cross a solid line.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What roadway layout defines a divided highway or freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: A divided highway or freeway has separate roadways for the two directions, often with several lanes on each side.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: What distinguishes a controlled-access expressway or freeway from an ordinary highway with traffic lights?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Some highways meet other roads at traffic signals, while controlled-access highways have no signals or intersections and are entered and left only by ramps; these are called expressways or freeways.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: When should you move into the target lane for entering or leaving a highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: Get into the proper lane well in advance so you can enter or leave the highway safely.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: At what point relative to the exit ramp must your turn signal already be flashing?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Signal your exit before you reach the exit ramp.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: Combine your right-of-way duty and throttle goal as you join a fast highway lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: When joining a highway, yield to drivers already on it and speed up to match their speed as you enter the travel lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: What two dangerous reactions are banned if you miss your exit, and what is the right fix?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: If you miss your exit, do not stop and never back up; leave at the next exit and follow the signs to rejoin the road going the other way.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: How do you legally get back to your destination after sailing past your highway exit?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: A missed exit is handled by driving on to the next exit and following signs back, never by stopping or reversing.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.front: May you ever shift into reverse on a freeway shoulder to catch an exit you just passed?
sec08-card-sec08-F41.expected_back: If you miss a freeway exit, do not back up; you must go on to the next exit.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: On any roadway with two or more lanes, which half belongs to your travel — and what two exceptions apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: On any road with two or more lanes, drive on the right half except when passing or when signs say otherwise.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: On a highway with three or more lanes one way, why can the far right lane move either slower or faster?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: On highways with three or more lanes in one direction, the right lane usually serves entering and exiting traffic, so it may move slower or faster than the other lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: Don't assume the right lane of a three-lane freeway is only slow — what two movements make it faster too?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: The right lane of a highway with three or more lanes can carry traffic both slower and faster than the other lanes, because it serves entering and exiting vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: During heavy rush hour on a multi-lane freeway, why do through drivers often leave the right lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: At rush hour, drivers who are not exiting may want to stay out of the right lane to leave room for vehicles entering and leaving.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: Which four merge, signal, speed, and spacing habits keep multi-lane highway cruising safe?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: Watch for vehicles merging into your lane, signal your own lane changes, keep within posted speed limits and do not tailgate.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: What is a freeway gore area, and which two vehicle actions inside it violate Arizona law?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: Driving over or parking on any part of a gore area, the space between a through roadway and an entrance or exit ramp, is against the law.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: Pinpoint where the gore area sits on a freeway and both unlawful uses of it?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: A gore area is the wedge between the through road and a ramp; driving over it and parking in it are both against the law.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: Where should you pull over if your car breaks down on a freeway — and what spot must you avoid?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: If you need help on a freeway, pull as far as you can onto the right shoulder and avoid stopping on or near the ramps.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: Which two daytime signals and two after-dark additions show you need help on a freeway shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: To signal for help, turn on your emergency flashers or raise the hood; after dark, switch on the inside dome light or set out flares or portable warning signals.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: Contrast daytime freeway help signals with what you add once darkness falls?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: By day you signal for freeway help with flashers or a raised hood, while after dark you add the dome light or flares and portable warning signals.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: While waiting for roadside assistance on a freeway, where should you stay and what is banned?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: Wait for help with your vehicle and do not walk along the freeway.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: What three protective steps apply when you spot a broken-down vehicle ahead on the freeway shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: When you come upon a disabled vehicle on the freeway, slow down, move over and pass around it with caution.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: What painted pavement symbol identifies High Occupancy Vehicle lanes in Arizona?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: HOV lanes are marked by white diamonds painted in the roadway.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: During posted weekday HOV hours, what minimum headcount — or which two vehicle types — may use the lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: At the posted times on weekdays, a vehicle carrying fewer than two persons, counting the driver, may not use an HOV lane, which is then reserved for car pools, motorcycles and buses.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: Does Arizona's two-person HOV minimum include the driver, and does it apply 24/7 or at posted weekday times?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: The HOV rule counts the driver as one of the two persons required, and it binds only at the posted weekday times.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.front: What awaits a solo motorist caught cheating Arizona's HOV restriction during posted hours?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.expected_back: A motorist who breaks the HOV restriction faces substantial fines and penalties.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.front: How should you cross the solid white line separating an Arizona HOV lane from regular lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.expected_back: Always signal and take care when crossing the solid white line into or out of an HOV lane.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: Pair the three vehicle groups eligible during restricted HOV hours with how they enter or exit?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: Car pools, motorcycles and buses may use an HOV lane during restricted times, and crossing its solid white line requires a signal.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.front: Which two turnaround moves across a freeway median or divider are strictly illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.expected_back: On a freeway, never drive over or across a median or divided-highway separation, and never make a U-turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.front: What lane-change rule and entry-point rule govern every Arizona freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.expected_back: On a freeway, never change lanes without signaling, and get onto the freeway only by an on-ramp.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.front: Where is non-emergency stopping allowed along a freeway, and when may you use the shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.expected_back: Do not park or stop on a freeway except in areas provided for it; parking on the shoulder is banned except in an emergency.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Contrast where you may take a routine freeway break against when shoulder parking becomes legal?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Shoulder parking on a freeway is banned except in an emergency, while stopping is allowed only in areas specially provided.

sec08-card-sec08-F42.front: What two mechanical capabilities should you verify before taking a vehicle onto a high-speed highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F42.expected_back: Before highway driving, make sure your vehicle is in good operating condition and can keep up highway speeds.

sec08-card-sec08-F43.front: What is the general left-lane rule, and how do the far right and far left lanes split jobs on a three-lane highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F43.expected_back: Keep right and use the left lane only to pass; on a three-lane highway, treat the far right lane as the slower through lane and the far left lane as the passing lane.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: Match the far right lane and far left lane of a three-lane highway to their designated roles?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.memory_hook: Far right slower, far left passes
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: On a three-lane highway the far right lane is treated as the slower through lane and the far left lane as the passing lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F44.front: Where between painted lines should your tires track, and which two tools pair for lane changes?
sec08-card-sec08-F44.expected_back: Drive in the middle of your lane between the lines, and use your rearview mirror and turn signals when changing lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F45.front: Which three visual systems regulate road traffic and require complete driver understanding?
sec08-card-sec08-F45.expected_back: Traffic is controlled by signal lights, traffic signs and pavement markings, and you must fully understand them to drive safely.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: What two aspects of intersection traffic do red, yellow, and green signal lights regulate?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Red, yellow and green signal lights stand at many intersections to control the direction and flow of traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Alongside motor-vehicle drivers, which three other groups on the road are legally bound by traffic lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Traffic lights bind pedestrians and bicycle and moped riders as well as motorists.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Under what sole exception may you disobey what an intersection signal light displays?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: You must obey the signal lights unless a police officer directing traffic tells you to do otherwise.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: If a traffic officer waves you through a red light, whose command takes priority?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: A police officer's directions override what the signal light shows.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: What condition must be met before you move through an intersection on a steady green light?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: A green light means you may go through the intersection in the direction the signal allows, if the roadway is clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: Why must you check left and right before accelerating into an intersection on a green light?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Even on green, look left and right for cross traffic before entering, so a red-light runner does not hit you.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: When your signal flips to green, which vehicles still hold priority ahead of you?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: On a fresh green, yield to any vehicle that was already in the intersection when the light changed.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: What upcoming signal change does a steady yellow traffic light announce?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: How does your legal duty on a steady yellow light depend on whether you have entered the intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: On a steady yellow, stop safely if you have not yet entered the intersection, but if you are already in it, keep going and clear it safely.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: How does Arizona law treat accelerating to beat a yellow light before it turns red?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: Speeding up to beat a yellow light is illegal and could cause a crash.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: Where must you come to a full stop for a steady red light, and how long must you wait?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.memory_hook: Stop before line; wait out red
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: On a red light, come to a complete stop before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk, and stay stopped as long as the light is red.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: How does the stopping duty on a steady yellow light differ from a steady red light?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: A steady yellow tells you the red is coming, so you stop if you can do so safely before entering, whereas a steady red requires a complete stop and waiting for as long as it stays red.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: Under what three conditions may you turn right against a steady red traffic light?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Unless a sign forbids it, you may turn right on red after a complete stop once vehicles and pedestrians are clear.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: What mandatory action and sign check govern every right turn on a steady red signal?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: A right turn on a steady red needs a complete stop first and is barred wherever a sign prohibits it.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: When leaving a freeway, where must you brake and shed speed instead of slowing on the main lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: The manual's freeway-exit figure shows the correct exit: do not slow down on the freeway itself, slow down in the exit lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: Which roadside traffic sign carries the exact same legal rule as a flashing red signal light?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop fully, then go on with caution when the way is clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: How should you handle an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution if the roadway is clear.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: How does your required action at a flashing red signal contrast with a flashing yellow signal?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: A flashing red light is treated as a stop sign, while a flashing yellow light only requires slowing down and proceeding with caution.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: May you turn after stopping when facing a lighted red arrow in your turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: A lighted red arrow means you may not turn in its direction; stop and wait for the green signal before turning.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: What signal transition does a lighted steady yellow arrow announce?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: A yellow arrow is the warning that the arrow signal is about to turn red.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: Facing a steady yellow arrow, what should you do before entering versus once already inside the intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Facing a yellow arrow, stop and wait for a green arrow if you have not entered the intersection, or finish your turn and clear it safely if you already have.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: Why should a driver already past the stop bar keep turning when the arrow flips to steady yellow?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: A yellow arrow is a warning that red is next, and a driver already inside the intersection should finish the turn and clear it rather than stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: What steps let you turn legally under a flashing yellow arrow?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn with caution after slowing, if the roadway is clear and you first yield to any oncoming vehicle or pedestrian.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: How does a lighted red arrow differ from a flashing yellow arrow for turning drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: A red arrow forbids the turn until a green signal appears, while a flashing yellow arrow permits the turn after you yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: When a green arrow lights up alone or beside another bulb, what must be true before you go?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: A green arrow, alone or with another light, lets you go in the arrow's direction if you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: How must every driver treat an intersection when its traffic signal lights are dark or out of order?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Treat an intersection whose traffic signal is not working as a four-way stop: stop completely before entering, then go when the roadway is clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: When two cars reach a dark signal at roughly the same moment, who stops and who yields?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: When two vehicles reach such an intersection at about the same time, both stop and the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: At an inoperative traffic light, which driver wins a simultaneous-arrival tie after both come to a stop?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: At a dark signal both vehicles stop, and the tie goes to the driver on the right.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: At an unmarked T-intersection, which street's drivers must yield the right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: At a T intersection, the driver on the street that ends must yield to vehicles on the cross street.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: Between the terminating road and the continuing cross street at a T-intersection, who yields?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: At a T intersection it is the driver on the street that ends who must yield to traffic on the cross street.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: What guides your stopping and yielding duties at a controlled intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: At controlled intersections, obey the signals and signs and yield to other vehicles as they direct.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: Why isn't having the legal right-of-way enough by itself to pull straight into an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: Having the right-of-way does not by itself make it safe to go; check for traffic and pedestrians first.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: Where do you bring your vehicle to a halt at a controlled intersection with pavement markings?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: At a controlled intersection, stop at the stop line.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: How does Arizona treat an open intersection that has no signals, stop signs, or yield signs?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: An intersection with no traffic lights, stop signs or yield signs is treated as a four-way stop, with a full stop before entering.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: What rule links an intersection with a blacked-out traffic signal and an intersection with no controls at all?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: A dark traffic signal and an intersection with no signals or signs at all are handled the same way, as a four-way stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: Does Arizona traffic law grant right-of-way to a driver, or specify who must yield?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: The law requires certain vehicles to yield to others; it never actually gives the right-of-way to any driver, it only says who must yield.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: When is every driver barred from insisting on taking the right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: No one may take the right-of-way if taking it could cause a crash.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: At which types of crosswalks are drivers required to yield to crossing pedestrians?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: You must yield to pedestrians crossing the street in any crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: Once your traffic light turns green, what duty do you still owe people or cars finishing in the intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: After your light turns green you must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles that are in the intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: What does Arizona law require at a school crossing while any person is inside the crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: The law requires a complete stop at any school crossing while anyone is in the crosswalk.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: May you pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian if your adjacent lane looks clear or your signal is green?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: You may not pass a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian, even if your lane is clear or your signal is green.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: How do Arizona's occupied school-crosswalk rule and its stopped-for-pedestrian passing rule protect walkers?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: A school crossing stop is required whenever anyone is in the crosswalk, and a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian may never be passed, even on green.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: For safety, whom does the Arizona manual advise yielding to whenever someone is crossing any street?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: For safety, give the right-of-way to anyone you see crossing any street.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: On a pedestrian-activated crosswalk beacon, what do flashing yellow and solid yellow each signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: At a pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal, flashing yellow means a pedestrian has pressed the signal, and solid yellow means prepare to stop.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: How does flashing yellow differ from solid yellow on a pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Flashing yellow on a pedestrian-activated signal means a pedestrian has pressed the button, while solid yellow means prepare to stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: What must you do when solid red lights illuminate on a pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: Solid red lights at a pedestrian crosswalk signal mean stop, because a pedestrian is in the crosswalk.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: What does flashing red allow on a pedestrian crosswalk beacon once you have stopped?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: Flashing red lights at a pedestrian crosswalk signal mean stop, then go on with caution after the pedestrian has crossed the driver's half of the road.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: On a pedestrian-activated signal, how does solid red differ from wig-wagging flashing red?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: On a pedestrian-activated signal, solid red means stop and stay stopped while the pedestrian is in the crosswalk, whereas flashing red means stop and then go once the pedestrian has cleared your half of the road.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: Which three real-world factors determine a roadway's proper speed limit, and how strictly must posted signs be obeyed?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Road conditions, traffic flow and the number of crashes are used to set a road's proper speed limit, and you must obey every posted limit.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: When no speed sign is posted, what is Arizona's legal limit approaching a school crosswalk?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is fifteen miles per hour as you approach a school crosswalk.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: What default speed limit applies inside an unsigned business or residential district?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour in any business or residential district.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: How does Arizona's unposted school-crosswalk speed limit compare with its unposted business or residential limit?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: A school crosswalk approach defaults to fifteen miles per hour, while a business or residential district defaults to twenty-five miles per hour

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Where no speed limit is posted, what limit governs open highways and city freeways?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is fifty-five miles per hour on open highways or city freeways.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: What default speed limit applies on designated open highways when no sign posts otherwise?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is sixty-five miles per hour on designated open highways.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: When no sign is posted, what is the speed limit along Arizona's rural freeways?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is seventy-five miles per hour on rural freeways.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How do Arizona's unposted highway limits step up across open/city, designated open, and rural freeways?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Open highways and city freeways default to fifty-five miles per hour, designated open highways to sixty-five miles per hour, and rural freeways to seventy-five miles per hour

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: What category of sign is a white speed sign with black lettering, and what does it set?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: A white speed limit sign with black letters is a regulatory sign showing the highest speed you may legally drive.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: What does an orange sign with black numbers communicate at a curve, hill grade, or special spot?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: An orange sign with black letters gives a recommended safe speed for a curve, a grade or another special condition, so slow down until you are sure you can get through safely.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: How does a black-on-white speed sign differ from a black-on-orange speed sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: A white sign with black letters is the legal maximum, while an orange sign with black letters is only a recommended safe speed for that spot.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: What weather and road baseline do posted speed limits assume, and how must you adjust in storms?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Speed limits assume the best driving conditions, so in bad weather lower your speed to one that is reasonable.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: How must your speed change whenever pavement turns wet, snowy, or icy?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: On wet roads, and on roads with snow or ice, reduce your speed appropriately.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: Along with dropping speed, how should you adjust your following distance in bad weather?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: In bad weather, double your following distance from the vehicle ahead as well as slowing down.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Why isn't merely easing off the gas enough by itself when driving in bad weather?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Bad weather calls for both a lower speed and twice the usual following distance, not just one of them.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: How dangerous is driving far too slowly compared with speeding?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Driving too slowly can be just as dangerous as driving too fast.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: Which lane belongs to you whenever you are traveling slower than surrounding traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: Whenever you are slower than the traffic around you, keep to the right lane and let faster vehicles pass.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: What two core purposes do roadside traffic signs serve?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Traffic signs control traffic and give drivers important information.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: How much meaning does a traffic sign's outer shape carry compared with its color or lettering?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: A sign's shape can tell you as much about its meaning as its color or its words.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: In which three Arizona visibility hazards might a sign's silhouette be the only clue you can see?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: In heavy rain, dust storms or fog, the shape may be the only part of a sign you can make out.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Which single traffic sign uses an eight-sided octagon, and what action does it demand?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: The octagon shape is used only for stop signs, which require a complete stop.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: What duty does a downward-pointing triangle sign place on you?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: A triangle-shaped sign requires you to yield the right-of-way to cross traffic or merging traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: How does an eight-sided octagon sign differ from a three-sided triangle sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: An octagon always means stop, while a triangle means yield to cross or merging traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: What do rectangular regulatory signs govern, and what turn rules commonly appear on them?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: Rectangular regulatory signs control traffic and direct your speed and direction, such as go straight or turn left, no U-turn, no left turn and no right turn.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: What upcoming roadway feature do turn, curve, and winding-road signs alert you to?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: Turn, curve and winding road signs warn drivers of bends in the roadway ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: What does a small square yellow plaque mounted beneath a curve warning sign indicate?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: Small yellow square signs may be mounted below a curve sign to show the safe speed through the curve.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: On a curve warning assembly, how do the upper curve sign and the small lower yellow square split duties?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.memory_hook: Diamond warns bend, square sets speed
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: The small yellow square that may sit under a curve sign is the one that shows the safe speed through that curve, while the curve sign itself only warns of the bend.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: What zone begins at a sideways pennant-shaped sign?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: A pennant-shaped sign marks where a no-passing zone begins.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: What general message do yellow diamond-shaped signs deliver?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: Yellow diamond-shaped signs warn of a possible danger ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: How does a sideways yellow pennant sign differ from a yellow diamond sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: A pennant marks the start of a no-passing zone, while a yellow diamond warns of a possible hazard ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: What shape is a permanent school crossing warning sign, and when might children be crossing there?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: A permanent five-sided, pentagon-shaped school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing at any time of day.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: Which two background colors are used on Arizona school crossing signs?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: School crossing signs may be yellow, and many Arizona school districts are posting yellow-green ones.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: When portable school signs stand in the roadway, what is the speed limit and where does that zone run?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.memory_hook: Fifteen from first sign past crossing
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: You must also obey portable signs sometimes set in the middle of the road, and from the first sign until past the school crossing sign the top speed is fifteen miles per hour

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: Which speed limit governs the street once portable school-zone signs have been taken off the roadway?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: When the portable school signs are not out, the area's normal speed limit applies.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: How do portable school signs turn Arizona's fifteen-mile-per-hour school zone on and off?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: The school-zone limit of fifteen miles per hour runs from the first portable sign until past the crossing sign, and it lapses when those portable signs are removed.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: Is passing another vehicle ever legal inside an Arizona school crossing zone?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: Passing another vehicle in a school crossing zone is prohibited.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: What two duties apply at a school crosswalk staffed by a crossing guard?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: Follow the crossing guard's instructions and stop completely whenever anyone is in the crosswalk.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: What single hazard ahead is announced by a circular traffic sign?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: A circle-shaped railroad warning sign tells you a railroad crossing is ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: Which sign silhouette warns of a school crossing, and which warns of an upcoming railroad crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: A pentagon is the school crossing shape, while a circle is the railroad warning shape.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: While the round sign warns ahead, what does the railroad crossing sign itself mark?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: The railroad crossing sign marks the exact location of the crossing.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: How far back from the nearest rail must you stop when lights, bells, gates, or a flagger warn of rail traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: Stop no closer than fifteen feet from the nearest rail when you see flashing red lights, a lowered barricade, ringing bells or a flagger warning of a train or other on-track equipment.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: Do gates have to come down before you stop fifteen feet from a railroad track, or does any single warning count?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: At a railroad crossing, any one of flashing red lights, a lowered barricade, ringing bells or a flagger is enough to require stopping at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: Which two Arizona rules both use the number fifteen while measuring speed versus distance?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: The school crossing speed and the railroad stopping distance share the number fifteen but measure different things, miles per hour versus feet.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: After a train passes, what must happen with crossing signals and gates before you drive onto the tracks?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.memory_hook: Every signal off, gate fully up
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: Do not cross the tracks until every signal has stopped and the barricade has risen all the way.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: Is weaving around or ducking beneath a lowered railroad gate ever legal?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: Never drive around or under a lowered crossing barricade.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: What should you always assume whenever you approach any railroad track at any time?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: Assume that a train or other rail equipment could be coming on any track, at any hour.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: Why must you check traffic space on the far side before rolling onto a railroad crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: Never let yourself get trapped on a railroad crossing.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.front: What immediate action does the Arizona manual instruct if your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.expected_back: If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, get out of it.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: Above everything else, what simple rule does Arizona's manual stress when a car dies on railroad tracks?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: If a vehicle stalls on the tracks, the rule the manual gives is simply to get out of it.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: Why must you never try to beat an approaching train or rail vehicle across a grade crossing?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Never try to race a train or any other on-track equipment to a crossing.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Which two types of large vehicles should you expect to stop at railroad tracks even without flashing lights?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Expect buses and gasoline tankers to stop at railroad crossings, because those vehicles are required to stop there.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: Why should you stay ready to brake behind the vehicle ahead whenever approaching railroad tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Buses and gasoline tankers must stop at railroad crossings, so be ready for the vehicle ahead of you to stop there.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: What extra railroad hazard must you scan for when driving at night?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: When driving at night, watch for railroad crossing warning signs that may not be lit.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: Which three highway networks have route markers included among highway guide signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Highway guide signs include route markers for interstate routes, national routes and state routes.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: What distinguishes Arizona's highway mileage-marker coverage compared with most other states?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.memory_hook: Mile markers on every state highway
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: Arizona is one of only a few states that has mileage markers on every state highway.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: How far off the right highway shoulder are Arizona mile posts positioned?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Arizona mile posts stand two feet off the right shoulder of the highway.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Roughly how far apart are Arizona highway mile posts set along a route?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Arizona mile posts are placed about one mile apart.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: For Arizona highway mile posts, what do two feet and one mile each measure?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: A mile post sits two feet off the right shoulder, and the posts are spaced about one mile apart, so one number is an offset and the other is a spacing.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: In which three roadside emergencies does reading a nearby mile post help rescuers find you?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: A nearby mile post lets you tell others where you are after a crash, a mechanical problem or running out of gas.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: Whenever you are forced to pull over along a highway, which two location facts should you note?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: If you have to stop on a highway, note which route you are on and roughly how far you are from a mile post.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: What two durations and sign setups can highway work zones take?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: A work zone can be a long-term project with permanent signs or a temporary site with portable signs that stays up for only a few hours.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: How does signage differ between a long-term highway project and a short few-hour maintenance zone?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: A long-term work zone uses permanent signs, while a temporary work area uses portable signs that may stay up for only a few hours.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: What three crash types happen most frequently inside highway work zones?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Typical work-zone crashes are rear-end collisions from drivers going too fast, collisions with fixed objects, and vehicles striking the people working there.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: What mindset and braking readiness do changing work-zone conditions and milled surfaces demand?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: In a work zone, stay on high alert and be ready to slow or stop suddenly for changing conditions, including a change in the road surface.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: Where might construction crews and heavy equipment operate or pull out inside a work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Workers and construction vehicles may be right beside the travel lanes or may enter them at any point in the work zone.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: Which three groups are protected or guided by construction warning and channelizing devices?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: The alerting and controlling devices used in construction and maintenance areas protect highway workers as well as guiding drivers and pedestrians.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: Which standard background color identifies road construction and maintenance warning devices?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: Orange is the basic color of the warning devices used in road construction and maintenance areas.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: What three rules apply every time you pass through a construction site?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: At every construction site you must drive slowly, stay especially alert and obey the posted speed limit.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: Whose lives are protected by reduced work-zone speed limits?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: A work-zone speed limit protects the workers doing the job as well as the drivers passing through.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: How does Arizona penalize speeding inside a work zone when work-zone signs are posted?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: When work-zone signs are posted, the fine for a speeding violation there is doubled.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: What exact condition triggers Arizona's doubled speeding fine in a work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: The doubled fine described for work zones applies to a speed violation when the work-zone signs are posted.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: What three traffic-control actions do human flaggers perform in road work zones?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Flaggers are used in road work zones to stop traffic, slow it down or guide it safely through.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: What high-visibility gear do flaggers wear, and what handheld tools do they use to direct you?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.memory_hook: Orange gear; red flags or paddles
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: Flaggers wear orange vests or jackets and direct traffic with red flags or stop and slow panels.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: What general purpose do construction and maintenance signs serve?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Construction and maintenance signs warn drivers of possible danger in or near a work area.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: Which geometric shape is used for most warning signs inside street and highway work zones?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Most of the signs used in highway and street work areas are diamond-shaped.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: Why do crews deploy large flashing arrow panels day and night ahead of work zones?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: Flashing arrow panels are used both day and night to warn you early that you must move left or right into another lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: What two steps should you take as soon as you spot a flashing work-zone arrow panel ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: When you see a flashing arrow panel, slow down and get ready to merge in the direction the arrow points.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: What four kinds of advance alerts appear on changeable electronic highway message signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Electronic message signs on some roads give advance warning of construction zones, special traffic directions, road closures or weather conditions.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: How do cones, drums, and barricades help drivers through a work zone—including after dark?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: Cones, drums and barricades alert you and guide you safely through a work area, and at night they may carry warning lights.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: How does a human flagger's role differ from a lighted flashing arrow panel?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: A flagger is a person in orange who stops, slows or guides traffic, while a flashing arrow panel is a lighted board that tells you to merge.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: How does a flashing arrow panel differ from an electronic text message sign?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: A flashing arrow panel asks you to change lanes in the arrow's direction, while an electronic message sign gives advance information such as closures, special directions or weather.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: How do advance construction signs and channelizing cones, drums, or barricades divide the job?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: Construction and maintenance signs warn of danger near the work area, while cones, drums and barricades guide you through the work area itself.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: What three functions do painted pavement markings perform for traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: Pavement markings guide and warn drivers and also regulate traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: Which two colors make up standard lane markings, and what happens when solid and broken lines combine?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: Pavement markings are either yellow or white, they can be combined, and each combination carries its own meaning.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: What traffic pattern do yellow centerlines indicate?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Yellow center lines tell you that traffic on the road flows in both directions.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: Besides dividing same-direction lanes, what three roadway features do white lines mark?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and also mark the road edge, stop lines and pedestrian crosswalks.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: What core directional split separates yellow lane stripes from white lane stripes?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, while white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: Why does passing across a single broken yellow line demand extreme caution even when legal?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: A broken yellow line lets you pass on the left when the road is clear, but because you face oncoming traffic you must pass with extreme caution.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: How many traffic directions are allowed to pass where a broken yellow line parallels a solid yellow line?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: Where a broken yellow line runs beside a solid yellow line, passing is allowed in only one direction.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: When the broken yellow stripe of a combo centerline sits on your side, when may you pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: If the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass once the road ahead is clear.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: May you cross to pass when the solid yellow stripe sits closest to your travel lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: Passing is not allowed when the solid yellow line is the one nearest your lane.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: Along a combination yellow centerline, how does the stripe touching your lane govern passing?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: With a broken yellow line on your side you may pass when the road is clear, but with a solid yellow line on your side you may not pass.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: While double solid yellow lines ban passing both ways, what single maneuver lets you cross them?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines ban passing in both directions, and you may cross them only to make a left turn.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: How does crossing double solid yellow lines contrast with crossing broken white lines?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines may be crossed only to turn left, while broken white lines may be crossed with caution to change lanes after signaling.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.front: What step must come before crossing a broken white line into a neighboring same-way lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.expected_back: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same way and may be crossed with caution after you signal your lane change.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.front: Why are solid white lane lines painted along turn bays and intersection approaches?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.expected_back: Solid white lines mark turn lanes and keep drivers from changing lanes near intersections.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: How do broken white lines and solid white lines differ as you approach an intersection?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: Broken white lines may be crossed with caution, while solid white lines mark turn lanes and keep drivers from changing lanes near intersections.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.front: What must you do if your lane is painted with a curved arrow and the word ONLY?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.expected_back: If your lane shows a curved arrow with the word ONLY, you must turn the way the arrow points.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.front: What choices do you have in a lane marked with a combined straight-and-curved pavement arrow?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.expected_back: If your lane shows both a curved arrow and a straight arrow, you may either turn that way or go straight.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: How does a curved arrow paired with ONLY differ from a combined curved-and-straight arrow?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: A curved arrow with the word ONLY requires the turn, while a lane with a curved arrow and a straight arrow lets you turn or continue straight.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.front: What does a bicycle symbol painted on the roadway alert drivers to expect?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.expected_back: A bicycle painted on the road warns that bicyclists may be present, so drive with caution.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.front: What does any painted color along a street curb tell a driver looking to park?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.expected_back: A painted curb means special rules apply if you want to park there, and each curb color has its own meaning.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: What is the sole reason and allowed duration for stopping alongside a white painted curb?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: At a white painted curb you may stop only for as long as it takes to pick up or drop off passengers.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: What activity is allowed at a yellow painted curb, and what must the driver do while stopped there?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: At a yellow painted curb you may stop only long enough to load or unload, and you must stay with your car.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: Which three actions are completely forbidden along a red painted curb?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: A red painted curb means you may not stop, stand or park there at all.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: How do Arizona's rules step across white, yellow, and red painted curbs?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.memory_hook: White riders, yellow loading, red nothing
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: A white curb allows a brief stop for passengers, a yellow curb allows a brief stop for loading while you stay with the car, and a red curb allows no stop at all.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: Which lane is typically best when driving several blocks straight down a multi-lane one-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: When you will stay on a one-way street for several blocks, the center lane is usually the best lane to use.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: On a multi-lane one-way street, what traffic uses the far-left and far-right lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: On a one-way street, the left and right lanes are used by vehicles that are turning.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: Why does the center lane flow smoother than outer lanes along a multi-block one-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: On a long one-way street the center lane is preferred because the outer lanes serve turning vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: What traffic flow direction is divided by white lane stripes?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: White lane lines divide lanes of traffic heading the same way.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: Besides separating same-way lanes, what boundary on the right side of the road can a single white line mark?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: A single white line may also mark the right edge of the pavement.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: What two requirements apply before crossing a broken white line into another lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: After you signal, you may cross a broken white line to change lanes if it is safe.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: Which two places on a roadway use a single solid white line?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.memory_hook: Right road edge and same-way lanes
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: A solid white line marks the right edge of the roadway and also divides lanes of traffic heading the same way.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: Under what two circumstances may you drive across the solid white line on the right edge of the road?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: Cross the solid white edge line on the right side of the road only in an emergency or to avoid a road hazard.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: When are Arizona drivers permitted to cross a single solid white stripe bordering an HOV lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.memory_hook: Merging into or out of HOV
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Drivers may cross a solid white line while merging into or out of a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: What direction do lanes on each side of a double solid white line travel, and is crossing allowed?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: A double solid white line divides two lanes heading the same way, and crossing it is prohibited.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: How does lane-changing permission differ between a broken white line and a double solid white line?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: A broken white line may be crossed after signaling when safe, while a double solid white line may not be crossed.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: How does the rule for crossing the right-edge solid white line differ from a single solid white HOV stripe?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: The solid white right-edge line is crossed only for an emergency or a road hazard, while a solid white line beside an HOV lane may be crossed to merge in or out.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: What traffic directions are separated by yellow lane lines?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Yellow lane lines divide lanes of traffic heading in opposite directions.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: What fundamental rule separates white lane lines from yellow lane lines?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: White lane lines divide traffic going the same way, while yellow lane lines divide traffic going opposite ways.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: On divided highways and one-way streets, which pavement boundary can a single yellow line mark?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: A single yellow line may mark the left edge of the pavement on divided highways and on one-way streets.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: On a divided highway or one-way street, which edge is marked white and which edge is marked yellow?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: A single white line can mark the right pavement edge, while a single yellow line can mark the left pavement edge on divided highways and one-way streets.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: How does a reversible lane operate across the day?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: A reversible lane switches its direction of travel depending on the time of day.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: What pavement striping typically borders a reversible lane in Arizona?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: Reversible lanes are usually marked with double dashed yellow lines.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: Where should you look to verify whether you may use a reversible lane right now?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: Signs beside the road or overhead may tell you which reversible lanes you are allowed to use at that time.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: What lane type do double dashed yellow lines signal, and what determines its direction?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: Double dashed yellow lines usually signal a reversible lane, whose direction depends on the time of day.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: Do Arizona turning laws apply only at street intersections, or elsewhere too?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Turning rules apply everywhere you turn, including driveways and alleys, not just at intersections.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: What three basic steps belong in every safe turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: To make any turn, signal, slow down and turn smoothly once it is safe.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: Which three smaller, harder-to-spot road users must you check for throughout every turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: While you turn, check for pedestrians, mopeds and bicycles.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: Where intersections allow turning from two or more lanes, how do you know which lanes qualify?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: Where turns may be made from more than one lane, signs and pavement markings will show you which lanes to use.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: Why must you scan regulatory signs before starting a turn at an unfamiliar corner?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: At some locations, signs prohibit turning.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: How close to the right edge should you approach a right turn, and what steering mistake must you avoid?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.memory_hook: Hug right edge; never swing wide
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: Before a right turn, keep close to the right curb or road edge and do not swing wide before or during the turn.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: Where must you come to a complete stop before making a right turn on a red light?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: To turn right at a red light, you must first come to a complete stop before the marked or unmarked crosswalk.
