sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: Which specific regulatory sign must you check for before turning right on a red signal?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.memory_hook: Scan for No Turn On Red
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Look for No Turn On Red signs before you turn right at a red light.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: Which three groups hold right-of-way over a driver turning right on red?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: When turning right on red, always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and oncoming traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: Unless signs or markings direct otherwise, which lane must you enter when finishing a right turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: Unless signs direct you otherwise, finish a right turn in the right lane of the road you enter.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: On a two-way street, which lane do you approach a left turn from, and where in the intersection does the turn start?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: For a left turn on a two-way road, approach in the lane just to the right of the center line and begin the turn just left of the center point of the intersection.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: When completing a left turn onto a two-way road, which lane should you land in and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: When a left turn on a two-way road is complete, you should be in the lane just to the right of the center line, which avoids conflict with other turning traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: Where a signed or painted left-turn lane is provided, may you turn left from an adjacent through lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: When a left-turn lane has been signed or marked, turn left only from that lane and never from any other lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: How does a single marked left-turn bay compare with turning from multiple lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: A marked left-turn lane must be used for a left turn, while turns from more than one lane are allowed only where signs and markings show it.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: Which start and finish lanes do you use when turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: For a left turn from a one-way road onto another one-way road, approach in the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the far left lane without swinging wide.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: Under what exact road combination—after stopping and yielding—is a left turn on red legal in Arizona?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: Turning left from a one-way road onto another one-way road is the only left turn you may make against a red light, after stopping and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless signs prohibit it.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: How do legal road setups for turning right on red compare with turning left on red?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: Turning right on red needs a full stop before the crosswalk, while turning left on red is allowed only from a one-way road onto another one-way road.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: Turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street requires which starting and ending lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: For a left turn from a two-way road onto a one-way road, approach in the lane just to the right of the center line and turn into the far left lane of the road you enter.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.front: Which lane do you approach in when turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.expected_back: For a left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road, approach the intersection in the lane closest to the left curb.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: How does your starting lane for a left turn differ when leaving a two-way street versus a one-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: A left turn from a two-way road starts in the lane just right of the center line, while a left turn from a one-way road starts in the lane nearest the left curb.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: How do the target finish lanes compare between a normal right turn and a left turn onto a one-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: A right turn normally ends in the right lane of the new road, while a left turn onto a one-way road ends in its far left lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: Into which exact lane must you turn when making a left from a one-way street onto a two-way street?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: When you turn left from a one-way road onto a two-way road, turn into the lane just to the right of the center line.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: Once you finish turning left onto a two-way road, what two steps precede moving over to the right lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: After that turn, check traffic on your right and signal a lane change before you move over to the right lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: Is turning left from a one-way road onto a two-way road ever legal against a red light in Arizona?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: A left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road can never be made against a red light.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: What target-lane rule and red-light restriction govern turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: The left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road ends in the lane just right of the center line and may not be made on a red light.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: What purpose does the painted middle lane serve along many two-way Arizona streets?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: On many two-way streets, the middle lane is painted as a shared left turn lane for both directions.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: How are the inner and outer yellow lines arranged along each edge of a two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: A two-way left turn lane is edged on each side by a pair of yellow lines, with the inner line broken and the outer line solid.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: Along a shared two-way left-turn lane, which yellow stripe sits next to the center chute and which faces through traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: Along a two-way left turn lane the broken yellow line is the inner line next to the center lane, while the solid yellow line is the outer line.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: Which drivers are legally permitted to occupy a two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: A two-way left turn lane may be used only by vehicles turning left, from either direction.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: Which two left-turn maneuvers is a two-way left-turn lane designed to support?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: The two-way left turn lane gives you a safe place to slow down before turning left off the street, or to pull into when turning left out of a side street or driveway.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: After pulling left from a driveway into a two-way left-turn lane, what merge tactic is strictly prohibited?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: You may pull into the two-way left turn lane when turning left out of a driveway, but you may not use it to speed up and merge with through traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: How does Arizona law treat slowing for a left turn versus overtaking traffic inside a shared center lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Slowing in the two-way left turn lane before a left turn is allowed, while passing or driving straight through in it is not.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: What communication step is required before steering into a two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: Signal before you enter a two-way left turn lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: How much of your vehicle belongs inside the two-way left-turn lane once you enter?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: Move your vehicle completely into the two-way left turn lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: Who else requires close attention whenever you pull into a two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: Watch for other drivers who are also using the two-way left turn lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: Which three maneuvers must you never perform inside a two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Never use the two-way left turn lane to pass, to travel straight through, or to speed up so you can merge with through traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: Where in Arizona do Metro light-rail trains operate, and how close is motor vehicle traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: METRO light rail trains run on streets in the Valley in Maricopa County, and car traffic moves right alongside them.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: Which three street improvements along the Metro corridor help protect pedestrians and discourage jaywalking?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: Pedestrian safety work along the METRO line includes countdown signals, new walkways and landscaping meant to cut down on jaywalking.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: What safety upgrade was added at certain school-area crossings along the Metro light-rail route?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: Some crossings near schools received new signals as part of the METRO safety design.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: From what kind of lane is a car permitted to turn across Metro light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: A car may turn across the METRO tracks only from a designated turn lane that has its own traffic signal control.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: What physical border separates the Metro light-rail trackway from adjacent car lanes?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: METRO trains travel in their own trackway, set apart from traffic by six-inch curbs.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Where are motor vehicles allowed to cross the Metro trackway, and what activates when a train nears?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Cars may cross the METRO trackway only at controlled locations, where special signals and warning signs switch on as a train approaches.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: How do Metro's rules pair turning across the rails with crossing the trackway straight through?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: Turning across the METRO tracks is allowed only from signal-controlled turn lanes, and crossing the trackway is allowed only at controlled locations.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: How many access points does each Metro station feature, and how do riders reach them?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: Each METRO station has two access points, and both are reached by a signalized crosswalk.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: How does Metro station platform height compare with the train floor?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: METRO station platforms sit at the same height as the train floor, so riders board without a step.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: How are frontage roads beside Metro tracks controlled, and which heavy vehicles are they engineered to carry?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Frontage roads near the METRO tracks are controlled by traffic signals and built to handle large trucks and emergency vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: What safety condition must be met before a Metro light-rail train can pull away from a stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: A METRO train cannot move until its doors have closed.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: How are the couplers linking Metro rail cars treated to lower crash injuries?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: The couplers that join light rail vehicles are covered in an energy-absorbing material to reduce injuries in a crash.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: What triggers the electronic Train Approaching signs mounted at Metro intersections?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: Electronic Train Approaching signs at every METRO light rail intersection flash when a train is coming toward the intersection.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: Why are U-turns permitted at nearly every intersection along the twenty-mile Metro corridor?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: U-turns are allowed at almost every light rail intersection along the twenty-mile METRO system so that vehicles can cross the tracks.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: What regulates both left turns and U-turns at light-rail intersections?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: At light rail intersections, left turns and U-turns are controlled by traffic signals.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: How does the flashing Train Approaching sign's job differ from the combined U-turn and left-turn sign?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: A flashing Train Approaching sign warns that a train is coming, while the combined U-turn and left turn sign marks the signal-controlled turns used to cross the tracks.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: What stopping and parking rule applies to both cars and bicycles on light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: Never stop or park a car or a bike on light rail tracks.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: How must you obey a steady red signal versus a red arrow at a light-rail crossing?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: At light rail crossings, stop on a red signal, and treat a red arrow as an order not to turn.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: At a light-rail junction, what distinguishes a red signal from a red arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: A red signal at a light rail crossing means stop, and a red arrow means do not turn.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: What visual check should every driver and cyclist make before crossing light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: Look both ways before you cross the light rail tracks, whether you are driving or biking.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: May motorists or bicyclists travel along the lane where light-rail trains run?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: Never drive a car or ride a bike in the lane where the train operates.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: Because light-rail trains run quietly, which visual and audio cues must you watch and listen for?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: Light rail trains make little noise, so near the tracks watch for their flashing headlights and listen for their bells and horns.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: Why is relying on engine noise dangerous near light rail, and what replaces it?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: A quiet train means you cannot rely on hearing it, so you look for flashing headlights and also listen for its bells and horns.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: Since both ends of a light-rail train look the same, how do its lights show whether it approaches or departs?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: Both ends of a light rail train look alike, so white headlights mean it is coming toward you and red taillights mean it is moving away.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: What do white headlights versus red taillights tell you on a double-ended light-rail car?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: White headlights mean a light rail train is approaching, while red taillights mean it is moving away from you.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: Where must pedestrians avoid walking or standing around light-rail corridors?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: Pedestrians should not walk on the light rail tracks or stand close to them.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: Where and how should pedestrians cross streets carrying light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: Pedestrians near light rail should cross only at crosswalks and follow the crosswalk signals.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: What shared rule keeps both drivers and pedestrians clear of live light-rail steel?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: Drivers must never stop or park on the tracks, and pedestrians must never walk on them or stand close to them.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: What precaution should adults take with young children near tracks and on Metro platforms?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: Adults should hold small children by the hand near the tracks and on station platforms.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.front: Which three safety steps should children practice anytime they are near light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.expected_back: Children should stop, look and listen whenever they are around light rail tracks.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.front: How should children handle bicycles and skateboards when using a crosswalk near light rail?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.expected_back: At crosswalks near light rail, children should get off their bikes and skateboards and walk them across.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: Instead of riding across a light-rail crosswalk, what should kids do with bikes or skateboards?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: At a light rail crosswalk, children walk their bikes and skateboards across instead of riding them.

sec14-card-sec14-F37.front: What rule applies to children playing around light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F37.expected_back: Children should never play near the light rail tracks.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.front: What basic distance reality governs bringing any moving vehicle to a safe, complete stop?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.expected_back: Bringing a vehicle to a safe, complete stop takes a long distance.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.front: Which six human, roadway, and vehicle factors shape your total stopping and braking distance?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.memory_hook: Speed, reaction, road, tires, weight, brakes
sec16-card-sec16-F02.expected_back: Braking distance depends on your speed, your perception and reaction times, the pavement, your tires, your vehicle's weight including any load or trailer, and the type and condition of your brakes.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.front: How does Arizona define perception time, and how many seconds does an average driver take?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.expected_back: Perception time, the time it takes a driver to see and recognize a dangerous situation, averages zero point seven five seconds.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.front: What does reaction time measure, and what is the average driver's figure?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.expected_back: Reaction time, the gap between perceiving danger and starting to brake, averages zero point seven five seconds.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.front: How many seconds on average pass from a roadway threat appearing until braking begins?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.expected_back: On average a person needs one point five seconds to perceive a threat in the roadway and react to it.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.front: How do average perception time and average reaction time combine before your brakes engage?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.expected_back: Perception time and reaction time each average zero point seven five seconds, and together they make the one point five seconds an average driver needs before braking begins.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.front: What practical everyday decision does understanding your vehicle's stopping distance support?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.expected_back: Knowing how far your vehicle needs to stop helps you pick a safe driving speed.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.front: Why shouldn't you treat the manual's stopping-distance chart as an exact guarantee for your car?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.expected_back: The manual's stopping-distance chart is only a guide, because your real stopping distance depends on factors such as your tires, brakes and the road.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.front: What minimum time cushion should you keep behind the vehicle ahead during normal driving?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.expected_back: Keep a following distance of at least three seconds in most driving situations, so you can avoid a crash if traffic ahead stops suddenly.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.front: To what range should your following gap expand when traffic or visibility grows trickier?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.expected_back: Some situations call for a longer following distance of three to six seconds.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.front: How far should you expand your following gap when pavement turns wet, icy, or slick?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.expected_back: On slippery roads, double your following distance to six seconds or more so you have room to adjust your speed or stop.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.front: How does Arizona's standard following-distance floor step up once roads turn slippery?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.expected_back: The everyday minimum is a three-second following distance, while slippery roads call for doubling it to six seconds or more.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.front: How does easing your speed help when a trailing driver pulls out to pass you?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.expected_back: If the driver behind you wants to pass, slowing down lets that driver get by sooner and gives more room to pull back into the lane.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.front: Between slowing down and speeding up, which response is right when a vehicle behind moves to overtake?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.expected_back: When someone behind you wants to pass, the right move is to slow down, not to speed up.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.front: How should you adjust your position when a tall semi-trailer ahead blocks your view of the road?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.expected_back: When a large vehicle such as a tractor-trailer blocks your view ahead, drop back farther so you can see around it.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.front: How does the crash risk on a quiet, open rural highway compare with busy city streets?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.expected_back: A quiet, empty rural highway can carry as much danger as busy city traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.front: Which three hazards commonly ambush drivers along Arizona's rural highways?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.expected_back: Common rural hazards include animals on the road, slow farm equipment just past the top of a hill, and low spots covered with water.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.front: What three habits keep you safe approaching blind curves and hill crests on open country roads?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.expected_back: On open rural roads, stay alert, watch for warning signs and slow down as you near curves or hills that hide the road ahead.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.front: Which two driving handicaps almost always strike simultaneously during bad weather?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.expected_back: In bad weather, poor visibility and poor traction often happen at the same time.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.front: How do shifting weather and surface conditions alter your reaction window and vehicle control?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.expected_back: Changing road and weather conditions shorten the time you have to react and affect how your car handles.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.front: What is the number-one rule whenever weather or road conditions deteriorate, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.expected_back: In bad conditions the first rule is to reduce speed, which offsets the visibility and reaction time you have lost.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.front: During which two daily windows does driving toward the sun create harsh windshield glare?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.expected_back: Driving toward the sun in the early morning or late afternoon creates glare.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.front: Which three simple tools or upkeep habits cut down blinding sun glare?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.expected_back: Sunglasses, clean windows and sun visors all help cut down sun glare.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.front: What hidden danger exists even when the low sun sits comfortably behind your back?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.expected_back: When the sun is behind you, oncoming drivers may be facing the glare and may not see your car or your signals.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.front: How does the victim of sun glare flip depending on whether the sun sits ahead or behind you?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.expected_back: With the sun ahead of you, you face the glare, but with the sun behind you, oncoming drivers face it and may not see you.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.front: Which wind direction creates the sharpest steering challenge for drivers?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.expected_back: Strong winds, and crosswinds in particular, make a vehicle harder to control.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.front: Which four vehicle or towing categories suffer the worst instability in strong winds?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.expected_back: Wind is very dangerous for campers, large recreational vehicles and anyone towing a trailer, and it also makes lightweight vehicles harder to control.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.front: What immediate speed adjustment gives you firmer control in strong wind?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.expected_back: To gain more control in a strong wind, slow down.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.front: What happens as your vehicle exits a canyon, bridge cut, or tree line into open terrain?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.expected_back: When you leave a sheltered stretch for open space, expect crosswinds that may push you toward the side or the middle of the road.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.front: Where do sudden crosswinds hit hardest, and which two directions can they push your car?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.expected_back: Crosswinds are most likely when you come out of a sheltered stretch into open space, and they can push you toward the edge or the middle of the road.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.front: What dangerous motion can wind trigger behind a vehicle towing a trailer?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.expected_back: Wind may make a vehicle that is pulling a trailer sway.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.front: What effect can air turbulence from passing semi-trucks or buses have on your car?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.expected_back: Gusts created by large trucks or buses you meet may force you to make steering corrections.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.front: What severe folding crash can strong wind currents trigger when pulling a trailer?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.expected_back: Wind currents can cause a vehicle pulling a trailer to jackknife.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.front: When towing a trailer and a truck or bus overtakes on your left, what three-part sequence keeps the trailer straight?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.expected_back: If you are towing a trailer and a truck or bus passes on your left, move as far right in your lane as you can and slow down, then speed up gently as it goes by so the trailer tracks straight.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.front: In what exact order do slowing down and gently speeding up occur when a semi passes your trailer?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.expected_back: When towing a trailer as a truck or bus passes on the left, you first move right and slow down, and then speed up only gently as it passes.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.front: Which two effects will you feel when driving straight into a strong headwind?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.expected_back: Driving into a strong headwind may take more acceleration and makes steering harder.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.front: How does a strong tailwind change your speed and your braking timing?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.expected_back: A tailwind pushes your speed up, so you must slow down and start braking earlier to stop.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.front: How do your gas and brake adjustments flip between a strong headwind and a strong tailwind?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.expected_back: A headwind calls for more acceleration and firmer steering, while a tailwind calls for slowing and braking earlier.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.front: How severely can an Arizona dust storm cut forward visibility?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.expected_back: Dust storms are common in Arizona and can sometimes cut a driver's visibility to zero.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.front: What are your very first two moves the moment you encounter a dust storm?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.expected_back: If you run into a dust storm, check the traffic around you at once and begin slowing down.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.front: Why should you leave the roadway right away rather than pressing deeper into a dust storm?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.expected_back: Pull off the road as soon as you can in a dust storm, rather than waiting until poor visibility makes it hard to do safely.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.front: Should you keep driving through thickening dust until you cannot see, or exit the road early?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.expected_back: Pull off early in a dust storm, before visibility drops, rather than waiting until you can no longer see to leave the road safely.

sec16-card-sec16-F35.front: Where exactly must you position and stop your vehicle during a severe dust storm?
sec16-card-sec16-F35.expected_back: In a severe dust storm, slow down immediately, drive all the way off the highway and stop as far to the right as you can.

sec16-card-sec16-F36.front: Which two parts of a highway must you never stop inside during a dust storm?
sec16-card-sec16-F36.expected_back: During a dust storm, never stop in a travel lane or in the emergency lane.

sec16-card-sec16-F37.front: Once parked completely off the highway in a dust storm, what must you do with your lights and brake pedal?
sec16-card-sec16-F37.expected_back: After pulling off in a severe dust storm, turn your lights off and take your foot off the brake.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.front: Combine Arizona's severe dust-storm parking spot with the exact lighting and pedal rule?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.expected_back: In a severe dust storm you leave the highway completely, avoiding both the travel lane and the emergency lane, and then switch off your lights and release the brake.

sec16-card-sec16-F38.front: Where should everyone remain while waiting for a dust storm to clear, and how?
sec16-card-sec16-F38.expected_back: Stay inside the vehicle with seat belts buckled until the dust storm has passed.

sec16-card-sec16-F39.front: What weather pairing makes heavy rain extra treacherous during thunderstorms?
sec16-card-sec16-F39.expected_back: Heavy rain is especially hazardous when it comes with gusty winds, as in a thunderstorm.

sec16-card-sec16-F40.front: Which nearby vehicles become toughest to spot during a heavy downpour?
sec16-card-sec16-F40.expected_back: In heavy rain, vehicles behind you and in your blind spots are especially hard to see.

sec16-card-sec16-F41.front: Why does Arizona suggest waiting briefly after light rain starts before flicking on windshield wipers?
sec16-card-sec16-F41.expected_back: Wait a short time after rain begins before switching on your wipers, because blades on a dirty windshield can smear it.

sec16-card-sec16-F42.front: To what minimum time gap should you drop back when driving in rain?
sec16-card-sec16-F42.expected_back: In rain, slow down so the gap to the vehicle ahead grows to at least six seconds.

sec16-card-sec16-F43.front: Why are the opening thirty minutes of a rainstorm the slickest on Arizona roads?
sec16-card-sec16-F43.expected_back: Take extra care in the first thirty minutes of rain, when road grime and oil mix with water and make the surface slippery.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.front: What do six seconds and thirty minutes each represent in Arizona rain-driving rules?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.expected_back: Rain calls for a gap of at least six seconds, while the thirty minutes figure marks the especially slippery period after rain starts.

sec16-card-sec16-F44.front: At what highway speed can good tires lose all pavement contact on a heavy film of water?
sec16-card-sec16-F44.expected_back: In heavy rain, tires can ride up on a film of water, and at fifty miles per hour they can lose all contact with the road.

sec16-card-sec16-F45.front: Which three tire conditions trigger hydroplaning well below fifty miles per hour?
sec16-card-sec16-F45.expected_back: Tires that are under-inflated, worn or bald lose contact with a wet road at much lower speeds.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.front: Compare the hydroplaning threshold of healthy tires against worn, bald, or soft tires?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.expected_back: In heavy rain, tires can lose all road contact at fifty miles per hour, while worn, bald or under-inflated tires can lose it at much lower speeds.

sec16-card-sec16-F46.front: What single driver action is the best defense against hydroplaning?
sec16-card-sec16-F46.expected_back: Slowing down is the best way to prevent hydroplaning.

sec18-card-sec18-F01.front: Why should you rehearse an action plan in advance for encountering a wrong-way vehicle?
sec18-card-sec18-F01.expected_back: Keep a plan in mind for meeting a wrong-way driver, so you do not lose a moment taking evasive action that could save your life.

sec18-card-sec18-F02.front: Which four substance categories never mix with driving because they cause crashes, injuries, and death?
sec18-card-sec18-F02.expected_back: Alcohol, marijuana, medications and illegal drugs do not mix with driving, and a driver who uses them can cause crashes, injuries and death.

sec18-card-sec18-F03.front: Which two peak human abilities does safe driving demand—and every impairing substance erode?
sec18-card-sec18-F03.expected_back: Driving demands the highest level of skill and judgment, and alcohol, marijuana, medications and illegal drugs all weaken both.

sec18-card-sec18-F04.front: Beyond illegal substances, which legal doctor-ordered and drugstore remedies can impair your driving?
sec18-card-sec18-F04.expected_back: Prescription drugs and over-the-counter allergy and cold medicines can impair your driving skills.

sec18-card-sec18-F05.front: What check must you perform on any medication container before getting behind the wheel?
sec18-card-sec18-F05.expected_back: Before you drive, always read medication labels for warnings about how the medicine may affect you.

sec18-card-sec18-R04.front: Why must you read warning labels on non-prescription cold or allergy pills just like prescriptions?
sec18-card-sec18-R04.expected_back: Over-the-counter allergy and cold medicines can impair driving just as prescription drugs can, so the label check applies to both.

sec18-card-sec18-F06.front: Which three critical driving defenses do alcohol and drugs severely cut down?
sec18-card-sec18-F06.expected_back: Alcohol or drugs seriously reduce your reflexes, your physical control of the vehicle and your ability to recognize danger.

sec18-card-sec18-F07.front: What dangerous mental illusion do alcohol or drugs create even when you feel sober?
sec18-card-sec18-F07.expected_back: Even when you do not look or feel impaired, alcohol or drugs give you a false sense of confidence in your driving.

sec18-card-sec18-F08.front: Who inside a passenger compartment may drink from or hold an open liquor container on public roads?
sec18-card-sec18-F08.expected_back: On any public roadway, neither a driver nor a passenger may drink from or possess an open container of spirituous liquor in the passenger compartment.

sec18-card-sec18-F09.front: Riding in which four commercial or living-space vehicles exempts passengers from the open-container ban?
sec18-card-sec18-F09.expected_back: The open container rule does not apply to passengers in a bus, a limousine, a taxi or a motor home's living area.

sec18-card-sec18-F10.front: Which storage spots and coolers count legally as part of the passenger compartment?
sec18-card-sec18-F10.expected_back: For the open container rule, the passenger compartment includes any unlocked compartment or portable device within reach of the driver or a passenger.

sec18-card-sec18-F11.front: Which two vehicle areas sit legally outside the passenger compartment for transporting unsealed containers?
sec18-card-sec18-F11.expected_back: The trunk is outside the passenger compartment, and so is the space behind the rearmost upright seat when a vehicle has no trunk.

sec18-card-sec18-R02.front: Contrast an unlocked reachable console with a trunk or cargo bay under Arizona's open-container law?
sec18-card-sec18-R02.expected_back: An unlocked compartment within reach counts as part of the passenger compartment, while the trunk, or the space behind the last upright seat when there is no trunk, does not.

sec18-card-sec18-R03.front: Does the bus, taxi, limo, or motorhome open-container exception ever extend to the person driving?
sec18-card-sec18-R03.expected_back: The open container exemption covers only passengers in a bus, limousine, taxi or motor home living area, so it never covers the driver.

sec18-card-sec18-F12.front: What alcohol standard governs every Arizona driver under age twenty-one?
sec18-card-sec18-F12.expected_back: For drivers under twenty-one, the manual's alcohol rule is zero tolerance.

sec18-card-sec18-F13.front: Up to how long can your license be suspended on a first conviction for buying or giving liquor to a minor?
sec18-card-sec18-F13.expected_back: After a first conviction for knowingly buying liquor for or giving it to a minor, the court may have MVD suspend the person's license for no more than thirty days.

sec18-card-sec18-F14.front: What maximum license suspension applies after a second or subsequent conviction for supplying liquor to a minor?
sec18-card-sec18-F14.expected_back: After a second or later conviction for supplying liquor to a minor, the suspension may last no more than six (six) months.

sec18-card-sec18-R01.front: Compare the license suspension ceilings for a first versus a repeat conviction of giving liquor to a minor?
sec18-card-sec18-R01.expected_back: Supplying liquor to a minor can cost up to thirty days of license suspension on a first conviction and up to six months on a second or later one.

sec18-card-sec18-F15.front: Which age category of drivers is involved in collisions far more frequently than any other?
sec18-card-sec18-F15.expected_back: Young drivers are involved in crashes far more often than drivers in any other age group.

sec18-card-sec18-F16.front: Which age bracket accounts for the highest rate of alcohol involvement in vehicle crashes?
sec18-card-sec18-F16.expected_back: Alcohol involvement in vehicle crashes is highest for people between the ages of twenty-one and thirty-four.

sec18-card-sec18-F17.front: According to survey data, which adult age range is most likely to drive after drinking?
sec18-card-sec18-F17.expected_back: Survey data shows that adults aged twenty-one to twenty-nine are the most likely to drive after drinking.

sec18-card-sec18-R08.front: What exact nine-year adult span tops surveys for driving after drinking?
sec18-card-sec18-R08.expected_back: Survey data puts the ages most likely to drive after drinking at twenty-one to twenty-nine.

sec18-card-sec18-F18.front: How does Arizona classify impaired driving, and in which direction are penalties moving?
sec18-card-sec18-F18.expected_back: Driving while impaired is a crime, and the consequences of driving under the influence are getting tougher.

sec18-card-sec18-F19.front: What personal rule is the only guaranteed way to avoid alcohol crashes, injuries, fines, and jail?
sec18-card-sec18-F19.expected_back: The surest way to avoid death, injury, penalties and jail is zero tolerance, which means no alcohol at all before driving.

sec18-card-sec18-F20.front: What license suspension hits a driver under twenty-one caught with even a trace of an impairing substance?
sec18-card-sec18-F20.expected_back: A driver under twenty-one with even a trace of an impairing substance, whether alcohol, marijuana, medication or an illegal drug, faces stiff penalties and a two-year license suspension.

sec18-card-sec18-F21.front: Does testing below zero point zero eight BAC shield an Arizona driver from a DUI arrest?
sec18-card-sec18-F21.expected_back: Being below the zero point zero eight blood alcohol concentration (BAC) legal limit does not make it legal or safe to drive, and a DUI arrest is still possible.

sec18-card-sec18-F22.front: What do driving studies show about impairment below zero point zero eight BAC?
sec18-card-sec18-F22.expected_back: Studies show that alcohol impairs driving at levels well below zero point zero eight BAC.

sec18-card-sec18-R07.front: Pair Arizona's under-twenty-one trace penalty with its adult rule below zero point zero eight BAC?
sec18-card-sec18-R07.expected_back: Under twenty-one, any impairing trace of alcohol or drugs brings a two-year suspension, while for any driver staying below zero point zero eight BAC still allows a DUI arrest.

sec18-card-sec18-F23.front: What combination of speeding, extra violations, and danger defines an aggressive driving citation?
sec18-card-sec18-F23.expected_back: You may be cited for aggressive driving if, during one continuous stretch of driving, you exceed the posted speed limit and commit two listed violations in a series of acts that is an immediate hazard to another person or vehicle.

sec18-card-sec18-F24.front: Which five specific traffic violations count toward Arizona's aggressive driving offense?
sec18-card-sec18-F24.expected_back: The violations that count toward aggressive driving are ignoring traffic control signs or signals, passing on the right, an unsafe lane change, following too closely and failing to yield to emergency vehicles.

sec18-card-sec18-R06.front: Can speeding by itself or speeding plus one violation qualify as aggressive driving?
sec18-card-sec18-R06.expected_back: Aggressive driving needs speeding plus two of the listed violations, not speeding alone or a single violation.

sec18-card-sec18-F25.front: What mandatory course and potential suspension follow a first aggressive driving conviction?
sec18-card-sec18-F25.expected_back: After a first aggressive driving offense you must complete Traffic Survival School, and a thirty-day license suspension is possible.

sec18-card-sec18-F26.front: What criminal charge and mandatory suspension hit a second aggressive driving offense within twenty-four months?
sec18-card-sec18-F26.expected_back: A second aggressive driving offense within twenty-four months is a Class one misdemeanor and brings a twelve-month license suspension.

sec18-card-sec18-R05.front: Compare the consequences of a first aggressive driving offense with a second inside twenty-four months?
sec18-card-sec18-R05.expected_back: A first aggressive driving offense means Traffic Survival School and a possible thirty-day suspension, while a second within twenty-four months is a Class one misdemeanor with a twelve-month suspension.

sec18-card-sec18-F27.front: Which four strong emotional states keep a person from driving well?
sec18-card-sec18-F27.expected_back: You cannot drive well when you are angry, excited, worried or depressed.

sec18-card-sec18-F28.front: Which single emotion hits motorists most frequently, particularly in congested traffic?
sec18-card-sec18-F28.expected_back: Anger is probably the emotion drivers feel most often, especially in heavy traffic.

sec18-card-sec18-F29.front: How should you handle driving decisions when strong emotions are running high?
sec18-card-sec18-F29.expected_back: Do not let your emotions shape your driving decisions, and wait until you are calm before you drive.

sec18-card-sec18-F30.front: What severe real-world outcomes can distracted driving cause?
sec18-card-sec18-F30.expected_back: Distracted driving may lead to crashes, injury or death.

sec18-card-sec18-F31.front: What personal factor outweighs every external road or weather hazard you could meet?
sec18-card-sec18-F31.expected_back: Your physical, mental and emotional condition matters more than any other problem you may meet on the road.

sec18-card-sec18-F32.front: Can routine ailments like a simple headache or common cold hurt your safe driving?
sec18-card-sec18-F32.expected_back: Even a simple headache or a cold can affect your ability to drive safely.

sec18-card-sec18-F33.front: What two choices should you make if honest self-check shows illness is hurting your fitness to drive?
sec18-card-sec18-F33.expected_back: If you are ill, judge your fitness honestly and postpone the trip or let someone else drive.

sec18-card-sec18-F34.front: Which health conditions must be reported to Arizona's Motor Vehicle Division?
sec18-card-sec18-F34.expected_back: Any condition that could affect your ability to drive safely must be reported to MVD.

sec18-card-sec18-F35.front: Within what pre-application timeframe must a license applicant report having had a seizure?
sec18-card-sec18-F35.expected_back: An applicant who had a seizure in the ninety days before applying for a license must report it to MVD.

sec18-card-sec18-F36.front: Which three steps apply if an already licensed driver experiences a seizure or impairing medical episode?
sec18-card-sec18-F36.expected_back: A licensed driver who has a seizure or another medical condition must stop driving, notify MVD and get a medical exam, and the physician sends the results to MVD.

sec18-card-sec18-R09.front: Contrast the seizure rule for new license applicants with the rule for drivers who already hold a license?
sec18-card-sec18-R09.expected_back: A seizure within ninety days before applying must be reported, while an already licensed driver who has a seizure must stop driving, notify MVD and get a medical exam.

sec18-card-sec18-F37.front: What does noticing yourself starting to feel sleepy behind the wheel tell you?
sec18-card-sec18-F37.expected_back: If you start feeling sleepy while driving, it is already past time to get off the road.

sec18-card-sec18-F38.front: How does fatigue impair your brain and behind-the-wheel responses?
sec18-card-sec18-F38.expected_back: Fatigue dulls the mind and weakens your ability to act quickly and correctly.

sec18-card-sec18-F39.front: Which five groups carry elevated crash risk from drowsy driving?
sec18-card-sec18-F39.expected_back: Five groups are known to be at higher crash risk from sleepiness: shift workers, business travelers, commercial drivers, people with sleep disorders and young people.

sec18-card-sec18-F40.front: How does drowsy driving compare with drunk driving in danger and detectability?
sec18-card-sec18-F40.expected_back: Drowsy driving is as serious and dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol, but it is harder to detect.

sec18-card-sec18-F41.front: What is the single safe cure for driver fatigue?
sec18-card-sec18-F41.expected_back: Rest is the only safe remedy for driver fatigue.

sec18-card-sec18-F42.front: Which two planning habits prevent fatigue before a long road trip?
sec18-card-sec18-F42.expected_back: To avoid fatigue, rest well before a long trip and avoid driving late at night.

sec18-card-sec18-F43.front: What should you do during frequent road-trip rest stops to recharge alertness?
sec18-card-sec18-F43.expected_back: Take frequent rest stops where you get out of the vehicle, exercise, breathe deeply and move around.

sec18-card-sec18-F44.front: How do you prevent locking into a hypnotic fixed forward stare while driving?
sec18-card-sec18-F44.expected_back: Avoid a fixed forward stare by shifting your eyes often and glancing at the mirrors and gauges.

sec18-card-sec18-F45.front: Which four simple habits help keep drivers engaged between rest stops?
sec18-card-sec18-F45.expected_back: Open the windows for fresh air, sing along with the radio or chew gum, and change drivers often if you can.

sec18-card-sec18-R11.front: How do fresh air, music, gum, and stretch breaks differ from genuine rest?
sec18-card-sec18-R11.expected_back: Fresh air, music, gum and frequent stops help fight drowsiness, but rest is the only safe remedy.

sec18-card-sec18-F46.front: What two outcomes define Arizona's Driver Improvement program for irresponsible motorists?
sec18-card-sec18-F46.expected_back: Driver Improvement is the process of finding drivers who are not driving responsibly and either correcting their behavior or taking away their privilege to drive in Arizona.

sec18-card-sec18-F47.front: What is license revocation, and when does Arizona law mandate it?
sec18-card-sec18-F47.expected_back: Revocation is the removal of your driving privilege, and the law requires it after conviction for certain driving offenses.

sec18-card-sec18-F48.front: Does your right to drive return automatically the day a revocation period expires?
sec18-card-sec18-F48.expected_back: When a revocation period ends, your privilege stays revoked until an investigation confirms that every withdrawal action has ended and all statutory requirements are met.

sec18-card-sec18-F49.front: Which two fees and potential insurance filing are required to reinstate after revocation?
sec18-card-sec18-F49.expected_back: To reinstate after a revocation you pay the application fee and a twenty dollars reinstatement fee, and you may have to file a Certificate of Insurance, commonly called an SR-twenty-two.

sec18-card-sec18-F50.front: Which three exams can Arizona require you to pass again when reinstating from revocation?
sec18-card-sec18-F50.expected_back: After a revocation, MVD may require you to take a written, vision and road test.

sec18-card-sec18-R10.front: Pair the investigation rule with the exact fee structure required after a revocation period ends?
sec18-card-sec18-R10.expected_back: When a revocation period ends, the privilege stays revoked until an investigation clears it, and reinstating costs the application fee plus a twenty dollars reinstatement fee.

sec20-card-sec20-F01.front: Beyond losing your driving privilege, what two criminal penalties can underage false-ID nitrous oxide offenses carry?
sec20-card-sec20-F01.expected_back: Besides the license suspension, the nitrous oxide false-identification offense can also bring fines or a jail sentence.

sec20-card-sec20-F02.front: Where is nitrous oxide legitimately used, and what severe risks come from abusing it?
sec20-card-sec20-F02.expected_back: Nitrous oxide, commonly called laughing gas, has legitimate uses such as an anesthetic for doctors and dentists, but it can be habit-forming, and using it over a long time can lead to serious health problems or death.

sec20-card-sec20-F03.front: How long is your Arizona driving privilege suspended for a first nitrous oxide offense?
sec20-card-sec20-F03.expected_back: A first nitrous oxide offense suspends your driving privilege for six months.

sec20-card-sec20-F04.front: How long is your Arizona driving privilege suspended for a second or later nitrous oxide offense?
sec20-card-sec20-F04.expected_back: A second or later nitrous oxide offense suspends your driving privilege for twelve months.

sec20-card-sec20-R03.front: How does the suspension length jump from a first nitrous oxide offense to a repeat offense?
sec20-card-sec20-R03.expected_back: A first nitrous oxide offense means a six-month suspension, while a second or later one means twelve months.

sec20-card-sec20-F05.front: Which five invalid or fake card statuses make displaying a driver license unlawful?
sec20-card-sec20-F05.expected_back: It is unlawful to display a license you know is canceled, revoked, suspended, fictitious or altered.

sec20-card-sec20-F06.front: What mandatory and possible penalties follow altering a driver license or obtaining a false one?
sec20-card-sec20-F06.expected_back: Altering a license or obtaining a false driver license is illegal and leads to suspension, with possible fines or jail.

sec20-card-sec20-F07.front: Under the influence of alcohol, marijuana, medications, or illegal drugs, what two vehicle roles are forbidden?
sec20-card-sec20-F07.expected_back: No one under the influence of alcohol, marijuana, medications or illegal drugs may drive or be in actual physical control of any vehicle.

sec20-card-sec20-F08.front: What chemical-testing agreement do you accept automatically under Arizona's Implied Consent Law?
sec20-card-sec20-F08.expected_back: By applying for and accepting an Arizona driving privilege, you agree to be tested for alcohol and drugs if you are arrested for DUI, which is called the Implied Consent Law.

sec20-card-sec20-F09.front: Which four types of bodily samples can an officer request when DUI is suspected?
sec20-card-sec20-F09.expected_back: An officer who has reason to believe you drove under the influence will ask you to take a blood, breath, urine or other bodily substance test.

sec20-card-sec20-F10.front: At what blood-alcohol concentration do ordinary adult drivers lose their Arizona privilege on the spot?
sec20-card-sec20-F10.expected_back: If a test shows an alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight percent or more, you lose your driving privilege on the spot.

sec20-card-sec20-F11.front: At what alcohol concentration does someone driving a commercial vehicle requiring a CDL lose driving privileges on the spot?
sec20-card-sec20-F11.expected_back: For someone driving a commercial vehicle that requires a commercial driver license, the on-the-spot limit is zero point zero four.

sec20-card-sec20-F13.front: What alcohol concentration can suspend the license of a driver under twenty-one in Arizona?
sec20-card-sec20-F13.expected_back: A driver under twenty-one may have the license suspended for any alcohol concentration at all.

sec20-card-sec20-R01.front: How do Arizona's alcohol cutoffs compare across ordinary drivers, commercial-vehicle drivers, and drivers under twenty-one?
sec20-card-sec20-R01.expected_back: The on-the-spot loss of privilege starts at zero point zero eight for an ordinary driver but at zero point zero four in a commercial vehicle that needs a commercial license, and any alcohol concentration can suspend a driver under twenty-one.

sec20-card-sec20-F12.front: Can an Arizona court convict you of driving while intoxicated if your BAC measured below zero point zero eight percent?
sec20-card-sec20-F12.expected_back: You may be found guilty of driving while intoxicated even when your BAC was below zero point zero eight percent.

sec20-card-sec20-R04.front: Why isn't a BAC reading below zero point zero eight percent a legal defense to driving while intoxicated?
sec20-card-sec20-R04.expected_back: A BAC under zero point zero eight is not a defense, because a driver can still be found guilty of driving while intoxicated.

sec20-card-sec20-F14.front: What automatic suspension hits a first DUI test refusal versus a second refusal within eighty-four months?
sec20-card-sec20-F14.expected_back: Refusing or failing to complete the tests after a DUI arrest automatically costs you the privilege to drive: twelve months the first time, and twenty-four months if it is your second refusal in eighty-four months.

sec20-card-sec20-R02.front: Across an eighty-four-month window, how do first and second DUI test-refusal suspensions compare?
sec20-card-sec20-R02.expected_back: A first test refusal costs twelve months of privilege, while a second refusal within eighty-four months costs twenty-four months.

sec20-card-sec20-F15.front: Alongside criminal court sentences, what happens automatically to your license on a second or third DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F15.expected_back: For a second or third DUI offense, the driving privilege is automatically revoked in addition to any criminal penalties from the court.

sec20-card-sec20-F16.front: What is the minimum consecutive jail sentence for a first ordinary DUI in Arizona?
sec20-card-sec20-F16.expected_back: A first DUI offense brings at least ten consecutive days in jail.

sec20-card-sec20-F17.front: What minimum license suspension and minimum dollar fine apply to a first ordinary DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F17.expected_back: A first DUI offense brings a license suspension of at least ninety days and a fine of at least one thousand two hundred fifty dollars.

sec20-card-sec20-F18.front: Beyond jail, fine, and suspension, what classes, service, and optional device accompany a first ordinary DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F18.expected_back: A first DUI offense also requires alcohol screening, education, treatment or evidence-based psychotherapy and community service, and the court may order an ignition interlock on any vehicle you drive.

sec20-card-sec20-F19.front: What minimum jail time, minimum fine, and license revocation hit a second or later ordinary DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F19.expected_back: A second or later DUI offense brings at least ninety days in jail, a fine of at least three thousand dollars and a twelve-month license revocation.

sec20-card-sec20-F20.front: Besides jail, fine, and revocation, what rehabilitation, service, and device provisions apply to a repeat ordinary DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F20.expected_back: A second or later DUI offense also requires alcohol screening, education, treatment or psychotherapy and community service, and an ignition interlock may be ordered.

sec20-card-sec20-R05.front: How do minimum jail time and license loss escalate from a first ordinary DUI to a second DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-R05.expected_back: A first DUI means at least ten consecutive days in jail and a ninety-day minimum suspension, while a second DUI means at least ninety days in jail and a twelve-month revocation.

sec20-card-sec20-F21.front: At what blood-alcohol concentration does an offense cross into Arizona's Extreme DUI category?
sec20-card-sec20-F21.expected_back: Extreme DUI applies to a driver with an alcohol concentration of zero point one five or higher.

sec20-card-sec20-F22.front: What minimum consecutive jail time and minimum fine hit a first Extreme DUI at point one five?
sec20-card-sec20-F22.expected_back: A first extreme DUI brings at least thirty consecutive days in jail and a fine of at least two thousand five hundred dollars.

sec20-card-sec20-F23.front: If a first Extreme DUI reaches zero point two zero or higher, what jail floor and sentencing rule apply?
sec20-card-sec20-F23.expected_back: On a first extreme DUI with an alcohol concentration of zero point two zero or higher, jail is at least forty-five days and a suspended sentence is not available.

sec20-card-sec20-F24.front: Along with treatment and service, what vehicle device is mandatory after even a first Extreme DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F24.expected_back: A first extreme DUI also requires alcohol screening, education or treatment or psychotherapy, community service, and a Certified Ignition Interlock Device on any vehicle you drive.

sec20-card-sec20-F25.front: What minimum fine and license loss apply to a second or later Extreme DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F25.expected_back: A second or later extreme DUI brings a fine of at least three thousand two hundred fifty dollars and a twelve-month license revocation.

sec20-card-sec20-F26.front: What minimum jail term and sentencing restriction apply to a repeat Extreme DUI at zero point two zero or higher?
sec20-card-sec20-F26.expected_back: On a second or later extreme DUI at zero point two zero or higher, jail is at least one hundred eighty days with no suspended sentence.

sec20-card-sec20-F27.front: Besides jail, fine, and revocation, what four program, device, and service items accompany a repeat Extreme DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F27.expected_back: A second or later extreme DUI also requires alcohol screening, education or treatment, an ignition interlock and community service.

sec20-card-sec20-R07.front: Where does Extreme DUI start, and how does the point-two-zero sub-tier raise mandatory jail on first and repeat offenses?
sec20-card-sec20-R07.expected_back: Extreme DUI begins at zero point one five, and a higher tier at zero point two zero raises the minimum jail to forty-five days on a first offense and one hundred eighty days on a repeat, with no suspended sentence.

sec20-card-sec20-R06.front: In ascending dollar order, what are the minimum fines for first DUI, first Extreme, second DUI, and second Extreme?
sec20-card-sec20-R06.expected_back: Fines start at one thousand two hundred fifty dollars for a first DUI, two thousand five hundred dollars for a first extreme DUI, three thousand dollars for a second DUI and three thousand two hundred fifty dollars for a second extreme DUI.

sec20-card-sec20-R08.front: How does the ignition-interlock rule on an ordinary first DUI differ from a first Extreme DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-R08.expected_back: For an ordinary first DUI the court may order an ignition interlock, while for a first extreme DUI the interlock is required.

sec20-card-sec20-F28.front: Which three license, repeat-count, or passenger situations turn a DUI into Aggravated DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F28.expected_back: Aggravated DUI covers a DUI committed while your privilege is suspended or revoked, a third DUI in seven years, or a DUI with a person under fifteen in the vehicle.

sec20-card-sec20-F29.front: What DUI charge applies if someone already under a Certified Ignition Interlock order commits another DUI or Extreme DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F29.expected_back: Aggravated DUI also covers a DUI or extreme DUI by a person who is already required to use a Certified Ignition Interlock Device.

sec20-card-sec20-F30.front: What prison exposure and license revocation come with an Aggravated DUI conviction?
sec20-card-sec20-F30.expected_back: Aggravated DUI brings prison for not more than two years and a one-year license revocation, on top of any other required penalty.

sec20-card-sec20-F31.front: Alongside prison and revocation, what treatment and vehicle requirements follow Aggravated DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F31.expected_back: Aggravated DUI also requires alcohol screening, education, treatment or psychotherapy and an ignition interlock on any vehicle you drive.

sec20-card-sec20-R09.front: What felony tier and prison cap unite a third DUI within seven years and a DUI carrying a child under fifteen?
sec20-card-sec20-R09.expected_back: A third DUI within seven years and a DUI with a passenger under fifteen are both aggravated DUI, which carries prison for not more than two years.

sec20-card-sec20-F32.front: What is a Certified Ignition Interlock Device and what vehicle systems does it connect into?
sec20-card-sec20-F32.expected_back: A Certified Ignition Interlock Device is a breath alcohol tester wired into the vehicle's ignition and power system.

sec20-card-sec20-F33.front: What must you do before turning the key on an interlock-equipped car, and when does it block starting?
sec20-card-sec20-F33.expected_back: The driver must blow into the interlock before trying to start the engine, and the vehicle will not start if the alcohol level is above a set level.

sec20-card-sec20-F34.front: Does ignition-interlock testing end once the engine starts, or when else must you blow?
sec20-card-sec20-F34.expected_back: While the vehicle is running, the driver must also blow into the interlock at random intervals.

sec20-card-sec20-R10.front: At which two stages of a trip does a Certified Ignition Interlock Device require breath samples?
sec20-card-sec20-R10.expected_back: An interlock test happens before starting the engine and again at random intervals while driving.

sec20-card-sec20-F35.front: How soon into most DUI-related Class D or Class G suspensions or revocations can eligible drivers apply for a Special Ignition Interlock Restricted License?
sec20-card-sec20-F35.expected_back: For most of the listed DUI-related cases, Arizona law lets a person apply for a Special Ignition Interlock Restricted Driver License on day one of a Class D or Class G suspension or revocation.

sec20-card-sec20-F36.front: Which three ongoing rules bind someone driving on a Special Ignition Interlock Restricted Driver License?
sec20-card-sec20-F36.expected_back: A person holding an interlock restricted license must follow the interlock rules, finish any required alcohol treatment classes, and carry proof of future financial responsibility coverage.

sec20-card-sec20-F37.front: Which MVD division conducts hearings when individuals or businesses contest an MVD order?
sec20-card-sec20-F37.expected_back: The Executive Hearing Office holds hearings requested by people or businesses contesting an MVD order.

sec20-card-sec20-F38.front: What type of MVD action makes up the bulk of Executive Hearing Office cases?
sec20-card-sec20-F38.expected_back: Most Executive Hearing Office cases are appeals of an order suspending or revoking a driver license, usually because of traffic law violations.

sec20-card-sec20-R11.front: What is the core role of Arizona's Executive Hearing Office, and which orders dominate its calendar?
sec20-card-sec20-R11.expected_back: The Executive Hearing Office hears challenges to MVD orders, most often orders suspending or revoking a license.

sec17-card-sec17-F01.front: What must your right foot do with the gas and brake pedals the instant your tires hydroplane?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.expected_back: If your car hydroplanes, take your foot off the accelerator and do not brake.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.front: How should you manage the steering wheel while your tires are hydroplaning?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.expected_back: While hydroplaning, avoid steering changes if you can and hold the wheel firmly until the tires grip the road again.

sec17-card-sec17-F03.front: What sudden water hazard does heavy rain routinely trigger across Arizona desert washes?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.expected_back: Heavy rain often causes flash floods in Arizona washes.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.front: Which three dangers explain why you must never drive into a flooded Arizona wash?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.expected_back: Never cross a flooded wash, because the water can stall your engine, hide potholes and carry your vehicle downstream.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.front: How can you estimate the depth of water standing on a roadway?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.expected_back: Judge how deep water is by looking at parked cars or other objects along the road and by watching what other vehicles do.

sec17-card-sec17-F06.front: How should two oncoming drivers coordinate crossing deep standing water, and why?
sec17-card-sec17-F06.expected_back: Two vehicles should not meet in deep water, so one should drive all the way through before the other starts from the opposite side, which lowers the risk of stalling from waves.

sec17-card-sec17-F07.front: What financial consequence can follow if rescuers have to pull you or your car from a flooded road?
sec17-card-sec17-F07.expected_back: You may be charged for emergency response costs if you or your vehicle has to be removed from a flooded road.

sec17-card-sec17-F12.front: What legal liability hits an Arizona driver who drives around flood barricades and gets stranded?
sec17-card-sec17-F12.expected_back: A driver who goes around flood barricades is liable for the cost of any emergency response needed to remove the driver or passengers when the vehicle becomes inoperable on a public street or highway.

sec17-card-sec17-F13.front: How does Arizona define the emergency-response expenses billed after a flood rescue?
sec17-card-sec17-F13.expected_back: The expenses of an emergency response are the reasonable costs that responding agencies directly incur when they make an appropriate response.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.front: How does general flood-rescue billing compare with bypassing a posted flood barricade?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.expected_back: Being removed from a flooded road may bring a charge for response costs, and going around a flood barricade makes the driver liable for those costs.

sec17-card-sec17-F08.front: How should you manage your speed whenever you must drive through shallow standing water?
sec17-card-sec17-F08.expected_back: Drive through water at a slow and steady speed.

sec17-card-sec17-F09.front: What pedal technique while rolling through water can help keep brake linings dry?
sec17-card-sec17-F09.expected_back: Pressing the brakes lightly with your left foot while driving through water may help keep them dry.

sec17-card-sec17-F10.front: Why must you test your brakes right after driving out of standing water?
sec17-card-sec17-F10.expected_back: After leaving water, test your brakes, because wet brakes may grab suddenly or pull to one side.

sec17-card-sec17-F11.front: How do you safely dry wet brakes once your wheels are back on dry pavement?
sec17-card-sec17-F11.expected_back: Dry wet brakes by accelerating slowly while holding the brake pedal down gently.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.front: Contrast your brake-pedal rule during hydroplaning with your brake routine after exiting deep puddles?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.expected_back: During a hydroplane you do not brake at all, while after driving through water you test the brakes and dry them by gently holding the pedal as you accelerate slowly.

sec17-card-sec17-F14.front: What optical problem do suspended fog droplets create with your own headlights?
sec17-card-sec17-F14.expected_back: Fog reflects light and can bounce your own headlights back into your eyes.

sec17-card-sec17-F15.front: Which headlight setting and pavement reference keep you aligned in fog?
sec17-card-sec17-F15.expected_back: In fog, use only your low beams and follow the road edge markings.

sec17-card-sec17-F16.front: Why does even thin, light fog demand an immediate speed reduction?
sec17-card-sec17-F16.expected_back: Even light fog cuts visibility and your ability to judge distance, so slowing down is very important.

sec17-card-sec17-F17.front: Why must you keep adjusting speed continuously when driving through fog?
sec17-card-sec17-F17.expected_back: Fog can thicken from one moment to the next, so keep adjusting your speed and be ready for emergency maneuvers.

sec17-card-sec17-F18.front: What three steps apply when fog grows too dense to continue safely?
sec17-card-sec17-F18.expected_back: If fog gets too thick, pull off the road, turn off your headlights and wait there until the fog lifts.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.front: How does your headlight setting in fog change between driving on the road and waiting off-road?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.expected_back: In fog you drive on low beams, but if you pull off the road to wait it out you turn the headlights off.

sec17-card-sec17-F19.front: What dual visibility purpose do headlights serve during falling snow?
sec17-card-sec17-F19.expected_back: Snow limits visibility, so you need your headlights on both to see and to be seen.

sec17-card-sec17-F20.front: How does snow-covered pavement change lane positioning and oncoming clearance?
sec17-card-sec17-F20.expected_back: Snow often hides lane markings completely, and drivers may drift away from the road edge and pass closer to one another.

sec17-card-sec17-F21.front: In the Arizona manual's phrasing, how much does snow or ice add to your needed stopping distance?
sec17-card-sec17-F21.expected_back: Snow or ice between your tires and the road greatly reduces traction and, in the manual's words, adds at least six seconds to the distance you need to stop.

sec17-card-sec17-F22.front: On slick snow or ice, why does your car respond better to steering than to hard braking?
sec17-card-sec17-F22.expected_back: On a slippery surface you keep the most traction and control while the front tires are rolling, so the car responds better to steering than to braking.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.front: What tire condition preserves maximum control on slippery surfaces, favoring steering over braking?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.expected_back: On slippery surfaces the car answers steering better than braking, because rolling front tires keep the most traction.

sec17-card-sec17-F23.front: How should you apply brake pressure when slowing down on ice or slick pavement?
sec17-card-sec17-F23.expected_back: If you brake on ice or another slippery surface, start gently and build pressure as you feel the tires grip.

sec17-card-sec17-F24.front: What braking mistake must you never commit on a slippery surface?
sec17-card-sec17-F24.expected_back: On a slippery surface, never brake so hard that the wheels lock.

sec17-card-sec17-F25.front: If your wheels lock up on slick pavement, what pedal cycle restores rolling grip?
sec17-card-sec17-F25.expected_back: If the wheels lock, ease slightly off the brakes without letting go completely, then brake and ease off again, repeating the cycle.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.front: When tires lock on ice, do you yank your foot completely off the brake or ease off slightly?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.expected_back: If the wheels lock on ice you ease slightly off the brake but do not release it fully, then brake and ease off again.

sec17-card-sec17-F26.front: Which two abrupt driver inputs must you avoid during winter driving?
sec17-card-sec17-F26.expected_back: In winter, drive with caution and avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

sec17-card-sec17-F27.front: What must you clear completely off your vehicle before pulling out in winter?
sec17-card-sec17-F27.expected_back: Before you start driving in winter, clear the snow and ice from every window and light.

sec17-card-sec17-F28.front: Which two benefits do snow tires or tire chains provide on winter roads?
sec17-card-sec17-F28.expected_back: Snow tires or chains help prevent skids and shorten stopping distances.

sec17-card-sec17-F29.front: What surface does packed snow mimic, and when must you shed speed on it?
sec17-card-sec17-F29.expected_back: Packed snow behaves much like ice, so slow down before you stop or turn on it.

sec17-card-sec17-F30.front: Which two roadway spots ice over earliest, and why do bridges freeze ahead of regular pavement?
sec17-card-sec17-F30.expected_back: Watch for ice on bridges and in shady spots, because bridge surfaces freeze before the rest of the road.

sec17-card-sec17-R09.front: Pair Arizona's rule on early-freezing spots with how to treat hard-packed snow?
sec17-card-sec17-R09.expected_back: Bridges and shady spots ice over first, and packed snow should be treated much like ice.

sec17-card-sec17-F31.front: During which daytime hazards should you switch on low-beam headlights?
sec17-card-sec17-F31.expected_back: Turn on your low-beam headlights in sun glare, rain, dust or any other condition where other drivers may not see your vehicle clearly.

sec17-card-sec17-F32.front: How do daytime headlights protect you along open two-lane rural highways?
sec17-card-sec17-F32.expected_back: On rural roads, your headlights help a driver who is thinking of passing in your lane see that you are coming.

sec17-card-sec17-F33.front: Which three visual challenges combine to make nighttime driving hazardous?
sec17-card-sec17-F33.expected_back: Reduced visibility, glare from oncoming headlights and objects you cannot see in the road combine to make night driving hazardous.

sec17-card-sec17-F35.front: Between which daily sun markers are headlights legally mandatory, and what caution remains?
sec17-card-sec17-F35.expected_back: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise, but remember that other drivers may not have switched theirs on.

sec17-card-sec17-R08.front: Should you switch on parking lights or full headlights at dusk, and when does the legal mandate run?
sec17-card-sec17-R08.expected_back: At dusk you switch on headlights rather than parking lights, and from sunset to sunrise headlights are required by law.

sec17-card-sec17-F36.front: How does headlight reach cap your safe driving speed after dark?
sec17-card-sec17-F36.expected_back: Never drive so fast that you cannot stop within the distance your headlights let you see.

sec17-card-sec17-F37.front: Which headlight beam setting belongs on city or town streets?
sec17-card-sec17-F37.expected_back: Use low beams when driving on city or town streets.

sec17-card-sec17-F38.front: On an open highway at night, within what oncoming distance are high beams prohibited?
sec17-card-sec17-F38.expected_back: On highways, use high beams only when no oncoming vehicle is within five hundred feet.

sec17-card-sec17-F39.front: Why must you switch from high beams to low beams whenever meeting oncoming traffic?
sec17-card-sec17-F39.expected_back: Switch to low beams whenever you meet oncoming traffic so you do not blind the other driver.

sec17-card-sec17-F40.front: Within what distance behind another vehicle must you switch from high beams to low beams?
sec17-card-sec17-F40.expected_back: When following another car, use low beams once you are within two hundred feet of it.

sec17-card-sec17-R06.front: Pair Arizona's oncoming high-beam dimming distance with its following high-beam dimming distance?
sec17-card-sec17-R06.memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred behind
sec17-card-sec17-R06.expected_back: High beams on a highway must be dimmed for an oncoming vehicle within five hundred feet, while low beams are needed within two hundred feet of a car you follow.

sec17-card-sec17-R07.front: Contrast where low beams belong with the sole setting where high beams are appropriate?
sec17-card-sec17-R07.memory_hook: Town storms low, open highways high
sec17-card-sec17-R07.expected_back: Low beams belong on city or town streets and in glare, rain or dust, while high beams are only for highways with no close oncoming traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-F41.front: Where should you direct your eyes if an oncoming driver forgets to dim high beams?
sec17-card-sec17-F41.expected_back: If an oncoming driver does not dim the high beams, do not stare into them, but glance at the right side of the road and then ahead to track the other vehicle.

sec17-card-sec17-F42.front: How long do you maintain that right-edge-and-ahead glance routine against bright oncoming lights?
sec17-card-sec17-F42.expected_back: Keep up that glance to the right and ahead until you are past the oncoming vehicle with bright lights.

sec17-card-sec17-F43.front: What is highway hypnosis, and what nickname describes it?
sec17-card-sec17-F43.expected_back: Highway hypnosis, also called white line fever, is a trance-like state that can set in during long periods of highway driving.

sec17-card-sec17-F44.front: What immediate action should you take anytime you start feeling tired on a trip?
sec17-card-sec17-F44.expected_back: Whenever you feel tired on a trip, pull over and rest.

sec17-card-sec17-F45.front: Which two simple cabin adjustments help fend off highway hypnosis?
sec17-card-sec17-F45.expected_back: The radio and fresh air can help you fight off highway hypnosis.

sec17-card-sec17-F46.front: How often does Arizona recommend stopping to walk and stretch on long highway trips?
sec17-card-sec17-F46.expected_back: On long trips, stop every hour to walk and exercise so you stay alert.

sec17-card-sec17-R12.front: Combine Arizona's three defenses against highway hypnosis on long drives?
sec17-card-sec17-R12.expected_back: Highway hypnosis is fought with rest when tired, the radio and fresh air, and an hourly stop to walk.

sec17-card-sec17-F47.front: Why must defensive awareness stay switched on at every hour of the day or night?
sec17-card-sec17-F47.expected_back: Drive defensively at every hour, staying aware of conditions and surroundings so you can take evasive action against a hazard such as a wrong-way driver.

sec17-card-sec17-F48.front: How does leaving generous following room protect you from a sudden wrong-way driver ahead?
sec17-card-sec17-F48.expected_back: Do not tailgate, so that if the car ahead swerves to avoid a wrong-way driver you have time to react as well.

sec17-card-sec17-F49.front: In which freeway lanes do wrong-way drivers usually travel, and how do they enter the highway?
sec17-card-sec17-F49.expected_back: Wrong-way drivers are usually in the left or HOV lane, yet they get onto highways from the right by using off-ramps.

sec17-card-sec17-F50.front: Why are a wrong-way driver's steering moves so unpredictable?
sec17-card-sec17-F50.expected_back: Wrong-way drivers are often impaired, which makes their movements unpredictable.

sec17-card-sec17-F57.front: What driver condition causes the majority of wrong-way freeway collisions?
sec17-card-sec17-F57.expected_back: Most wrong-way crashes are caused by impaired drivers.

sec17-card-sec17-R10.front: Why must you watch both right-side off-ramps and the far-left HOV lane for wrong-way cars?
sec17-card-sec17-R10.expected_back: Wrong-way drivers usually travel in the left or HOV lane even though they enter the highway from the right by an off-ramp.

sec17-card-sec17-F51.front: What is your immediate pedal move if headlights come straight at you on a divided highway?
sec17-card-sec17-F51.expected_back: On a divided highway, if a vehicle is coming at you head-on, lift your foot off the gas to slow down.

sec17-card-sec17-F52.front: What quick check precedes steering away from an oncoming wrong-way vehicle?
sec17-card-sec17-F52.expected_back: Make sure no vehicle is beside you, then steer away from the wrong-way driver.
