sec17-card-sec17-F53.front: When and how should you report a wrong-way vehicle to authorities?
sec17-card-sec17-F53.expected_back: Once you reach a safe place, call nine one one and report the wrong-way driver.

sec17-card-sec17-F54.front: How do Arizona highway officials warn motorists once a wrong-way vehicle is reported?
sec17-card-sec17-F54.expected_back: When ADOT is alerted to a possible wrong-way driver, overhead message boards on that part of the freeway show a wrong-way driver alert.

sec17-card-sec17-F55.front: What action should you take as soon as an overhead board displays a wrong-way driver alert?
sec17-card-sec17-F55.expected_back: If you see a wrong-way driver alert on an overhead board, move safely toward the nearest exit as soon as you can.

sec17-card-sec17-R11.front: Contrast your response to spotting oncoming headlights versus reading an overhead wrong-way alert?
sec17-card-sec17-R11.expected_back: Seeing a wrong-way vehicle coming at you means ease off the gas and steer away, while seeing an overhead wrong-way alert means head for the nearest exit.

sec17-card-sec17-F56.front: Which two personal pledges keep you and friends from causing distracted or wrong-way tragedies?
sec17-card-sec17-F56.expected_back: Never drive while distracted or impaired, and never let an impaired person drive.

sec21-card-sec21-F01.front: Why must you submit any MVD hearing request within the statutory deadline?
sec21-card-sec21-F01.expected_back: File any hearing request within the time the law allows, because you may lose your right to a hearing if you delay.

sec21-card-sec21-F02.front: What scope of guidance can the Executive Hearing Office provide, and whom should you ask for specific legal advice?
sec21-card-sec21-F02.expected_back: The Executive Hearing Office may give only general information, so for specific legal advice you might consult an attorney.

sec21-card-sec21-F03.front: When can skids, tire blowouts, or sudden mechanical failures strike on the road?
sec21-card-sec21-F03.expected_back: Skids, tire blowouts and mechanical failures can happen at any time, so be prepared to handle them.

sec21-card-sec21-F04.front: What routine maintenance habit lowers your risk of suffering a tire blowout?
sec21-card-sec21-F04.expected_back: Checking your tire pressure regularly lowers your chances of a blowout.

sec21-card-sec21-F05.front: What is your immediate steering-wheel duty the instant a tire blows out?
sec21-card-sec21-F05.expected_back: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle traveling straight.

sec21-card-sec21-F06.front: While rolling through a fresh tire blowout, how do you handle the accelerator and brake pedals?
sec21-card-sec21-F06.expected_back: During a blowout, ease off the gas pedal and do not use the brakes.

sec21-card-sec21-F07.front: After a blowout, how slow should the car coast before you signal, pull off the roadway, and brake?
sec21-card-sec21-F07.expected_back: After a blowout, let the vehicle slow until it is almost stopped, then signal, pull off the roadway and brake.

sec21-card-sec21-R01.front: In Arizona's blowout sequence, at what exact stage do you finally touch the brake pedal?
sec21-card-sec21-R01.expected_back: During a blowout you do not brake until the car is almost stopped, and only then do you signal, pull off and apply the brakes.

sec21-card-sec21-F08.front: What system fault causes most motor-vehicle fires?
sec21-card-sec21-F08.expected_back: Vehicle fires are usually caused by a short circuit in the electrical system.

sec21-card-sec21-F09.front: In order, what four life-safety steps must you take if your vehicle catches fire?
sec21-card-sec21-F09.expected_back: If your vehicle catches fire, pull off the road quickly, shut off the ignition to cut electrical power, get every passenger away from the car and call nine one one.

sec21-card-sec21-F10.front: Which rated type of portable fire extinguisher is best suited for motor-vehicle fires?
sec21-card-sec21-F10.expected_back: Always carry a fire extinguisher, and an ABC-rated dry chemical extinguisher is best for vehicle fires.

sec21-card-sec21-F11.front: Why must you never pour water onto burning gasoline?
sec21-card-sec21-F11.expected_back: Never use water on burning gasoline, because water spreads the flames.

sec21-card-sec21-F12.front: If you don't have a fire extinguisher handy, which three items can help smother small vehicle flames?
sec21-card-sec21-F12.expected_back: Without an extinguisher, a heavy blanket, a heavy coat or sand can help smother the flames.

sec21-card-sec21-F13.front: What is the rule whenever a vehicle fire looks like it might grow beyond your control?
sec21-card-sec21-F13.expected_back: If there is any sign the fire may be beyond your control, get away from the vehicle.

sec21-card-sec21-R02.front: Which tools safely fight a small vehicle fire, and what liquid must never touch burning gasoline?
sec21-card-sec21-R02.expected_back: A vehicle fire calls for an ABC dry chemical extinguisher, or a heavy blanket, coat or sand, but never water on burning gasoline.

sec21-card-sec21-F14.front: What mechanical trouble does white steam billowing from under your hood usually indicate?
sec21-card-sec21-F14.expected_back: Steam rising from under the hood may mean the cooling system has overheated.

sec21-card-sec21-F15.front: What two immediate steps should you take as soon as your engine overheats?
sec21-card-sec21-F15.expected_back: If the engine overheats, pull to the side of the road and shut off the engine right away.

sec21-card-sec21-F16.front: On an overheated car, how do you handle the hood versus the radiator cap—and why?
sec21-card-sec21-F16.expected_back: With an overheated engine, raise the hood but leave the radiator cap closed, since opening it while hot can release steam and cause severe burns.

sec21-card-sec21-F17.front: In desert Arizona driving, what spare fluid should you pack for the radiator, and when may you add it?
sec21-card-sec21-F17.expected_back: Carry extra water for the radiator, and add it only after the engine has cooled.

sec21-card-sec21-R03.front: With an overheated engine, how do the hood, radiator cap, and spare water work together?
sec21-card-sec21-R03.expected_back: With an overheated engine you raise the hood but keep the radiator cap on, and you add water only once the engine has cooled.

sec21-card-sec21-F18.front: If your engine stalls mid-turn and power steering drops out, how do you steer to safety?
sec21-card-sec21-F18.expected_back: If power steering fails, for example when the engine dies in a turn, grip the wheel firmly with both hands to finish the turn and move to the right side of the road.

sec21-card-sec21-F19.front: After losing engine power and power steering, how must you press power brakes to stop?
sec21-card-sec21-F19.expected_back: After a power steering failure, stop the car, pressing extra hard on the brake pedal if the vehicle has power brakes.

sec21-card-sec21-R06.front: When an engine dies mid-turn, how do your hands on the wheel and your foot on power brakes adapt?
sec21-card-sec21-R06.expected_back: When the engine dies in a turn, the steering response is to grip with both hands and finish the turn, while the braking response is to press extra hard if the car has power brakes.

sec21-card-sec21-F20.front: If your headlights suddenly go dark at night, which switch should you try first?
sec21-card-sec21-F20.expected_back: If your headlights fail, first try the high and low beam switch, which may bring them back.

sec21-card-sec21-F21.front: If toggling the high-low dimmer doesn't bring headlights back, what switch action comes second?
sec21-card-sec21-F21.expected_back: If the headlights stay off, turn the headlight switch on and off several times.

sec21-card-sec21-F22.front: If headlights refuse to come back on at all, which backup lights do you use as you pull off?
sec21-card-sec21-F22.expected_back: If the headlights still fail, switch on the parking lights, emergency flashers or turn signals, then pull to the side of the road and stop.

sec21-card-sec21-F23.front: On a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes, should you ever pump the brake pedal?
sec21-card-sec21-F23.expected_back: Many vehicles have anti-lock braking systems (ABS), and anti-lock brakes should not be pumped.

sec21-card-sec21-F24.front: If regular brakes fail on a vehicle without anti-lock brakes, what pedal technique should you try first?
sec21-card-sec21-F24.expected_back: If brakes fail on a vehicle without anti-lock brakes, pump the pedal rapidly, which may build enough pressure to stop.

sec21-card-sec21-R04.front: How does proper pedal technique differ between working anti-lock brakes and failed conventional brakes?
sec21-card-sec21-R04.expected_back: Anti-lock brakes should not be pumped, while failed ordinary brakes should be pumped rapidly to build pressure.

sec21-card-sec21-F25.front: When main brakes fail completely, how must you apply the parking brake and why hold its release?
sec21-card-sec21-F25.expected_back: If pumping does not help, apply the parking brake slowly while holding the brake release so you can ease off if the rear wheels lock and the car starts to skid.

sec21-card-sec21-R07.front: During brake failure, what skid hazard explains keeping your thumb or hand on the parking-brake release?
sec21-card-sec21-R07.expected_back: When the parking brake is used for a brake failure, you hold the release so you can let off if the rear wheels lock.

sec21-card-sec21-F26.front: Alongside pedal and parking-brake work, what gearshift and scanning steps help stop a car with failed brakes?
sec21-card-sec21-F26.expected_back: During a brake failure, shift to a lower gear and look for a safe place to stop.

sec21-card-sec21-F27.front: If you're stopped at a sign or light and spot a car closing fast in your mirror, what can help?
sec21-card-sec21-F27.expected_back: If you are stopped at a light or stop sign and a vehicle is coming up fast behind you, pull forward if you can to give it more room to stop.

sec21-card-sec21-F28.front: How do you brace your body and time your brake foot right before an unavoidable rear-end impact?
sec21-card-sec21-F28.expected_back: If a rear-end crash cannot be avoided, brace yourself between the steering wheel and the seat back and release the brake an instant before impact.

sec21-card-sec21-F29.front: Which three actions warn an oncoming driver drifting into your lane toward a head-on crash?
sec21-card-sec21-F29.expected_back: To head off a possible head-on crash, slow down, flash your headlights and sound your horn to warn the other driver.

sec21-card-sec21-F30.front: If an oncoming vehicle keeps coming in your lane, where should you steer to escape?
sec21-card-sec21-F30.expected_back: Facing a possible head-on crash, head for the shoulder and get off the road away from the oncoming driver.

sec21-card-sec21-F31.front: If a head-on collision cannot be escaped altogether, what is your steering goal?
sec21-card-sec21-F31.expected_back: If a head-on crash cannot be avoided, steer so as to make the impact less severe.

sec21-card-sec21-R05.front: How does your final-moment action before a rear-end hit contrast with facing a head-on threat?
sec21-card-sec21-R05.expected_back: Before a rear-end hit you release the brake an instant before impact, while before a head-on crash you slow down and head for the shoulder.

sec21-card-sec21-F32.front: What single habit gives you the strongest protection against injury if a crash happens?
sec21-card-sec21-F32.expected_back: Buckling your safety belt every time is your single best protection against injury if a crash happens.

sec21-card-sec21-F33.front: When two road hazards appear together and cannot be separated in time, what does compromise mean?
sec21-card-sec21-F33.expected_back: Compromise means that when two or more risks cannot be separated, you give the most room to the greatest or most likely danger.

sec21-card-sec21-F34.front: With oncoming traffic on your left and a child bicycling on your right, where do you position your car—and why?
sec21-card-sec21-F34.expected_back: With oncoming cars on your left and a child on a bike on your right, the child is the most likely to move suddenly, so moving closer to the center line is the right compromise.

sec21-card-sec21-R09.front: Why does Arizona's compromise rule give extra space to a bicycling child over oncoming cars?
sec21-card-sec21-R09.expected_back: When two hazards cannot be separated, the extra room goes to the most likely danger, such as a child on a bike rather than oncoming cars.

sec21-card-sec21-F35.front: Which surface condition and pedal mistake commonly throw a vehicle into a skid?
sec21-card-sec21-F35.expected_back: A slippery road or braking too sharply can throw your vehicle into a skid.

sec21-card-sec21-F36.front: Once your vehicle enters a skid, what must you do with the brake pedal—and why?
sec21-card-sec21-F36.expected_back: In a skid, stop pressing the brake, since more braking only makes the skid worse.

sec21-card-sec21-F37.front: Which direction do you turn the steering wheel immediately when your car skids?
sec21-card-sec21-F37.expected_back: In a skid, quickly turn the wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go, which is the direction of the skid.

sec21-card-sec21-F38.front: What steering follow-up prevents fishtailing as your skidding vehicle begins to straighten out?
sec21-card-sec21-F38.expected_back: As the car starts to straighten, quickly turn the wheel back the other way, and keep correcting until the vehicle returns to its normal path.

sec21-card-sec21-R08.front: What two linked steering motions bring a skidding vehicle cleanly back onto its normal path?
sec21-card-sec21-R08.expected_back: In a skid you steer toward where you want to go, which is the direction of the skid, and then steer back as the car straightens.

sec21-card-sec21-F39.front: Which three types of roadway debris show up frequently on Arizona highways?
sec21-card-sec21-F39.expected_back: Road debris is common in Arizona, including pieces of blown tires, unsecured loads falling off trucks and rocks washed onto the road in storms.

sec21-card-sec21-F40.front: How do many serious Arizona road-debris crashes actually happen compared with driving straight over small debris?
sec21-card-sec21-F40.expected_back: A common debris crash happens when a driver swerves to miss the debris, loses control and leaves the road, when driving over it might have been far less severe.

sec21-card-sec21-F41.front: Why should you mentally rehearse debris scenarios while scanning ahead on clean pavement?
sec21-card-sec21-F41.expected_back: Stay alert and think ahead about what you would do if debris suddenly appeared in front of you, since you may have only a split second to decide.

sec21-card-sec21-R11.front: Why isn't swerving hard to dodge road debris always the safest move?
sec21-card-sec21-R11.expected_back: Swerving hard to miss road debris is a common cause of run-off-road crashes, and sometimes driving over the debris is the less severe choice.

sec21-card-sec21-F42.front: How do wild animals and ranch livestock end up on Arizona roadways?
sec21-card-sec21-F42.expected_back: Wildlife may dart onto the road in unexpected places, and livestock may get out when people leave gates open or cut fences.

sec21-card-sec21-F43.front: What braking and steering response applies when an animal is already standing in your roadway?
sec21-card-sec21-F43.expected_back: When an animal is in the roadway, brake down to the lowest speed you safely can and steer to avoid a direct hit without losing control.

sec21-card-sec21-F44.front: Why must you keep off your horn when passing an animal standing near—not yet on—the road?
sec21-card-sec21-F44.expected_back: If an animal is near but not yet on the road, do not honk, because the noise may startle it into your path.

sec21-card-sec21-F45.front: Whom should you call when loose livestock or an animal on the highway endangers traffic?
sec21-card-sec21-F45.expected_back: Report an animal that endangers traffic by calling nine one one so law enforcement can respond.

sec21-card-sec21-R10.front: How does handling an animal already in your lane differ from passing one standing beside the shoulder?
sec21-card-sec21-R10.expected_back: An animal already on the road calls for slowing and steering around it without losing control, while an animal beside the road calls for not honking.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: Which windows and doors must operate properly on the vehicle you bring to an Arizona road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: For the road test, the driver and passenger side windows must work and both front doors must open and close properly.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: Which two current vehicle documents must you show before starting your Arizona road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: At the road test you must show proof of current registration and current automobile liability insurance for the vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: Starting with which model year must a road-test vehicle have properly fastened and adjusted seat belts?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: A road test vehicle that is a nineteen seventy-two model or newer must have seat belts, and they must be fastened and adjusted properly.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: Why doesn't Arizona's road-test seat-belt rule say every vehicle ever built?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: The seat belt requirement for a road test vehicle depends on model year, applying to nineteen seventy-two and newer vehicles.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: Are auto-drive or parking-assist features allowed during your Arizona road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems such as auto-drive and parking assistance are banned during the road test, so every maneuver must be done by hand.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: What company requirement applies to the liability policy covering any motor vehicle driven on Arizona roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Every motor vehicle driven on Arizona roads must be covered by a liability insurance policy from a company licensed to do business in Arizona.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Which state's policy rating must cover a vehicle driven primarily on Arizona roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: The policy must be an Arizona-based policy that matches where the vehicle is mainly driven.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: Why isn't holding just any active auto policy enough to satisfy Arizona's insurance law?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: Having a policy is only half the rule: the policy must come from an insurer licensed in Arizona and be an Arizona-based policy for where the vehicle is mostly driven.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: What are Arizona's three minimum passenger-vehicle liability limits for one injury, two-plus injuries, and property damage?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: Arizona's minimum liability coverage for a private passenger vehicle is twenty-five thousand dollars for bodily injury to one person, fifty thousand dollars for bodily injury to two or more people, and fifteen thousand dollars for property damage.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: How do Arizona's bodily-injury liability floors split by headcount compared with the property-damage floor?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: The two bodily injury minimums differ by headcount, twenty-five thousand dollars for one person and fifty thousand dollars for two or more, while property damage has its own lower minimum of fifteen thousand dollars.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: What should you verify about the VIN your insurer transmits—and what if one digit differs from your registration?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Check that the VIN your insurance company reports matches the VIN on your registration, and ask the insurer to resubmit the correct VIN if it does not.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: When must current insurance proof ride inside your vehicle, and when do officers demand it?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: You must keep proof of current insurance in the vehicle whenever you drive, because officers ask for it at traffic stops and at crashes.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Which three policy events do insurers report electronically to MVD, and how does MVD react to an inactive notice?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: Insurance companies report every new policy, cancellation and non-renewal to MVD, and MVD sends you an inquiry if your insurer says your policy is no longer active.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Which credentials can MVD suspend if you fail to maintain proper Arizona insurance with a matching VIN?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: Not keeping proper Arizona insurance with a correct VIN on file can lead MVD to suspend your vehicle registration, your driver license, or both.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: Does an Arizona insurance lapse or wrong VIN threaten only your vehicle registration, or your driver license too?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Losing proper insurance or carrying a wrong VIN can suspend the vehicle registration and the driver license, not just the registration.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: Which tool on AZMVDNow lets you verify the exact insurance policy MVD currently shows on file?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: You can confirm the insurance MVD has on file by using the Manage Insurance option at AZMVDNow.gov.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: What is the National Driver Register, and when does Arizona query it?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Arizona belongs to the National Driver Register, a nationwide computer system about problem drivers, and every Arizona license application is checked against it.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: What happens to your Arizona license application if the National Driver Register flags unresolved actions in another state?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: If the register shows outstanding or unresolved actions against you in another state, Arizona will not issue you a license.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: What happens if MVD discovers you gave false information on your license application?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: Giving false information on your application can get your Arizona license canceled.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: How does a National Driver Register hit differ in outcome from lying on an Arizona license application?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: The National Driver Register can block an Arizona license because of unresolved actions in another state, while false statements on the application lead to cancellation of a license already issued.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: How soon after meeting any Arizona residency trigger must you obtain an Arizona license and registration?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: State law requires you to get an Arizona driver license and vehicle registration right away once any one of the listed residency conditions applies to you.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: Which Arizona employment and child school-enrollment situations trigger immediate residency—and what job is exempt?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: Those conditions include working in Arizona (seasonal farm work excepted) and enrolling children in school without paying the non-resident tuition rate.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: Which single type of paid work inside Arizona does NOT make you an Arizona resident for licensing?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: Seasonal agricultural work is the one kind of Arizona job that does not trigger residency.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: Which two commercial office or transport activities establish Arizona residency for vehicle and licensing rules?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: They also include having a business office in Arizona that bases and operates vehicles here, or running a business that moves goods or passengers within Arizona.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: How do state occupational licenses or resident-rate tuition payments affect your Arizona driver-license status?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: Getting a state license or paying school tuition at the resident rate also makes you a resident for licensing purposes.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: Spending how many total months inside Arizona during one calendar year makes you a resident regardless of permanent home?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: Staying in Arizona for seven months or more in total during any calendar year makes you a resident no matter where your permanent home is.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: Do your seven months in Arizona have to run back-to-back in a row to trigger residency?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: Residency by time is seven months in total within a calendar year, counted regardless of where your permanent home is, not seven consecutive months.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: What does registering to vote in Arizona do to your driver-license obligation?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: Being registered to vote in Arizona is another condition that triggers the duty to get an Arizona license.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: When does an out-of-state college student stay a non-resident in Arizona—even while working a local job?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: An out-of-state student taking seven or more semester hours is not considered an Arizona resident, even with a job in the state.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Which rule wins when an out-of-state student taking eight semester hours picks up a part-time job in Tempe?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: Out-of-state students with seven or more semester hours stay non-residents even if employed, which overrides the general rule that working in Arizona makes you a resident.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: Is filling out the voter-registration section on an Arizona license or ID application mandatory?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: The driver license or ID application includes a voter registration portion you can fill out at the same time, but registering is not required to get a license.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: How does MVD protect privacy whether you decline voter registration or choose to register?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: If you decline to register to vote, that choice stays confidential, and if you do register, the application is kept confidential and used only for voter registration.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: What level of crime is submitting false voter registration information in Arizona?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: Submitting a false voter registration is a Class six felony in Arizona.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: Which three age, citizenship, and residency requirements must you meet to register to vote in Arizona?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: To register to vote you must be at least eighteen by the next General Election, a United States citizen and an Arizona resident.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Can a seventeen-year-old register to vote in Arizona if they turn eighteen on the date of the next General Election?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: The voter age test is measured on the next General Election date, so an applicant who will be eighteen on or before that date can register.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: Which two legal or court statuses disqualify someone from registering to vote in Arizona?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: You also cannot have a felony conviction unless your civil rights were restored, and you cannot have been adjudicated incompetent.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: Aside from the license application itself, what two other MVD channels let you register to vote?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: Besides the license application, you can register to vote online at AZMVDNow.gov or on a separate form available at MVD offices.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: How many days before an election must you register to vote in it, and what is the fee?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: To vote in an upcoming election you must be registered twenty-nine days before it, and registering costs nothing.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: What voter-registration step is required every time you move to a new Arizona address?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: When you change your address you must register to vote again.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: What pre-election day count and post-move rule govern keeping your Arizona ballot eligibility active?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: You must be registered twenty-nine days before an election to vote in it, and moving to a new address means you must register to vote again.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: Which donor registry can you join directly by checking a box on your Arizona license or ID application?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: The license or ID application has a box to join the Donate Life AZ Registry as an organ and tissue donor.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: Beyond the paper application box, what three other ways can you join Arizona's organ and tissue donor registry?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: You can also sign up as a donor by saying yes at an MVD or third-party office, by checking the box when applying online at AZMVDNow.gov, or through DonateLifeAZ.org.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: What optional health alert can be printed on an Arizona license for first responders?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: Your license has space for a medical condition indicator for conditions that may need immediate attention.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: Which three signed medical or legal documents qualify you to add the medical condition indicator to your license?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: Getting the medical code takes paperwork about the condition: a statement signed by a licensed physician or by a registered nurse practitioner, or an advanced healthcare directive.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: What federal identification number must you prove under state and federal law when applying for an Arizona license?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: State and federal law require you to provide proof of a valid Social Security number when you apply.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: How does Arizona's medical condition indicator differ from Social Security number proof on a license application?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: The medical condition indicator is an optional entry you request with documentation, whereas proof of a valid Social Security number is mandatory under state and federal law.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: If MVD revokes, suspends, or cancels your license, which two fees may you owe to get back on the road?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: If MVD revokes, suspends or cancels your license, you may owe a fresh application fee in addition to a reinstatement fee.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: Does paying a single reinstatement fee cover everything owed after an Arizona revocation, suspension, or cancellation?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: A revoked, suspended or canceled license can cost two charges, a new application fee plus a reinstatement fee, not just one reinstatement fee.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: What fees does MVD assess for an abandoned vehicle—including on federal land—and for a bounced check?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: MVD lists an abandoned vehicle fee of five hundred dollars (six hundred dollars when the vehicle is left on federal land) and a twenty-five dollars fee for a returned check.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: Beyond cash, which three payment forms do most MVD offices accept, and what payee name goes on checks?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Besides cash, most MVD fees can be paid by credit card, cashier's check or money order, and checks or money orders should be made out to Motor Vehicle Division.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: Which online portal should you check before driving to MVD, and which three applications can you start there?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: To save time, check AZMVDNow.gov first to see whether your transaction can be finished online, and use it to fill out an application for an ID, driver license or title.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Which three in-person MVD appointments do you schedule through the AZMVDNow portal?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: AZMVDNow.gov is also where you book an appointment for a road test, a Travel credential or a license renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: On which monthly and post-holiday days are MVD lobbies busiest, and when do most offices stay shut until noon?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: Offices are busiest on the first two and last two days of each month and on the day after a holiday, and most offices stay closed until noon on the second Wednesday of every month.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Which two advantages come from bringing your valid out-of-state driver license to an Arizona MVD visit?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: Bring your out-of-state driver license to MVD, because it serves as a secondary form of identification and can waive the written or road test.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Alongside required personal ID, which four vehicle items or numbers should you bring to MVD?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: When visiting MVD, bring your required identification, any out-of-state title, registration and license plates, and have the vehicle identification number (VIN) ready.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Does presenting an out-of-state driver license let you leave your primary required identification at home?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: An out-of-state license brought to MVD works as secondary identification and may waive the written or road test, and you still bring the required identification as well.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: Under Arizona statute twenty-eight three-one-five-three D, what must every applicant prove before MVD issues or renews a card?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Under Arizona Revised Statutes section twenty-eight-three thousand one hundred fifty-three(D), MVD may not issue or renew a driver license or ID card unless the applicant proves that federal law authorizes their presence in the United States.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: Does Arizona verify authorized federal presence only on your first license application, or at renewals too?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: Legal presence is a gate for both issuing and renewing a license or ID card, not only for a first license.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: What caution does MVD give applicants regarding its acceptable identification list?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: MVD warns that identification requirements can change without notice.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Within how many days must you notify Arizona MVD after changing your name or residential address?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: Arizona law requires you to tell MVD about any change of name or address within ten days.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: Does Arizona grant more time to report a legal name change than a street address change?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: Name changes and address changes share one deadline in Arizona: both must reach MVD within ten days, so there is no separate longer window for a name change.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Which two real-world problems hit drivers who fail to report a name or address change to MVD?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: If you skip reporting a change, renewal notices and other mail about your license or vehicles may never reach you, and police may cite you.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Which five personal details verify an online address update at AZMVDNow?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: An address change can be filed online at AZMVDNow.gov by giving your full name, the new address with zip code, your license number and birth date, plus the final four digits of your Social Security number.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Does filing your new address with MVD automatically mail you a reprinted card—or how do you get one?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Reporting a new address does not reprint your card; to show the new address on the credential you must apply for and buy a replacement license.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: Right after you file an online address change, what address still shows on the card in your wallet?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: Filing an address change updates MVD records but leaves the old address on your card until you buy a replacement license.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: Because Arizona MVD links customer records, which files update together when you submit a single address change?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Because MVD links all of your records, one address change updates your license or ID record and every vehicle record that lists you as first registered owner.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: Where must you go to record a legal name change, and what two sets of identification are required?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: A name change is done in person at any MVD office or at an authorized third party office that handles driver licenses, with identification in both your new and your former name.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How does Arizona's filing channel for an address change contrast with filing a legal name change?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: An address change can be done entirely online, while the manual sends a name change to an MVD or authorized third party office with identification in both names.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: What agency's records must match your new name before MVD prints a replacement license?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: To have the new name printed on your license you apply for a replacement license, and every name must be verifiable against Social Security Administration records.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: When are military service members stationed in Arizona exempt from being treated as Arizona residents?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: Service members based in Arizona are not counted as Arizona residents when they qualify for the Soldiers and Sailors Relief Act exemption.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: How does the active-duty Relief Act residency exemption differ from Arizona's post-discharge military rule?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Service members stationed in Arizona under the relief act exemption are not residents, which is different from the post-discharge rule that limits work on an outside license.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: For how many days after military discharge may a former service member work in Arizona using an outside license?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: After discharge, a former service member may work in Arizona for up to ninety days without an Arizona license, but only if all of the listed conditions are met.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: Which three license, vehicle-class, and employer rules unlock that ninety-day post-discharge work allowance?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: Those conditions are a valid license from another state or country, driving a vehicle that needs only a Class D license, and working for an organization that operates both in Arizona and in at least one other state or country.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Does Arizona's ninety-day post-discharge rule give every newly arrived civilian ninety days to switch licenses?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: The ninety-day allowance for discharged service members is a work allowance that applies only when all three conditions hold, not a general grace period for every new arrival.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: Who qualifies to have VETERAN printed on the front of an Arizona license, permit, or ID?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: A Veteran Designation, printed as the word VETERAN on the front of the license, instruction permit or ID, is available to United States military veterans and active duty service members.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: Who qualifies to have NATIVE AMERICAN printed on the front of an Arizona credential?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: A Native American Designation, printed as NATIVE AMERICAN on the front of the credential, is available to enrolled members of a federally recognized tribe located in Arizona.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: How does eligibility for Arizona's VETERAN front designation differ from its NATIVE AMERICAN designation?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: The VETERAN mark is open to veterans and active duty members, while the NATIVE AMERICAN mark requires enrollment in a federally recognized tribe located in Arizona.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: What three application, photo, and cost steps apply when adding VETERAN or NATIVE AMERICAN to your card?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: Adding either designation requires a new application and a new photo, and the standard transaction fees apply.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: What are the two ways—online versus form forty-six four-four-one-six—to obtain your Arizona driving or motor vehicle record?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: A copy of your driving or motor vehicle record is available through AZMVDNow.gov, or by filling out the Motor Vehicle Record Request form forty-six-four thousand four hundred sixteen and taking it to an MVD or Authorized Third Party office, where you must show identification.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: Where do you book an Arizona road test, and why check multiple MVD locations when scheduling?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: Road test appointments are booked at AZMVDNow.gov, booking ahead is strongly encouraged so you can test when you arrive, and checking several offices helps you find the earliest slot.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: Does holding a confirmed AZMVDNow appointment guarantee your road test will run that day?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: Road tests can be suspended for extreme weather or safety conditions even when an appointment was booked, so a booking is not a guarantee.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: Which two environmental or operational hazards cause MVD to pause road testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: Extreme weather or unsafe conditions can lead MVD to suspend road testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: What roadway literacy check must you clear before your Arizona road test rolls out?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: Before the road test you must show that you understand Arizona traffic signs.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: Which spoken English driving commands and cabin checks must you follow for the Arizona road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: You must also respond to spoken English directions: stop, slow down, change lanes left or right, drive straight ahead, turn at the next street, corner, stop sign or light, confirm your speedometer works, and fasten your seat belt.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How does the timing of Arizona's sign and spoken-English check differ from route grading?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: Sign knowledge and the spoken English directions are checked before the road test starts, whereas the route and grading happen during the drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: What does the MVD examiner do inside your car during the road test, and what two dimensions are graded?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: When a road test is required, an examiner rides in your vehicle, directs you along a route with varied traffic situations, and grades both specific actions and your overall ability to drive safely.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: Who provides the Arizona road-test car, and which seven mechanical, glass, mirror, and tire items must pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: You supply the road test vehicle, and it must have working brakes, brake lights, turn signals and horn, an uncracked windshield, inside and outside rearview mirrors, and tires in good condition.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: Will an Arizona examiner accept a road-test car missing one rearview mirror or sporting a small windshield crack?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: A road test vehicle needs both an inside and an outside rearview mirror and a windshield with no cracks; one mirror or a small crack does not meet the list.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: What does Arizona require regarding missing or defective gear—and which five controls, gauges, and alerts must work?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Your vehicle may not have defective or missing equipment, and the brakes, speedometer, turn signals, horn and emergency flashers must all be in working order.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: What condition must your windshield, tires, seat belts, and two front side windows meet?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: The windshield must be intact, the tires in good condition, the seat belts working, and the driver and front passenger side windows operational.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: Which three cockpit adjustments belong BEFORE you start the engine?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Before starting the vehicle, adjust your seat, the steering wheel, and the rearview and outside mirrors.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: Which two mechanical and electrical checks come right before shifting the vehicle into motion?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Before putting the vehicle in motion, check that the turn signals and brakes work.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: How does Arizona split your cockpit adjustments before starting the engine from your functional check before moving?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Seat, steering wheel and mirrors are adjusted before you start the vehicle, while the turn signal and brake check is the step before you put it in motion.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Which three seasonal Arizona weather extremes put extra stress on vehicle tires?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Arizona's extremes — intense summer heat, summer monsoon storms, and winter snow and ice in the high country — make tire maintenance especially important.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: What cost-free step does the Arizona manual recommend as the best way to verify tire readiness?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: A free inspection from a tire professional, which many offer, is the best way to make sure your tires can handle Arizona conditions.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: How do you place a penny into your lowest tire groove, and what visual result warns you need new tires?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: For the penny test, put Lincoln's head into a groove where the tread looks lowest; if no part of his head is covered by tread, it may be time for new tires.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: What restraint must every front-seat occupant wear while moving—including in older seats equipped only with lap belts?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Every front seat occupant must wear a properly adjusted and fastened lap and shoulder belt while the vehicle is moving, or wear a properly adjusted and fastened lap belt when only a lap belt is installed.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: If a seating position was built with only a lap belt and no shoulder strap, what rule applies in motion?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Where only a lap belt is installed at a seat, that lap belt must be properly adjusted and fastened while the vehicle is moving.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: For vehicles manufactured after which year must every front-seat occupant ride belted and adjusted?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: Each front seat occupant of a motor vehicle made after nineteen seventy-two must have a seat belt fastened and adjusted.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: Up to what passenger birthday is the driver legally responsible for making sure riders buckle up?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: The driver must make every passenger under sixteen buckle up.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: How does Arizona's front-seat belt mandate differ in reach from the driver's under-sixteen belt duty?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: The front-seat belt rule covers every front seat occupant of any age, while the driver's duty to make passengers buckle up covers every passenger under sixteen.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: How does a lap-and-shoulder belt lower severe crash trauma, and what specific job does the lap strap do?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: A combined lap and shoulder belt greatly cuts your chance of serious injury in a crash, and the lap belt keeps you from being thrown out of the vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: Which parts of your body—and which cabin surfaces—does the diagonal shoulder belt protect against?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: The shoulder belt stops your head and chest from hitting the dashboard or windshield.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: How do the lap portion and shoulder portion divide crash protection across your body?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: The lap belt prevents ejection and protects the lower body, while the shoulder belt protects the head and chest from the dashboard and windshield.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: In older cars with motorized automatic shoulder straps, what manual step remains critical?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: In vehicles with an automatic shoulder belt and a manual lap belt, buckling the lap belt is extremely important.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: Why aren't regular seat belts safe for small children, and what does Arizona mandate under age five?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Seat belts are not designed for children, and Arizona law forbids driving on state highways with a child under five who is not properly secured in a child restraint system.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Until what height milestone must children aged five through eight continue riding in a child restraint?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Children aged five to eight must stay in a child restraint system until they are at least four feet nine inches tall.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: How does Arizona's child-restraint rule for kids under five differ from kids aged five through eight?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Under five a child restraint is always required, but from five to eight the restraint is required only until the child reaches four feet nine inches.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: What does Arizona require when transporting multiple children under eight in a limited cabin space?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: A driver carrying more than one child under eight must secure as many of them in child restraints as is reasonable for the size of the passenger area and the number of passengers.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: Does Arizona set a rigid numeric seat quota when carrying several children under eight, or a space-based standard?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: With several children under eight, the rule is to secure as many as reasonably fit given the passenger area and passenger count, rather than a fixed number of seats.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: Which federal safety benchmark—and which two instruction manuals—govern installing a child restraint?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: Child restraint systems must meet United States Department of Transportation safety standards and be used according to both the seat maker's and the vehicle maker's instructions.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: Through what age should children never ride in the front passenger seat—and why?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: Air bags save lives but are unsafe for children under twelve, and children twelve and under should never ride in the front seat.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: How does Arizona's booster-seat age ceiling compare with its keep-out-of-the-front-seat airbag age?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: Car-seat ages stop at eight, but the front-seat warning reaches higher: children twelve and under should never ride in front because air bags are unsafe for them.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: What safety step must you take in a pickup or two-seater if a child has no choice except riding up front?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: If a child must ride in front, turn off the passenger-side air bag, which most newer vehicles allow with an on or off switch.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: Which three details does the Arizona manual ask motorists to report to the child-safety hotline when spotting an unbuckled child?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: The manual asks anyone who sees an unrestrained child in a moving vehicle to report the plate number, city and the child's location to its child-safety hotline.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: Which state office—and website—serves as Arizona's contact point for highway safety information?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: The Arizona Governor's Office of Highway Safety is the contact for more information on safety issues, online at azgohs.gov.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: When is Arizona's five-one-one travel phone line open, and which four core travel topics does it cover?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: Dialing five hundred eleven at any time, day or night, gives up-to-the-minute reports on traffic conditions and road closures, transit and airports.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Beyond closures, transit, and airports, which three regional or trip topics does five-one-one report?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: The five hundred eleven service also reports on tourism, metro-region quick reports, and construction and work zones.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: How do you switch a five-one-one call to touch-tone keypad mode—or make voice prompts work cleanly?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: On a five hundred eleven call, pressing the star key switches to touch-tone mode, or you can use voice prompts by listening to the whole introduction and cutting background noise.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: Which website mirrors Arizona's five-one-one phone reports, who runs both, and what do they charge?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: Travel information is also online at az511.com, and both five hundred eleven and az511.com are free services from the Arizona Department of Transportation.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: How much does ADOT charge motorists to check five-one-one by phone or at az511.com?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: The five hundred eleven line and az511.com are free ADOT services, so checking road conditions before a trip costs nothing.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: Who holds responsibility for vehicle roadworthiness, and how does skipping upkeep hit your wallet?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: Drivers are responsible for making sure the vehicle they drive is safe, and an unsafe vehicle costs more to run than a maintained one.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: What split-second advantage does a well-maintained vehicle give you in traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: A vehicle in good condition gives you an extra margin of safety when you need it.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: Where do you find your vehicle's factory maintenance schedule, and who performs those tasks?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Follow the owner's manual for routine maintenance; some tasks you can do yourself, while others need a qualified technician.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: How many days do you get to repair your vehicle and return for a follow-up re-check after failing emissions?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: If your vehicle fails a required emission inspection at an authorized station, you get thirty days to fix the problem and return for a follow-up emission re-check.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: What window opens the day your car fails an authorized Arizona emissions inspection?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: A failed emission inspection opens a thirty-day window to fix the problem and come back for a follow-up re-check.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: Under Arizona statute twenty-eight ten-ninety-eight A, what standard governs anything hauled in or on a vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: Arizona law (A.R.S. twenty-eight-one thousand ninety-eight.A) bars driving or moving a vehicle on a road unless it is built or loaded so none of its load can drop, sift, leak or otherwise escape.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: Does Arizona's secured-cargo law stop only big items falling off on freeways, or cover sifting and leaking on any street?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: The secured-load rule applies to any vehicle on a highway, street or roadway, and covers loads that drop, sift or leak as well as any other way a load can escape.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: Which two separate braking systems must every passenger car and truck carry in good working order?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: Every motor vehicle must have brakes in good working condition, and cars and trucks need both a foot brake and a parking brake.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: At minimum, how many wheels must each car or truck brake system grip—and how many brakes must a motorcycle have?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: Each set of brakes on a car or truck must work on at least two wheels, and a motorcycle needs at least one brake applied by hand or foot.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: How do Arizona's minimum brake-system and wheel rules contrast between cars-and-trucks and motorcycles?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: Cars and trucks need two separate brake systems, a foot brake and a parking brake, each acting on at least two wheels, while a motorcycle needs only one brake worked by hand or foot.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: How far ahead should moving eyes read the road in town, and what trap does that prevent?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Keep your eyes moving and read the road about one city block ahead, so you are not forced into last-minute decisions.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: Keep Arizona's two road rules separate — what uses 'one city block' versus a count in seconds?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Looking about one city block ahead is the scanning rule, and it is separate from the seconds-based count used for following distance.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: Which two directions must you scan before continuing into any intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: As you approach an intersection, look both left and right before you continue.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: What two hazards behind your bumper do frequent rearview mirror checks catch early?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Checking the rearview mirror often shows you where traffic behind you is and warns you when someone is tailgating or closing in too fast.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: Which mirror check and physical body movement must both happen before changing lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Before a lane change, check the side mirrors and also turn your head to look over your shoulder.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What awareness of surrounding traffic lets you make quick, safe choices when surprises pop up?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: When you keep track of how fast and where the traffic is in front, behind and on both sides, you can make decisions quickly and safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: How do you use a fixed roadside sign or overpass to test whether you are following too closely?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: The manual's three-six second rule tests your gap: when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point such as a sign or overpass, start counting, and if you reach that point before you finish, you are following too closely.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: Roughly how many seconds pass when you count from one-thousand-one to one-thousand-four?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Counting from one-thousand-one to one-thousand-four takes about four seconds.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: Separate the manual's four-second counting example from the full seconds range recommended for poor conditions?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: The count in the example runs to four and takes about four seconds, while the cushion the manual recommends in poor conditions spans three to six seconds.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: How must your physical following distance change as your driving speed climbs?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: The faster you go, the greater your following distance should be.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: When rain, dust, or bad pavement degrades traction, how many seconds should your following cushion span?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Poor road conditions call for more than a three-second cushion, so give yourself three to six seconds.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: What happens during your reaction delay at high speed that shrinks your margin for error?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: At high speed you travel farther while reacting to a problem, so your margin for error shrinks.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: Which single driving mistake causes the majority of rear-end collisions?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: Following too closely causes most rear-end crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: Why does open space around your car matter, and where inside your lane should you ride?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Space around your vehicle gives you and other drivers time to react to emergencies, and staying in the middle of your lane helps create that cushion.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: What two maneuvers must your front and rear space cushions stay big enough to allow?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Keep enough room ahead of you to stop suddenly, and enough room ahead and behind to pass or stop safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: When sharing a lane with a bicyclist, what minimum side gap and speed adjustment apply?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: When you share a lane with a bicycle, keep at least three feet between your vehicle and the rider and moderate your speed.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: Contrast the unit used for following cars ahead with the unit used for passing a bicycle?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: Following distance is counted in seconds behind the vehicle ahead, while bicycle clearance in a shared lane is a fixed three feet to the side.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Which two smooth habits help the driver behind you maintain a safe following gap?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: You help the driver behind you keep a safe gap by holding a steady speed and signaling early before you slow down or stop.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: If a driver tailgates you closely, how should you adjust speed and forward space — and why?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: If someone is tailgating you, slow down gradually and open more space ahead, so you can brake more gently and give the tailgater time to react.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: Why does adding space in front of your own hood protect you from a tailgater behind your trunk?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: A tailgater is handled by slowing gradually and adding space ahead of you, which lets you brake more gently when you must stop.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: When multi-lane traffic makes it safe, what simple move encourages a tailgater to go around you?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: When it is safe, changing to another lane encourages a tailgater to go around you.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: Whose safety rides directly on your smoothness whenever you have to stop unexpectedly?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: What you do affects the driver behind you, especially when you have to stop suddenly.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: Where do vehicle blind spots sit, and why don't mirrors eliminate them?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: Blind spots are the areas at the left and right sides of your vehicle that your mirrors do not show.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: How should you proceed when parked cars, bushes, trees, or buildings block your corner view?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: When cars parked near an intersection or bushes, trees or buildings block your view, creep forward slowly until you can see clearly, then go when the way is clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: How do you stay out of neighboring drivers' blind spots — and which narrow two-wheeler needs special care?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Stay out of other drivers' blind spots, watching for motorcycles too, by speeding up or dropping back rather than lingering beside them.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: What visibility goal applies to your own car, and why shouldn't you trust mirrors alone?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle, and do not trust your mirrors alone to show vehicles or motorcycles beside you.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: What physical check confirms the adjacent lane is clear right before you move over?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: Look over your shoulder to confirm the way is clear before changing lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Contrast the fix for your own blind spots with the fix for other drivers' blind spots?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: Your own blind spots are cleared with a shoulder check, while other drivers' blind spots are avoided by speeding up or dropping back.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: What two steps apply before pulling onto a street from a side road or private drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: When entering the road from a side road or a private drive, stop and wait until traffic clears.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: Why shouldn't you pull out in front of an approaching car or motorcycle just because its turn signal is blinking?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Do not assume a vehicle or motorcycle with its turn signal on will really turn; wait until you see the driver commit to the turn before you pull out.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: When waiting to exit a private drive, does an approaching car's turn signal count as a safe gap?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Entering from a private drive means stopping and waiting for a clear gap, and another driver's blinking signal does not create that gap.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Which five everyday changes of direction call for your turn signals?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Use your turn signals whenever you change direction, such as moving to another lane, turning at an intersection, merging onto a freeway, leaving a curb or pulling off the road.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: Why should you signal out of habit even when the street looks completely deserted?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Signal out of habit even when no one else seems to be around, because the vehicle or motorcycle you have not noticed poses the greatest danger.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: What does communicating on the road mean for other drivers and pedestrians?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: Communicating means showing other drivers and pedestrians what you intend to do early enough to prevent a collision.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: At least how many feet — and roughly how many seconds — before a turn must you signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: Signal at least one hundred feet, roughly four seconds, before you turn so others have time to react.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: Roughly how many seconds of travel does Arizona's one-hundred-foot turn-signal rule represent?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: The turn-signal distance is one hundred feet, which the manual puts at about four seconds of driving.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: Which two geometric requirements and what signaling distance does Arizona law set for turns?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: The law sets the lanes and positions you must use for turns and requires a signal at least one hundred feet before you turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: If your driveway or alley sits just beyond an intersection, when should you turn on your signal — and why?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: If your turn comes just past an intersection, wait until you are inside the intersection to signal, because drivers there could pull into your path.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: Which specific turn location flips the normal 'signal well ahead' rule so you wait until mid-intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: For a turn just past an intersection you hold the signal until you are inside the intersection, the opposite of the usual rule to signal well ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: What quick instrument check belongs after every completed lane change or gentle turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: After you finish your move, make sure the turn signal has gone off.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: What does a turn signal give nearby drivers — and what legal right does it NEVER grant you?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: A signal warns others of your move and gives them time to react, but it does not give you the right-of-way.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: Which combinations of electric lights and arm positions may you use to indicate a turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: You may show a turn with your turn signals, with hand signals, or with both.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: From driveways and alleys to curbs and freeways, list the six moves that always require signaling?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: Always signal before changing lanes, turning at an intersection or into a driveway or alley, entering or leaving a freeway, pulling away from the curb, or pulling over to the side of the road.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: When relying on hand signals, what additional non-turning action must you signal beforehand?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.expected_back: When you are using hand signals, also signal before you slow down or stop suddenly.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: Which situation appears on the hand-signal requirement list that electric turn blinkers don't handle?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: Hand signals add one case the turn-signal list does not: signaling before you slow down or stop suddenly.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.front: How do you normally overtake a vehicle or motorcycle traveling in your direction?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.expected_back: To pass a vehicle or motorcycle going your way, signal the lane change and pass on the left.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.front: What must you verify about time, space, and oncoming traffic before pulling out to pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.expected_back: Before passing, be sure you have the time and room to get completely ahead of the other vehicle without endangering oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.front: What mirror sight — paired with a shoulder check and blinker — tells you to return right after passing?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.expected_back: Return to the right lane once you can see the whole front, or both headlights, of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, after a shoulder check and a signal.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: Pinpoint the exact rearview-mirror landmark that confirms safe clearance ahead of a passed vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: The cue for returning to the right lane is seeing the whole front or both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.front: Do your signaling, clearance, and mirror-return steps change when overtaking slow motorcycles, bicycles, or mopeds?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.expected_back: The same passing steps apply when you pass slow-moving motorcycles, bicycles and mopeds.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.front: When a driver behind you honks or flashes lights to pass, how must you respond with lane position and speed?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.expected_back: If a vehicle behind you honks or flashes its lights to pass, move right when it is safe and let it by, and never speed up while you are being passed.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.front: What pedal response is strictly forbidden whenever another vehicle is overtaking you?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.expected_back: Being passed calls for moving right when it is safe and letting the other vehicle by; speeding up while being passed is never allowed.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.front: In which three situations is passing on the right allowed — and which two moves around pavement or left-turners are banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.expected_back: Passing on the right is permitted only when safe and either the driver ahead is turning left, you are on an open highway clearly marked for two or more lanes in your direction, or you are in a business or residential district marked for two or more lanes in your direction; never leave the paved or main roadway to pass on the right, and never pass to the left of a driver signaling a left turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.front: How many clearly marked lanes in your direction allow passing on the right on an open highway?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.expected_back: Passing on the right is also allowed on an open highway clearly marked for two or more lanes moving in your direction.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: Contrast Arizona's default passing side against what passing on the right requires?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: Normal passing is on the left; passing on the right needs both safety and a listed condition such as a driver ahead who is turning left.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Is it ever legal to pass another vehicle on the right by driving off the paved or main roadway?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: You may never pass on the right by leaving the paved or main part of the roadway.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Which two center or dividing line patterns forbid crossing to pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Passing is forbidden where your lane is bordered by a double solid line or by a solid dividing line on your side.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: When does approaching a curve or hilltop forbid passing even without reading paint?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Do not pass when approaching a curve or a hilltop where you cannot see far enough ahead to know passing is safe.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: Does a blind curve or hilltop ban passing on its own even if lane paint is faded or absent?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: A solid line on your side forbids passing, and a curve or hilltop that hides the road ahead forbids it too; the manual lists them as separate conditions.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: Within how many feet of a street intersection or railroad crossing is passing illegal?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Do not pass within one hundred feet of a street crossing or within one hundred feet of a railroad crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: Within how many feet of a view-blocking bridge, tunnel, or underpass is passing forbidden?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Do not pass within one hundred feet of a bridge, tunnel or underpass that blocks your view.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: What single distance unites Arizona's no-passing rule for intersections, rail tracks, and view-blocking bridges or tunnels?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: Street crossings, railroad crossings and view-blocking bridges, tunnels or underpasses all share one no-passing distance of one hundred feet.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: How does traffic flow through a roundabout intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: A roundabout is a circular intersection where traffic moves almost nonstop in one direction around a central island.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: To which side of the central island must you always steer when entering a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Always enter a roundabout to the right of its central island.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: Who always holds priority in the crosswalks approaching or leaving a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: At a roundabout, always yield to pedestrians and bicyclists who are crossing the road.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: Besides cars already inside the circle, which arriving vehicles must you also yield to at a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: Drivers arriving at a roundabout must yield to every vehicle already circulating and to large vehicles entering at the same moment.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: Combine all three groups that earn your yield as you arrive at a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Entering a roundabout you yield to circulating traffic and to large vehicles arriving with you, and pedestrians and bicyclists crossing the road are always yielded to as well.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: Between an approaching car at the yield line and a vehicle already inside the roundabout, who has right-of-way?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: Vehicles already in the roundabout have the right-of-way.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: What three planning and lane-selection steps happen as you approach a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Know where you want to go as you approach a roundabout, follow the signs, and move into the appropriate lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: For what miles-per-hour speed band are roundabouts engineered?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: Slow down on approach, because roundabouts are designed for speeds of fifteen to twenty miles per hour

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: Once a safe gap lets you enter a roundabout, what stopping rule and lane guide apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: Enter only when there is a gap, do not stop once you are inside, and follow signs or pavement markings for which lane to use.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: Pair the fifteen-to-twenty approach speed with what you do once rolling inside the roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: The roundabout design speed of fifteen to twenty miles per hour is an approach speed, and once inside you keep moving rather than stopping.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: What simple, safe fix applies if you miss your intended street inside a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: You may leave a roundabout at any street, and if you miss your exit you can simply go around again.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: What two rules protect your car around large trucks entering or circling a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Yield to large trucks entering a roundabout and do not try to pass them inside it.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already inside a roundabout, what should you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: If you see an emergency vehicle while in a roundabout, proceed carefully and exit if you can, or else pull over to the right.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: In a roundabout emergency-vehicle encounter, which choice comes first and which is the backup?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: An emergency vehicle in a roundabout calls for proceeding with caution and exiting if you can, and only otherwise pulling over to the right.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: How should pedestrians cross at a roundabout, and which two options do bicyclists have?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Pedestrians at roundabouts should use the crosswalks with caution, and bicyclists should either follow the traffic rules or walk the bike across in the crosswalks.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: Can you complete a U-turn using a roundabout, and what three-step approach leads into it?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Coming up to a roundabout, slow down and yield until a safe gap opens, then enter and finish your turn or U-turn.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: Where in Arizona road networks are diverging diamond interchanges used?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: A diverging diamond interchange is a newer design now used at some Arizona freeway interchanges.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: What unusual lane shift happens to cross-street traffic inside a diverging diamond interchange, and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: In a diverging diamond, traffic on the cross street above or below the freeway briefly moves over to the left side of the road to improve flow and safety.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: Which three standard road guides steer you cleanly through a diverging diamond?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: You drive through a diverging diamond the same way as other interchanges, by following its traffic signals, signs and pavement markings.
