sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Why doesn't driving briefly on the left inside a diverging diamond require special new maneuvers?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: The diverging diamond is the design in which cross-street traffic briefly drives on the left side of the road, yet drivers get through it simply by following its signals, signs and markings.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: At what exact traffic control feature do the right-to-left and left-to-right crossovers happen in a diverging diamond?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: The crossover points, where cross-street traffic moves from the right side to the left side of the road and back, happen at the signals.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: What missing signal phase makes traffic lights simpler inside a diverging diamond?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: Signals in a diverging diamond are simpler because no green-light time has to be set aside for left turns from the cross street onto the on-ramps.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: Once past the crossover in a diverging diamond, how do drivers turn left onto freeway on-ramps?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: In a diverging diamond, left turns onto the on-ramps are made from free-flowing lanes after the crossover.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: Connect where traffic swaps sides in a diverging diamond with how on-ramp left turns work afterward?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: In a diverging diamond, traffic switches sides at the signals, and the left turns onto the on-ramps then flow freely without their own green light.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: Which three problems — involving traffic, sightlines, and legality — must you avoid when parking on a public road?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: When parking on a public road, make sure you are not blocking traffic, not blocking anyone's view and not in a zone where parking is illegal.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: Where does the international symbol of access appear, and what spaces does it reserve?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: The international symbol of access, shown on reserved parking signs, placards and license plates, identifies parking for persons with disabilities.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: May you park in an accessible stall using a valid family placard when the person it belongs to stayed home?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: An accessible space needs both a valid placard or plate and the person it was issued to on board; the placard alone is not enough.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: What legal consequence hits anyone who parks unlawfully in a reserved accessible space?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: Anyone else who parks in an accessible space is breaking the law and may be fined.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: What fundamental visibility limitation makes backing up a dangerous maneuver?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: Backing up is dangerous because it is hard to see what is behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: What physical check belongs before climbing into the driver's seat to back out — and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: Check behind the car before getting in, since children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: Where must you physically turn and look while backing — instead of relying on mirrors or cameras?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: To back up, turn around and look straight out the rear window rather than depending on mirrors or a backup camera.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.front: Put Arizona's pre-entry check and in-seat gaze together for safe reversing?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.expected_back: Backing safely means checking behind the car before getting in and then turning to look through the rear window, not relying on a camera or mirrors.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: At what pace should you always move a vehicle in reverse?

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: What traffic check continues throughout parallel parking, and which two skills are the key to nailing it?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: Keep checking for oncoming traffic while parallel parking; judging distance while controlling your speed is the key to the maneuver.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: What two actions kick off step one of parallel parking before you stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: The first step of parallel parking is to check traffic behind you and signal that you are stopping.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: How do you align your rear bumper and side gap beside the forward car before backing in?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: Stop beside the forward car with your back bumper even with its back bumper, about two feet away from it.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: In which direction is Arizona's 'about two feet' parallel-parking setup distance measured?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: The gap to leave beside the forward car before backing into a parallel space is about two feet, measured side to side.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: Once in reverse looking over your right shoulder, which way do you turn the steering wheel first?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: Shift into reverse and, looking over your right shoulder, back slowly while turning the wheel sharply to the right.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.front: At what exact clearance point while parallel parking do you swing the wheel sharply left?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.expected_back: Once your front bumper clears the forward car's rear bumper, turn the wheel sharply left and keep backing until you are parallel to the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: Keep the two sharp steering turns of parallel parking in the right sequence?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: In parallel parking you turn the wheel sharply right first while backing, then sharply left once your front bumper clears the forward car.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.front: Which two final touches finish a clean parallel-parking maneuver?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.expected_back: Finish parallel parking by straightening the wheels and pulling forward slowly.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.front: Which way do your front wheels point — and what brake step applies — when parked downhill beside a curb?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.expected_back: Parked facing downhill with a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.front: How do you turn and rest your front wheels before setting the brake when parked uphill beside a curb?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.expected_back: Parked facing uphill with a curb, turn the wheels to the left and let the car roll back until the right front wheel rests against the curb, then set the parking brake.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.front: Uphill or downhill on a road with NO curb, which direction must your front wheels point — and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.expected_back: Where there is no curb, point the wheels to the right, so a car whose brakes failed would roll away from the middle of the road.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: Compare front-wheel direction across all three hill cases — downhill curb, uphill curb, and curbless?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.memory_hook: Only uphill with curb goes left
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Downhill with a curb the wheels turn toward the curb, uphill with a curb they turn to the left, and with no curb they turn to the right.

sec07-card-sec07-F42.front: Regardless of wheel angle or slope direction, what step applies every time you park on a grade?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.expected_back: Whatever the slope, always set the parking brake.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: How should you handle a pedestrian-activated crosswalk beacon when all of its lights are dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: At a pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal with all lights dark, you may proceed with caution if the crosswalk is clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Why can someone walking at night, dusk, dawn, or in storms spot an approaching car long before its driver sees them?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: When you are the pedestrian, you can often see an approaching vehicle more easily than its driver can see you, especially at night, at dusk and dawn, and in bad weather.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: What dangerous assumption must a pedestrian never make when a vehicle is approaching?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: As a pedestrian, never assume an approaching vehicle has seen you and will yield.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: Which two roadway locations should pedestrians choose when crossing a street?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Pedestrians should use crosswalks where they exist or cross at an intersection.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: What visual connection should a pedestrian try to establish with approaching drivers before crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Whenever possible, a pedestrian should make eye contact with the drivers of approaching vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Why must a pedestrian still look both ways before stepping into a marked crosswalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Look before stepping into the road, because even at a crosswalk drivers need time to notice you and react.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: Which three personal electronics should pedestrians put away or uncover while crossing streets?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Pedestrians should avoid distractions such as phones, headphones or earbuds while crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: What lighting choice and legal duty keep pedestrians safer when crossing streets at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: At night, cross in a well-lit spot, and always follow the traffic rules, signs and signals where you cross.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: Where must you bring your vehicle to a stop when pulling out of a driveway or alley?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: When you drive out of an alley or driveway onto the road, you must stop before reaching the sidewalk.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: Once you have stopped before the sidewalk at a driveway or alley, whom must you yield to next?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: After stopping at the sidewalk, yield to pedestrians and to approaching vehicles before entering the road.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: How does pulling out of an alley or driveway differ from making a left turn on the road?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: Leaving an alley or driveway you stop before the sidewalk and then yield, while turning left you yield to oncoming vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: Which three oncoming or crossing road users hold priority over a driver turning left?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: When turning left, you must yield to any oncoming vehicle, bicycle or pedestrian.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: What three conditions must all be met before making a U-turn in Arizona?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: A U-turn is allowed when you can make it safely, it will not get in the way of other traffic, and no sign forbids it.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: Which three factors each make a U-turn illegal on an Arizona roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: A U-turn is legal unless a sign bans it, it cannot be made safely, or it would interfere with other traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: How must you handle approaching traffic when completing an allowed U-turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: When making a U-turn, yield to approaching traffic and turn only when it is safe.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: Which court program might a civil red-light ticket let you attend, and where are your options listed?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: A citation for running a red light or another civil traffic violation may make you eligible for the Arizona Supreme Court's Defensive Driving Program, so read the papers that come with the citation.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: After receiving a civil traffic or red-light citation, how do you find out if Defensive Driving applies?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: A red-light or other civil traffic citation may make you eligible for the Defensive Driving Program, and the options are explained in the papers that come with the citation.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Which mandatory course must you complete if convicted of running a steady red or flashing red signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: A conviction for running a red light or a flashing red light means you must attend Traffic Survival School.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: What happens once you successfully complete Traffic Survival School for a red-light conviction?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: MVD is told when you finish Traffic Survival School successfully, and no further court appearance is then required.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: Does MVD have discretion to waive Traffic Survival School when a court reports a red-light conviction?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: By law, MVD must order Traffic Survival School for every red-light conviction the courts report.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Which agency orders Traffic Survival School after a red-light conviction, and what happens if you ignore it?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Traffic Survival School is ordered by MVD after a red-light conviction, and skipping it ends in an indefinite suspension.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: Alongside mandatory school, what does a red-light conviction place on your Arizona driving record?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: A red-light conviction also adds points, which appear on your driver record.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: Legally, what does simply mailing in or paying a red-light fine count as?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Paying the fine means accepting responsibility for the violation, and it is reported to MVD as a conviction.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: Why doesn't paying a red-light fine quietly keep the ticket off your MVD record?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: Paying a red-light fine is not a quiet way out: it is reported to MVD as a conviction and points go on the record.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: What happens to your driving privilege if you fail to finish ordered Traffic Survival School?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Not completing Traffic Survival School leads to an indefinite suspension of your driving privilege.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: How do maximum fines and license suspensions escalate between a life-threatening injury red-light crash and a fatal one?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.memory_hook: Injury five-hundred three-months; death thousand six
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: A red-light crash with life-threatening injuries carries up to five hundred dollars and three months of suspension, while a crash causing death carries up to one thousand dollars and six months.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: What three penalties can follow causing a crash that kills another driver or passenger?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: If you cause a crash in which another driver or passenger dies, you may be fined up to one thousand dollars, have your driving privilege suspended for six months and be ordered to do community service.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: At which roadway locations must you stay sharpest for approaching emergency vehicles?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: Stay alert for emergency vehicles, especially at intersections.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: What three steps must you take on an ordinary road when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: When a police car, fire engine, ambulance or other emergency vehicle approaches with a siren, lights or other warning device, yield, move to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: On a four-lane highway with two or more lanes in the emergency vehicle's direction, how do you yield?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: On a four-lane highway with at least two lanes going the same way as the emergency vehicle, proceed with due caution and yield by moving into a lane that is not next to its lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: What must you do on that multi-lane highway if changing out of the adjacent lane is unsafe or blocked?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: If that lane change is impossible or unsafe, proceed with due caution and reduce your speed.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: How does yielding to an approaching emergency vehicle differ between an ordinary street and a four-lane same-way highway?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.memory_hook: Street pulls right; highway shifts lanes
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: With an approaching emergency vehicle on an ordinary road you pull right and stop, while on a four-lane highway with two lanes in its direction you move to a lane not next to it.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: What minimum following distance must you keep behind a fire truck answering an emergency?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: Keep at least five hundred feet behind a fire department vehicle that is responding to an emergency.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: What minimum following distance must you keep behind a police vehicle responding to an emergency?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: Keep at least three hundred feet behind a police vehicle that is responding to an emergency.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How does Arizona's required following distance behind a responding fire truck compare with a responding police car?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.memory_hook: Five hundred fire, three hundred police
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: The following distance behind an emergency fire department vehicle is five hundred feet, while behind an emergency police vehicle it is three hundred feet.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: What restriction applies to the street block where an emergency vehicle has stopped to work an incident?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: Do not drive into or park in the block where an emergency vehicle has stopped to respond to an emergency.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: What primary action does Arizona's Move-Over law require when passing any stopped roadside vehicle with flashing lights?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: The move-over law requires you to shift over one lane to leave a safe margin when you pass any vehicle with flashing lights stopped at the side of a road or highway.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.front: Under Arizona's Move-Over law, what must you do when traffic makes changing lanes impossible or unsafe?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.expected_back: If moving over is unsafe or impossible, you must slow down and use caution instead.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: Does Arizona's Move-Over law let you freely pick slowing down when an open lane is available?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.memory_hook: Move over first; slow if blocked
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Under the move-over law you change one lane away, and only if that is unsafe or impossible do you slow down and use caution instead.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.front: Which types of pulled-over vehicles with flashing lights are protected by Arizona's Move-Over law?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.expected_back: The move-over law covers every pulled-over vehicle with flashing lights, including emergency-response and police vehicles, tow trucks, highway maintenance vehicles and private vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Why don't you need to check whether flashing roadside lights are red, blue, or amber hazards before moving over?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: The move-over law is about driving past a vehicle that is already pulled over at the roadside with its flashing lights on, whatever kind of vehicle it is.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.front: On which Arizona roadways does the Move-Over law apply?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.expected_back: The move-over law applies on all freeways and other multi-lane highways and on city roads and streets.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.front: When must drivers yield right-of-way to vehicles traveling in a funeral procession?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.expected_back: You must yield to any vehicle in a funeral procession led by a funeral escort vehicle flashing a red or blue light.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.front: On an undivided roadway, which traffic directions must stop completely before reaching a loading or unloading school bus?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.expected_back: When you approach a school bus that is picking up or dropping off passengers, stop completely before reaching it, whichever direction you are traveling.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.front: What two visual devices show that a school bus is stopped to load or unload students?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.expected_back: A school bus loading or unloading passengers shows alternating flashing lights and an extended mechanical stop-sign arm.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.front: Once stopped for a school bus, what must happen before you may start moving again?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.expected_back: Stay stopped until the school bus moves on or until its stop-sign arm and flashing lights are withdrawn.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: Which two events legally release waiting traffic at a stopped school bus?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: A stopped school bus is released when it moves on or when both its stop-sign arm and flashing lights are put away.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.front: Why must you scan carefully around both the front and rear of a stopped school bus?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.expected_back: Watch for children crossing in front of or behind a stopped school bus, since a child may dart out from either end.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.front: When are you excused from stopping for a loading school bus?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.expected_back: On a divided roadway you do not have to stop for a school bus when you are traveling in the opposite direction.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.front: What separates a truly divided roadway under Arizona's school-bus law, and what never counts?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.expected_back: A divided roadway is separated by a physical barrier such as a fence, curbing or a gap in the pavement; painted striping alone does not count.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: If only painted yellow lines or a painted flush median separate you from an oncoming school bus, must you stop?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: Oncoming drivers may pass a loading school bus only on a roadway divided by a physical barrier; painted lines alone leave everyone required to stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F41.front: On a physically divided highway, how does the rule differ for a bus across the barrier versus on your side?
sec10-card-sec10-F41.expected_back: On a divided roadway you may proceed with caution past a school bus in the approaching lanes, but not past one stopped on your side of traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F42.front: What two ongoing duties govern your speed on every Arizona trip?
sec10-card-sec10-F42.expected_back: Every speed regulation must be obeyed, and you should be prepared to change your speed quickly when needed.

sec19-card-sec19-F01.front: What happens to your Arizona driving privilege after any homicide or aggravated assault involving a vehicle?
sec19-card-sec19-F01.expected_back: Any homicide or aggravated assault involving the use of a vehicle leads to revocation of your driving privilege.

sec19-card-sec19-F02.front: What licensing penalty follows committing any felony that involves using a motor vehicle?
sec19-card-sec19-F02.expected_back: Any felony committed with the use of a vehicle leads to revocation.

sec19-card-sec19-F03.front: What happens to your driving privilege if you lie under oath about vehicle ownership or operation?
sec19-card-sec19-F03.expected_back: Lying under oath about who owns or operates a vehicle leads to revocation.

sec19-card-sec19-F04.front: What licensing action hits a driver who fails to stop and render aid at a crash they were involved in?
sec19-card-sec19-F04.expected_back: Failing to stop and give aid at the scene of a traffic crash you are involved in leads to revocation.

sec19-card-sec19-F05.front: What happens to your driving privilege upon accumulating two or more DUI convictions?
sec19-card-sec19-F05.expected_back: Having two or more DUI convictions leads to revocation.

sec19-card-sec19-F06.front: What happens to your Arizona driving privilege upon a single aggravated DUI conviction?
sec19-card-sec19-F06.expected_back: An aggravated DUI conviction leads to revocation.

sec19-card-sec19-F07.front: What licensing consequence follows causing death or serious physical injury through the use of a vehicle?
sec19-card-sec19-F07.expected_back: Causing a death or serious physical injury by using a vehicle leads to revocation.

sec19-card-sec19-R01.front: How do two or more DUI convictions differ in licensing outcome from two or more reckless driving or racing convictions?
sec19-card-sec19-R01.expected_back: Two or more DUI convictions bring revocation, while two or more reckless driving or racing convictions bring suspension.

sec19-card-sec19-F09.front: What can happen to your driving privilege if MVD orders a driving retest and you fail to take and pass it?
sec19-card-sec19-F09.expected_back: Your privilege may also be revoked if you do not take and pass a driving retest that you were required to take.

sec19-card-sec19-F10.front: What licensing action may apply if someone is found medically, psychologically, or physically unable to operate a vehicle?
sec19-card-sec19-F10.expected_back: Your privilege may be revoked if you are found medically, psychologically or physically unable to operate a motor vehicle.

sec19-card-sec19-F11.front: What may happen if your continued driving would endanger public health, safety, or welfare?
sec19-card-sec19-F11.expected_back: Your privilege may be revoked if your continued driving would endanger public health, safety or welfare.

sec19-card-sec19-F08.front: What happens to your driving privilege after two or more convictions for reckless driving or highway racing?
sec19-card-sec19-F08.expected_back: Two or more convictions for reckless driving, or two or more for racing on the highways, lead to suspension of your driving privilege.

sec19-card-sec19-F15.front: How does Arizona define a license suspension, and what two triggers bring it about?
sec19-card-sec19-F15.expected_back: Suspension is the temporary removal of your driving privilege, taken after a review of your driving record or when the law requires it.

sec19-card-sec19-R02.front: When repeat reckless driving or highway racing suspends your privilege, is that removal permanent or temporary?
sec19-card-sec19-R02.expected_back: Repeat reckless driving or racing convictions bring a suspension, which is only a temporary removal of the privilege.

sec19-card-sec19-F16.front: Which two fees must you pay to get your license back after an Arizona suspension?
sec19-card-sec19-F16.expected_back: After a suspension you pay the reinstatement fee plus the license application fee for your age group.

sec19-card-sec19-F12.front: What must happen to the vehicle when someone drives while their privilege is suspended or revoked for any reason?
sec19-card-sec19-F12.expected_back: A vehicle must be impounded or immobilized when the driver's privilege is suspended or revoked for any reason.

sec19-card-sec19-F13.front: When does driving without ever holding an Arizona license or permit trigger mandatory vehicle impoundment?
sec19-card-sec19-F13.expected_back: A vehicle must be impounded or immobilized when the driver has never held a valid license or permit and cannot show an out-of-state license.

sec19-card-sec19-F14.front: What happens to the vehicle if an interlock-restricted driver operates a car lacking a working certified interlock?
sec19-card-sec19-F14.expected_back: A vehicle must be impounded or immobilized when a driver who must use an ignition interlock device is driving without a working certified device.

sec19-card-sec19-F17.front: Which two outcomes on a moving traffic violation add points to your permanent Arizona driving record?
sec19-card-sec19-F17.expected_back: Every conviction or bail forfeiture for a moving traffic violation adds points to your permanent driving record.

sec19-card-sec19-F18.front: How many points accumulated within twelve months trigger mandatory Traffic Survival School or possible suspension?
sec19-card-sec19-F18.expected_back: If you build up eight or more points within any twelve-month period, you must attend Traffic Survival School, or your privilege may be suspended.

sec19-card-sec19-R03.front: What exact point total and rolling time window trigger Arizona's Traffic Survival School requirement?
sec19-card-sec19-R03.expected_back: The points threshold for Traffic Survival School is eight or more points, counted inside any twelve-month period.

sec19-card-sec19-F19.front: Which six impaired, reckless, racing, or aggressive offenses each drop eight points onto your record at once?
sec19-card-sec19-F19.expected_back: DUI, extreme DUI, aggravated DUI, reckless driving, racing on highways and aggressive driving each carry eight points.

sec19-card-sec19-F20.front: How many points does leaving the scene of a crash add to your Arizona driving record?
sec19-card-sec19-F20.expected_back: Leaving the scene of a crash carries six points.

sec19-card-sec19-F21.front: How many points apply when failing to stop for a sign or signal—or failing to yield—causes a death?
sec19-card-sec19-F21.expected_back: Failing to stop for a signal or stop sign, or failing to yield the right-of-way, carries six points when it causes a death.

sec19-card-sec19-F22.front: How many points apply when failing to stop for a sign or signal—or failing to yield—causes serious injury?
sec19-card-sec19-F22.expected_back: Failing to stop for a signal or stop sign, or failing to yield the right-of-way, carries four points when it causes serious injury.

sec19-card-sec19-R04.front: Which crash-related offenses carry six points in Arizona compared with four points?
sec19-card-sec19-R04.expected_back: Leaving the scene of a crash and a failure to stop or yield that causes death each carry six points, while the same failure causing serious injury carries four points.

sec19-card-sec19-F23.front: How many points does a speeding conviction add to your Arizona driving record?
sec19-card-sec19-F23.expected_back: A speeding violation carries three points.

sec19-card-sec19-F24.front: How many points come from driving across or parking inside a highway gore area?
sec19-card-sec19-F24.expected_back: Driving over or parking in a gore area carries three points.

sec19-card-sec19-F25.front: How many points do wrong-way driving and all other unlisted moving violations carry?
sec19-card-sec19-F25.expected_back: Wrong-way driving carries two points, the same as every other moving violation not listed separately.

sec19-card-sec19-R05.front: Which violations sit on Arizona's three-point shelf versus the baseline two-point shelf?
sec19-card-sec19-R05.expected_back: Speeding and gore-area violations each carry three points, while wrong-way driving and all other moving violations carry two points.

sec19-card-sec19-F26.front: Even without reaching eight points, what extra requirement follows a conviction for running a steady or flashing red light?
sec19-card-sec19-F26.expected_back: A conviction for running a red light or a flashing red light makes TSS mandatory on top of all court fines and fees.

sec19-card-sec19-F27.front: What three options can MVD take if frequent serious traffic convictions show disregard for others' safety?
sec19-card-sec19-F27.expected_back: MVD may suspend or revoke your privilege, or require TSS, if you are convicted of frequent serious traffic offenses that show disregard for the safety of others.

sec19-card-sec19-F28.front: Can MVD take license action for a single reckless-driving conviction or repeat negligent driving?
sec19-card-sec19-F28.expected_back: MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of reckless driving or are a repeat reckless or negligent driver.

sec19-card-sec19-F29.front: What happens if you commit—or let someone else commit—unlawful or fraudulent use of your driver license?
sec19-card-sec19-F29.expected_back: MVD may act against your license if you commit or allow an unlawful or fraudulent use of your driver license.

sec19-card-sec19-F30.front: Alongside alcohol and drugs, conviction for driving under the influence of what third substance triggers MVD action?
sec19-card-sec19-F30.expected_back: MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol, drugs or toxic vapors.

sec19-card-sec19-F31.front: How long is your license suspended for a first chemical-test refusal versus a repeat refusal within seven years?
sec19-card-sec19-F31.expected_back: Refusing or failing to complete a chemical test for alcohol or drug content brings a twelve-month suspension, or two years for a second or later refusal within a seven-year period.

sec19-card-sec19-R06.front: How does a second chemical-test refusal within seven years change the suspension length from a first refusal?
sec19-card-sec19-R06.expected_back: A first chemical test refusal brings a twelve-month suspension, while a second or later refusal within seven years brings two years.

sec19-card-sec19-F32.front: Can an unresolved traffic or court judgment from another state affect your Arizona driver license?
sec19-card-sec19-F32.expected_back: MVD may act against your license if you have an unresolved judgment from another state.

sec19-card-sec19-F33.front: May MVD act against your license when you commit an offense that carries mandatory revocation upon conviction?
sec19-card-sec19-F33.expected_back: MVD may act against your license if you commit an offense that requires mandatory revocation upon conviction.

sec19-card-sec19-F34.front: Even outside a car, which three alcohol acts can trigger MVD license action for someone under twenty-one?
sec19-card-sec19-F34.expected_back: MVD may act against the license of a driver under twenty-one who is convicted of receiving, drinking or possessing alcohol.

sec19-card-sec19-F35.front: What can MVD do to the license of a driver under twenty-one convicted of any illegal drug violation?
sec19-card-sec19-F35.expected_back: MVD may act against the license of a driver under twenty-one who is convicted of any illegal drug violation.

sec19-card-sec19-F36.front: What can MVD do if medical evidence shows you are unsafe behind the wheel?
sec19-card-sec19-F36.expected_back: MVD may act against your license if you are medically unsafe to drive.

sec19-card-sec19-F37.front: Which three crash outcomes allow MVD license action if you are convicted as a driver in that collision?
sec19-card-sec19-F37.expected_back: MVD may act against your license if, as a driver, you are convicted in a crash that caused death, personal injury or serious property damage.

sec19-card-sec19-F38.front: What can happen to your privilege if you are convicted of violating a restriction printed on your license?
sec19-card-sec19-F38.expected_back: MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of violating a restriction on your license.

sec19-card-sec19-F39.front: What may MVD do if you fail to comply with a certified ignition interlock device order?
sec19-card-sec19-F39.expected_back: MVD may act against your license if you fail to comply with a certified ignition interlock device order.

sec19-card-sec19-F40.front: How many moving civil traffic convictions—or certain criminal traffic offenses—let MVD act against a driver under eighteen?
sec19-card-sec19-F40.expected_back: MVD may act against the license of a driver under eighteen who is convicted of a first moving civil traffic violation or certain criminal traffic offenses.

sec19-card-sec19-F41.front: What can MVD do if you are convicted of driving the wrong way on a controlled-access highway?
sec19-card-sec19-F41.expected_back: MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of wrong-way driving on a controlled-access highway.

sec19-card-sec19-R07.front: In what two separate places does wrong-way driving appear in Arizona's penalty rules?
sec19-card-sec19-R07.expected_back: Wrong-way driving appears both as a two-point violation and, on a controlled-access highway, as a ground for MVD action.

sec19-card-sec19-F42.front: After finishing a suspension or revocation term, what fee, review, and insurance filing can reinstatement involve?
sec19-card-sec19-F42.expected_back: After a suspension or revocation period, you must pay the application fee to reinstate, and you may face an investigation and have to file an SR-twenty-two Certificate of Insurance.

sec19-card-sec19-F43.front: For up to how many days may police impound your vehicle if you are cited for driving while suspended or revoked?
sec19-card-sec19-F43.expected_back: If you are cited for driving on a suspended or revoked license, police may impound your vehicle for up to thirty days.

sec19-card-sec19-F44.front: What limited credential might someone qualify for after a conviction for driving on a suspended or revoked license?
sec19-card-sec19-F44.expected_back: A person convicted of driving on a suspended or revoked license may be eligible for a restricted driver license.

sec19-card-sec19-R09.front: How does getting cited roadside for driving while suspended differ from what can follow a conviction?
sec19-card-sec19-R09.expected_back: Being cited for driving while suspended can mean an impound of up to thirty days, while being convicted of it can make you eligible for a restricted license.

sec19-card-sec19-F45.front: What three items get suspended—and for how long—after a first conviction for lacking proof of financial responsibility?
sec19-card-sec19-F45.expected_back: A first conviction for lacking or failing to show proof of current financial responsibility in the vehicle suspends the license, registration and plates for three months.

sec19-card-sec19-F46.front: How long are license, registration, and plates suspended for a second financial-responsibility conviction within thirty-six months?
sec19-card-sec19-F46.expected_back: A second financial responsibility violation within thirty-six months brings a six-month suspension of the license, registration and plates.

sec19-card-sec19-F47.front: What suspension hits your license, registration, and plates on a third or later insurance violation within thirty-six months?
sec19-card-sec19-F47.expected_back: A third or later financial responsibility violation within thirty-six months brings a one-year suspension of the license, registration and plates.

sec19-card-sec19-R08.front: How do Arizona's financial-responsibility suspensions escalate across first, second, and third offenses within thirty-six months?
sec19-card-sec19-R08.expected_back: Financial responsibility suspensions rise from three months for a first violation to six months and then one year for repeat violations within thirty-six months.

sec19-card-sec19-F48.front: What happens to your license if MVD is notified that you skipped court or left a criminal traffic charge unpaid?
sec19-card-sec19-F48.expected_back: Your license will be suspended if MVD is told that you missed a court appearance or did not pay a criminal traffic violation charge.

sec19-card-sec19-F49.front: What exact legal promise are you making when you sign a traffic citation?
sec19-card-sec19-F49.expected_back: Signing a traffic citation is your promise to appear in traffic court.

sec19-card-sec19-F50.front: Which three court-related failures can suspend the driving privilege of someone under eighteen?
sec19-card-sec19-F50.expected_back: A driver under eighteen may have the privilege suspended for missing court, not paying a fine or not following any court order.

sec19-card-sec19-R11.front: Beyond missing traffic court or skipping a fine, what broader court failure can suspend a driver under eighteen?
sec19-card-sec19-R11.expected_back: Drivers under eighteen can be suspended for failing any court order, not only for missing court or not paying a fine.

sec19-card-sec19-F51.front: What must MVD block when courts report delinquent traffic or boating fines or missed criminal traffic or boating cases?
sec19-card-sec19-F51.expected_back: Courts report people who are behind on traffic or boating fines, or who missed a criminal traffic or boating case, and MVD must then block renewal of any vehicle registration they own.

sec19-card-sec19-R10.front: How do missed criminal traffic cases and delinquent fines hit both your driver credential and your vehicle?
sec19-card-sec19-R10.expected_back: Missing court or not paying a criminal traffic charge suspends the license, while delinquent traffic fines also block vehicle registration renewal.

sec19-card-sec19-F52.front: What pressurized substance is someone under eighteen barred from obtaining using false identification?
sec19-card-sec19-F52.expected_back: A person under eighteen may not use false identification to get someone to sell, serve, give or furnish a nitrous oxide container.

sec22-card-sec22-F01.front: What two core duties explain why you must stay at the scene if you are involved in a crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F01.expected_back: If you are in a crash, stay at the scene to help anyone who is injured and to exchange information with the other drivers.

sec22-card-sec22-F02.front: Which five identification, policy, witness, and vehicle details should drivers share after a collision?
sec22-card-sec22-F02.expected_back: After a crash, share your driver license number, name and address, insurance company and policy number, any witness information and license plate numbers.

sec22-card-sec22-F03.front: What immediate action is mandatory whenever anyone is injured in a crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F03.expected_back: If anyone is injured in the crash, you must call the police immediately.

sec22-card-sec22-F04.front: If you are one of the first passersby arriving at a crash, where do you park and what lights go on?
sec22-card-sec22-F04.expected_back: When you arrive early at a crash scene, park well off the roadway and switch on your hazard flashers.

sec22-card-sec22-F05.front: What fire-safety step should be taken with the ignition switches of wrecked vehicles at a crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F05.expected_back: At a crash scene, turn off the ignition of the vehicles involved.

sec22-card-sec22-F06.front: Which emergency number alerts dispatchers and emergency officials at a crash scene?
sec22-card-sec22-F06.expected_back: At a crash scene, call nine one one to notify emergency officials.

sec22-card-sec22-F07.front: Where must you never stand or walk while dealing with a crash scene?
sec22-card-sec22-F07.expected_back: At a crash scene, do not stand or walk in the traffic lanes.

sec22-card-sec22-F08.front: How can other bystanders who have pulled over at a crash scene help prevent a pileup?
sec22-card-sec22-F08.expected_back: At a crash scene, ask others who have stopped to warn approaching traffic.

sec22-card-sec22-R03.front: How does the manual pair an involved driver's injury duty with an early-arriving bystander's scene role?
sec22-card-sec22-R03.expected_back: A driver in a crash calls the police immediately when someone is injured, while a bystander arriving first calls nine one one and warns traffic through others.

sec22-card-sec22-F09.front: Under what injury condition must crashed vehicles be moved off the main traveled roadway?
sec22-card-sec22-F09.expected_back: When a crash causes no serious physical injury or death, the vehicles involved must be moved off the main traveled part of the roadway.

sec22-card-sec22-F10.front: Who is allowed to move a minor-crash vehicle off the road, and what three vehicle/safety conditions apply?
sec22-card-sec22-F10.expected_back: Any licensed driver may move a crashed vehicle if it can run under its own power without a tow and moving it will not cause more damage or more traffic hazards.

sec22-card-sec22-F11.front: Does moving your car off the roadway before police arrive make you legally at fault for the crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F11.expected_back: A person who moves a vehicle off the main roadway before police arrive is not held liable or at fault for the crash just because the vehicle was moved.

sec22-card-sec22-R02.front: Why shouldn't fear of legal blame keep you blocking traffic after a minor fender-bender?
sec22-card-sec22-R02.expected_back: Moving your car before police arrive is protected, since the move alone cannot make you liable or at fault for the crash.

sec22-card-sec22-F12.front: How soon should drivers relocate operable vehicles after an injury-free minor collision?
sec22-card-sec22-F12.expected_back: After a minor crash with no injuries, drivers should move operable vehicles out of the travel lanes as soon as it is safe.

sec22-card-sec22-F13.front: Is clearing a drivable car after a minor, injury-free Arizona crash optional advice or state law?
sec22-card-sec22-F13.expected_back: State law requires a driver in a minor, injury-free crash to remove the vehicle from the roadway if it can be driven and moved safely.

sec22-card-sec22-F14.front: Which three safety benefits come from moving minor-crash vehicles out of active travel lanes?
sec22-card-sec22-F14.expected_back: Getting out of the travel lanes gives you a safer place to check for damage, protects first responders and lowers the chance of a secondary crash.

sec22-card-sec22-R01.front: Putting injury, power, damage, and hazard rules together, when must crashed vehicles clear the main roadway?
sec22-card-sec22-R01.expected_back: When a crash involves no serious physical injury or death, vehicles must be removed from the main traveled roadway if they remain safely operable under their own power without needing towing and moving them will not cause further vehicle damage or increase traffic hazards.

sec22-card-sec22-F15.front: Right after any collision stops moving, what is your very first priority?
sec22-card-sec22-F15.expected_back: After any crash, your first step is to make sure that you and everyone in your vehicle are OK.

sec22-card-sec22-F16.front: If your car still runs after a highway collision, which three places can you move to before calling nine-one-one?
sec22-card-sec22-F16.expected_back: If your vehicle still runs after a crash, move to the emergency shoulder or median or exit the highway, then call nine one one.

sec22-card-sec22-F17.front: While waiting near a crash site, where do you position yourself and where should your attention stay?
sec22-card-sec22-F17.expected_back: After a crash, stay out of the travel lanes, stay alert and watch the approaching traffic.

sec22-card-sec22-F18.front: May an involved driver ever simply drive off and leave a crash scene?
sec22-card-sec22-F18.expected_back: Never leave the scene of a crash.

sec22-card-sec22-R04.front: How does pulling onto a shoulder, median, or exit ramp differ legally from leaving the crash scene?
sec22-card-sec22-R04.expected_back: Moving to the shoulder, median or an exit after a crash is expected, but leaving the crash scene altogether is never allowed.

sec22-card-sec22-F19.front: Which three crash outcomes legally require every involved driver to stop and remain at the scene?
sec22-card-sec22-F19.expected_back: A driver in a crash involving vehicle damage, injury or death is required by law to stop and remain at the scene.

sec22-card-sec22-F20.front: How must an involved driver fulfill the legal duty to render aid when someone is hurt?
sec22-card-sec22-F20.expected_back: At such a crash you must give aid to anyone injured, including calling nine one one to arrange medical treatment.

sec22-card-sec22-F21.front: Which three identification items must you give police and emergency responders at the crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F21.expected_back: At such a crash you must tell emergency responders and police your name, your address and your plate number.

sec22-card-sec22-F22.front: What license penalty follows a conviction for failing to stop at a crash that caused only vehicle damage?
sec22-card-sec22-F22.expected_back: A conviction for failing to stop at a crash that caused only vehicle damage suspends your driving privilege for one year.

sec22-card-sec22-F23.front: What license loss hits a driver who fails to stop at a crash involving non-serious bodily injury?
sec22-card-sec22-F23.expected_back: Failing to stop at a crash that caused an injury other than death or serious physical injury brings a three-year revocation.

sec22-card-sec22-F24.front: How long is your license revoked—and how does prison time count—for fleeing a serious-physical-injury crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F24.expected_back: Failing to stop at a crash that caused serious physical injury brings a five-year revocation, not counting any time spent incarcerated.

sec22-card-sec22-F25.front: How long is your license revoked—and how does incarceration count—for failing to stop at a fatal crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F25.expected_back: Failing to stop at a crash that caused a death brings a ten-year revocation, not counting any time spent incarcerated.

sec22-card-sec22-R05.front: How does failing to stop at a damage-only crash compare with failing to stop at a non-serious-injury crash?
sec22-card-sec22-R05.expected_back: Failing to stop at a damage-only crash brings a one-year suspension, while failing to stop at a crash with injury brings a three-year revocation.

sec22-card-sec22-R06.front: How do Arizona's revocations for fleeing a serious-injury crash versus a fatal crash compare—including prison time?
sec22-card-sec22-R06.expected_back: Failing to stop at a crash with serious physical injury brings a five-year revocation, while a crash with a death brings ten years, and neither counts time spent incarcerated.

sec22-card-sec22-F26.front: Which two national leadership groups approved the traffic-stop guidance in Arizona's manual?
sec22-card-sec22-F26.expected_back: The manual's traffic stop guidance was approved by national groups of motor vehicle administrators and law enforcement leaders.

sec22-card-sec22-F27.front: What legal threshold prompts a law-enforcement officer to pull a driver over?
sec22-card-sec22-F27.expected_back: An officer pulls a driver over when there is reasonable suspicion that a traffic or criminal law was broken.

sec22-card-sec22-F28.front: How should both you and your passengers behave as soon as police lights flash behind you?
sec22-card-sec22-F28.expected_back: When you see emergency lights behind you, you and your passengers should stay calm and cooperate.

sec22-card-sec22-F29.front: What signaling and positioning steps belong to pulling over for emergency lights?
sec22-card-sec22-F29.expected_back: When signaled to stop, use your turn signal and pull off or to the side of the road as soon as it is safe.

sec22-card-sec22-F30.front: Which two things inside your car should you turn off once parked for a traffic stop?
sec22-card-sec22-F30.expected_back: Once stopped, turn off the engine and any audio devices.

sec22-card-sec22-F31.front: During a routine traffic stop, when should you step out of your vehicle?
sec22-card-sec22-F31.expected_back: During a traffic stop, stay in your vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out.

sec22-card-sec22-F32.front: What cabin light should you switch on during a nighttime stop, and what cruiser light should you expect?
sec22-card-sec22-F32.expected_back: If you are pulled over at night, turn on your interior lights to help visibility, and expect the officer may use a spotlight.

sec22-card-sec22-F33.front: Where should your hands rest throughout a traffic stop?
sec22-card-sec22-F33.expected_back: Keep your hands on the steering wheel or somewhere the officer can easily see them.

sec22-card-sec22-F34.front: Whose roadside instructions apply to both you and every passenger in your car?
sec22-card-sec22-F34.expected_back: Follow every instruction the officer gives to you or your passengers.

sec22-card-sec22-F35.front: Because officers sometimes walk up on the passenger side, which window do you lower?
sec22-card-sec22-F35.expected_back: The officer may approach either side of the vehicle, so lower the window on that side to talk.

sec22-card-sec22-F36.front: At what exact point in a traffic stop should you inform the officer if a weapon is in the vehicle?
sec22-card-sec22-F36.expected_back: If there is a weapon in the vehicle, tell the officer at first contact.

sec22-card-sec22-F37.front: When should you reach into your pocket, purse, or glovebox for your license and registration?
sec22-card-sec22-F37.expected_back: Wait for the officer's instructions before reaching for your license or vehicle documents.

sec22-card-sec22-R07.front: How do weapon disclosure timing and reaching for documents pair together at a stop?
sec22-card-sec22-R07.expected_back: You keep your hands visible and wait for instructions before reaching, but you speak up right away if there is a weapon in the vehicle.

sec22-card-sec22-R08.front: What is the default rule on staying in your car, and what two rules apply if the officer asks you out?
sec22-card-sec22-R08.expected_back: During a stop you stay in the vehicle unless told to get out, and if told to get out you keep your hands visible and stand where directed.

sec22-card-sec22-F38.front: What will an officer normally explain, and which three documents will they ask to see?
sec22-card-sec22-F38.expected_back: The officer will typically explain the reason for the stop and ask for your license, proof of insurance and registration.

sec22-card-sec22-F39.front: What two-step courtesy applies if your registration or wallet is tucked out of immediate reach?
sec22-card-sec22-F39.expected_back: If your documents are out of reach, tell the officer where they are and wait for an acknowledgment before reaching for them.

sec22-card-sec22-F40.front: What must a non-uniformed officer display at a stop, and what may you ask if they haven't?
sec22-card-sec22-F40.expected_back: An officer who is not in uniform should show law enforcement credentials, and if not, you may ask to see them.

sec22-card-sec22-F41.front: If an officer instructs you to step out of the vehicle, how should you manage your hands and position?
sec22-card-sec22-F41.expected_back: If the officer asks you to get out, keep your hands visible and stand where the officer directs.

sec22-card-sec22-F42.front: Which three enforcement outcomes can conclude a stop, and what may you ask if the action isn't explained?
sec22-card-sec22-F42.expected_back: The officer may give a warning, write a ticket or make an arrest, will typically explain the action, and you may ask if it is not explained.

sec22-card-sec22-F43.front: If you think a ticket is wrong, why shouldn't you argue roadside and where do you contest it?
sec22-card-sec22-F43.expected_back: If you disagree with the officer, do not argue at the roadside, but contest the decision in court through the proper legal channels.

sec22-card-sec22-R10.front: Where does Arizona law resolve disagreements over an officer's traffic decision?
sec22-card-sec22-R10.expected_back: A disagreement with an officer is settled later in court, not by arguing during the stop.

sec22-card-sec22-F44.front: Does signing an Arizona traffic ticket admit guilt, and what happens if you refuse to sign?
sec22-card-sec22-F44.expected_back: Signing a traffic ticket is not an admission of guilt, but refusing to sign one may lead to your arrest.

sec22-card-sec22-R09.front: Contrast the legal effect of signing a traffic ticket with refusing to sign it at the roadside?
sec22-card-sec22-R09.expected_back: Signing a ticket is not an admission of guilt, while refusing to sign it may lead to arrest.

sec22-card-sec22-F45.front: Whom should you contact—and when—if you believe an officer acted inappropriately during a stop?
sec22-card-sec22-F45.expected_back: If you believe an officer acted inappropriately, contact the officer's agency and ask to speak to a supervisor, ideally soon after the stop.

sec22-card-sec22-R11.front: Where does a complaint about an officer's behavior go, and why act promptly?
sec22-card-sec22-R11.expected_back: A complaint about an officer's conduct goes to the officer's agency, where you can ask for a supervisor, ideally soon after the stop.

sec22-card-sec22-F46.front: Which five vehicle ownership, testing, and coverage topics are covered on the ADOT website?
sec22-card-sec22-F46.expected_back: The ADOT website offers information on titles and registration, temporary and resident registration, vehicle inspections, emissions testing and vehicle insurance.

sec22-card-sec22-F47.front: Which eight hydration, fire, medical, light, warmth, battery, warning, and tire items belong in an Arizona car kit?
sec22-card-sec22-F47.expected_back: Consider carrying an emergency kit with items such as drinking water, a fire extinguisher, a first aid kit, a flashlight, blankets, jumper cables, flares and a spare tire with a jack and lug wrench.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Which children by age must ride secured in a child passenger restraint system in Arizona?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Any child younger than eight riding in a vehicle in Arizona has to be properly secured in a child passenger restraint system.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: What specific crash injury are seat-back head restraints designed to reduce, and from which impact direction?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Head restraints on seat backs exist to lower the risk of a whiplash injury when you are hit from behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: Against which part of your head — and even with what feature — should an adjustable head restraint sit?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: An adjustable head restraint should sit against the back of your head, level with the middle of your ear.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: Why are 'top of the head' and 'base of the neck' wrong choices for setting a head restraint?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: A head restraint lines up with the middle of the ear and touches the back of the head; it is not set to the top of the head or left low at the neck.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: When must a motor vehicle's muffler operate, and which two problems does it prevent?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Every motor vehicle needs a muffler that works well and runs at all times, so it does not cause excessive pollution or unusual noise.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: Does Arizona law allow installing a muffler cutout, exhaust bypass, or similar device?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Fitting a muffler cut-out, a bypass or any similar device is illegal.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: Starting with which model year must motor vehicles carry an exhaust emissions system?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Motor vehicles of the nineteen sixty-seven model year or newer must have an exhaust emissions system to help cut air pollution.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: What must every motor-vehicle engine be equipped to keep from escaping into the air?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: The engine of every motor vehicle must be equipped so that excessive fumes and smoke cannot escape.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: Contrast what Arizona's muffler rule regulates against what its nineteen sixty-seven emissions rule requires?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: The muffler rule targets noise and pollution and bans bypass devices, while the emissions rule requires an exhaust emissions system on nineteen sixty-seven and newer models.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: What two condition requirements apply to every vehicle's windshield and wiper blades?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: A vehicle must have a windshield with no cracks, and its windshield wipers must work properly.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: When is window or windshield tint film legal in Arizona, and who should verify compliance?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Tint film on windows and windshields is legal only within certain limits, so owners should confirm the maker or installer follows Arizona law.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: Does the Arizona manual print exact tint percentages, or where does it place responsibility?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: The manual gives no tint numbers; it says only that tint is lawful within limits and puts the burden on the owner to check that the installer complied.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: When your vehicle's build or cargo blocks the rear view, what mirror is required and how far back must it show?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: If a vehicle's build or load blocks the driver's rear view, it needs at least one outside mirror on the driver side showing at least two hundred feet of highway behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: From at least how many feet away must your vehicle's horn be heard?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Your vehicle must have a working horn that can be heard from two hundred feet away.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: Which two Arizona equipment rules share the exact same two-hundred-foot benchmark?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: The required outside mirror must show two hundred feet of road behind, and the required horn must be audible at two hundred feet, so one distance covers both rules.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: Which vehicles are the only ones allowed to carry a siren, whistle, or bell?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: Emergency vehicles are the ones that may carry a siren, whistle or bell.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: May a broken-down civilian car show forward-facing flashing red lights — and which three fleets are exempt?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Flashing red lights on the front of a vehicle are banned, even on a disabled vehicle, except on authorized emergency vehicles, school buses and snow removal equipment.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: In which two stopped locations should an ordinary motorist switch on hazard warning lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Turn on your hazard warning lights whenever your vehicle is stopped on the roadway or on the shoulder.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: Contrast standard hazard warning flashers on a disabled car against forward-facing flashing red lights?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Hazard flashers are switched on when you are stopped on the roadway or shoulder, while flashing red lights facing forward are off-limits to ordinary vehicles even when they break down.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: What two things does defensive driving protect, and which two habits start it?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Driving defensively protects both your life and your driving record, and it starts with constant awareness of conditions and planning ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: Beyond awareness, what two action steps let a defensive driver avoid hitting obstacles or vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Defensive driving also means anticipating dangers and acting in time so that you never strike an obstacle or another vehicle.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: Even when nobody gets hurt in a crash, which five hassles and financial hits can still follow?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Even a crash with no injuries brings inconvenience and repair bills, and it can lead to a court appearance, fines and higher insurance rates.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: Which two attitudes toward fellow road users does the Arizona manual rank as the most important key to safety?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: The manual names courtesy and consideration for others as the most important driving attitudes and the key to safe driving.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Alongside courtesy, which two mental-focus habits must stay switched on behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Concentration and alertness also matter, so make keeping your mind on the road a habit.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: How does the manual's wording separate courtesy and consideration from concentration and alertness?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: Courtesy and consideration are ranked as the most important attitudes, while concentration and alertness are described as other important elements.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: How risky can driving while exhausted or emotionally upset become?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Driving while drowsy or emotionally upset can be as dangerous as driving impaired.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: How does the Arizona manual define foresight behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Foresight is the ability to size up a traffic situation quickly and be ready to take corrective action.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: How does foresight fit inside the broader concept of defensive driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Foresight is about sizing up a situation fast and being ready to correct, while defensive driving is the wider practice of awareness, planning, anticipation and right action.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: Regardless of years behind the wheel, which four mechanical, weather, and human hazards will every driver face?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: However many years you have driven, you will eventually meet equipment failures, bad weather, unskilled drivers and drivers who ignore the rules, and defensive driving is the best preparation.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Which four visual, mental, speed, and restraint habits form the manual's defensive checklist?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: The defensive habits the manual lists are keeping good vision ahead and around you, staying alert, obeying speed limits and knowing when to slow or stop, and always wearing your safety belt.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: Where do a defensive driver's eyes keep moving to catch developing hazards?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: A defensive driver keeps looking ahead and around, checks the mirrors constantly, and watches for hazards in front, at the sides and behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: Which three building blocks teach a beginner to drive — and who should coach if you skip formal driver ed?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: A beginner learns by instruction, observation and practice, and someone not in a driver training program should ask an experienced, skilled, licensed driver to help.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: Once your instruction permit is in hand, where should you practice starting, pulling out, and stopping?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.memory_hook: Quiet parking lot or open area
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: Once you hold an instruction permit, practice starting, pulling out of a parking space, stopping and controlling the vehicle in a parking lot or other open area with little traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: May a beginner practice behind the wheel in a public parking lot before getting an instruction permit?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: Beginner practice in an open lot comes after the instruction permit is issued, not before it.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: Which three traps — rather than lack of basic skill — trip up experienced drivers over time?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Experienced drivers often struggle with carelessness, overconfidence and bad habits that build up over time.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: Why is 'lack of basic skill' the wrong answer for what threatens experienced drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: The risk the manual names for experienced drivers is carelessness, overconfidence and old bad habits, not a lack of basic skill.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: As road laws evolve and traffic volume climbs, what quality determines how safe you stay?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: Driving rules and techniques have changed and traffic keeps growing, so how well you adapt decides how safe a driver you really are.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: What three-part rehearsed strategy defines a 'driving skill' in the Arizona manual?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: The manual defines a driving skill as a rehearsed strategy of anticipating, reacting and constantly adjusting the space between you and other vehicles.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: Which three changes show that a learner is genuinely progressing as a safe driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: Progress as a driver shows in dropping risk-taking, keeping to speed limits and being able to take corrective action when needed.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: Alongside phones and maps, which three everyday cabin tasks — including seat belts — belong off-limits while moving?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: Distractions to avoid at the wheel include reading a GPS or map, using a phone or texting, hunting for a dropped item, tending to children and buckling a safety belt.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.front: Why does 'fastening a safety belt' show up on Arizona's distraction list, and what is the fix?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.expected_back: Fastening a safety belt is on the distraction list only when it is done while driving, so the belt goes on before the vehicle moves.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: What must you do first whenever you need to handle a call or send or read a text?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: If you need to use a cell phone or send or read a text, first pull safely off the road and stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: Where should both of your hands stay while driving, and why?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: While you drive, both hands should be on the steering wheel so you keep full control.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: Which two physical ways of handling a wireless device while driving are illegal in Arizona?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: Arizona law forbids holding or supporting a wireless device while driving.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: Which two text actions and three video actions are strictly banned while driving in Arizona?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: While driving you may not write or read any text-based message, and you may not watch, record or broadcast video.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: What are the only wireless-device uses allowed while driving in Arizona?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: While driving, a driver may use a wireless device only to report an emergency or for hands-free or voice-to-text operation.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.front: Which two non-handheld ways of operating a wireless device stay lawful for Arizona drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.expected_back: Hands-free and voice-to-text use of a wireless device is permitted.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: Draw the exact line between what Arizona's wireless law bans and what it permits?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: Holding or supporting a device is what the law bans, while hands-free and voice-to-text operation stays allowed.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: When may you use a wireless device while moving versus having to pull off the road and stop?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: While driving, wireless device use is limited to reporting an emergency or hands-free or voice-to-text operation; otherwise you must pull safely off the road and stop before using a cell phone or texting.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.front: What gaze distance and steering touch keep your vehicle tracking smoothly inside its lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.expected_back: To stay in your lane, look well down the road and make only small steering corrections when needed.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.front: Because hands follow your eyes, where should you look while rounding a curve or turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.expected_back: Drivers tend to steer toward where they look, so in a curve or turn, looking toward the outside of your lane helps you stay in it.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.front: Contrast where your eyes focus on a straight stretch versus through a curve?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.expected_back: On a straight road you look well ahead and make slight corrections, while in a curve you look toward the outside of your lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.front: Which road users and animals may cross your path — and at which five busy places must scanning intensify?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.expected_back: Scan for cars, motorcycles, bicyclists, people and animals that may cross your path, especially at intersections, crosswalks, shopping centers, construction areas and playgrounds.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: Which two flying toys must children never launch near overhead light-rail power lines?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: Children should not fly kites or model airplanes near the overhead power lines used by light rail.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: What rule governs skateboarding, rollerblading, and bike riding on light-rail tracks or platforms?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: Skateboarding, rollerblading and bike riding on light rail tracks or station platforms is unsafe and not permitted.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: Which traffic laws bind bicyclists, and when do riders hold right-of-way?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: Bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws as drivers, and they get the right-of-way in the same situations that drivers do.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: Why do bicyclists require active scanning and extra caution from motorists?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: Bicyclists are often hard to see, so drivers must watch for them along the road and use extra caution.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: What minimum lateral gap must you leave when overtaking a same-direction bicyclist in Arizona?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: When passing a bicyclist who is going the same direction, a driver must leave a safe distance of at least three feet.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: Why shouldn't you blast your horn while overtaking a bicyclist?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: Honking at a bicyclist while you pass is unsafe because the sound may startle the rider and cause a crash.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: How should you adjust your headlights at night when approaching a bicyclist?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: At night, dim your headlights as a courtesy to bicyclists.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: For which four legal reasons might a bicyclist move away from the right curb toward the left?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: Be ready for a bicyclist to swerve, because a rider may legally move left to turn left, avoid a hazard, pass a pedestrian or vehicle, or when the lane is too narrow to share safely.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: Although cyclists usually ride near the right edge, when does Arizona law back moving left?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: Bicyclists normally ride with traffic near the right side, yet they may legally move left to turn left, avoid a hazard, pass, or when the lane is too narrow to share.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: Relative to motor vehicle lanes, in which direction must bicyclists always ride?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: Bicyclists must ride in the same direction as traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: What passenger limit applies to riding a bicycle on Arizona streets?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: A bicycle may not carry more people than it was designed to carry.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: What is the maximum number of bicyclists allowed to ride side by side?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: Bicyclists may not ride more than two abreast.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: Under normal conditions without hazards or turns, where on the roadway should a bicyclist ride?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: Bicyclists should ride as close to the right side of the road as is practicable.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: How should bicyclists communicate upcoming turns or stops to nearby traffic?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: Bicyclists should use proper hand signals.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: How does Arizona law treat riding a bicycle under the influence of alcohol or drugs?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: Riding a bicycle under the influence of drugs or alcohol is illegal.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: Which two lighting items are mandatory on a bicycle ridden at night, including visibility range?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: A bicycle ridden at night needs a white headlamp that can be seen from five hundred feet and a rear reflector.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: Beyond mandatory equipment, what rear accessory helps motorists spot a nighttime cyclist sooner?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: A flashing red light on the back of a bicycle can make the rider easier for drivers to see.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: In Arizona bicycle law, what do the three-foot and five-hundred-foot measurements each govern?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: The three feet figure is the minimum gap when passing a bicyclist, while the five hundred feet figure is how far away a bicycle's white night headlamp must be visible.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: How does the two-abreast bicycle rule differ from the bicycle passenger rule?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: The limit on riding two abreast is about how many bicycles ride side by side, while the passenger limit is about how many people one bicycle may carry.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: Which nighttime bicycle visibility items are required by law, and which rear light is optional?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: A white headlamp and a rear reflector are required on a bicycle at night, while a flashing red rear light is an optional way to be seen better.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: Between a car driver and a motorcyclist, who faces far higher odds of injury in a collision?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.expected_back: In a crash, a motorcyclist is more likely to be injured than the driver of a car.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: What driver mistake causes the majority of collisions between cars and motorcycles?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: Most crashes between cars and motorcycles happen when a car turns in front of a motorcycle, usually because the driver did not see it or misjudged its distance and speed.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: How does a motorcycle's compact size trick a motorist's eyes regarding distance and speed?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: A motorcycle's small size can make it hard to spot and can make it look farther away and slower than it really is.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.front: Why is judging a motorcycle's distance at night tougher than judging a car's?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.expected_back: A motorcycle's single headlight or taillight gives you fewer clues for judging its distance.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.front: Which two weather conditions noticeably reduce a motorcyclist's stability?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.expected_back: Motorcyclists are less stable in rain and wind.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.front: What maneuver does Arizona call lane filtering for motorcycles?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.expected_back: Lane filtering is when a motorcyclist safely passes a vehicle that is stopped in the same lane and direction.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.front: What minimum street layout is required before a motorcyclist may legally lane-filter?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.expected_back: Lane filtering is allowed only on a street with at least two adjacent lanes going the same direction.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.front: What is the highest posted road speed limit where motorcycle lane filtering is legal in Arizona?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.expected_back: Lane filtering is allowed only where the posted speed limit is no higher than forty-five miles per hour.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.front: How fast may a motorcyclist travel while actively lane-filtering past stopped cars?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.expected_back: While lane filtering, the motorcycle may not go faster than fifteen miles per hour.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: How do the forty-five and fifteen mile-per-hour caps divide Arizona's motorcycle lane-filtering law?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: For lane filtering, the posted limit may be no higher than forty-five miles per hour, while the motorcycle itself may go no faster than fifteen miles per hour.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: Which traffic state and lane-count requirement must both hold true for legal lane filtering?
