sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: Lane filtering means passing a vehicle stopped in the same lane, and it also needs at least two adjacent lanes going the same direction.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: How does the small-profile illusion directly trigger the most common car-and-motorcycle crash?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: A motorcycle tends to look farther away and slower than it really is, which is why drivers turning in front of motorcycles cause most car and motorcycle crashes.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.front: Where do car-and-motorcycle crashes cluster heavily, and why?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.expected_back: Intersections carry a high risk of car and motorcycle collisions, usually because a driver turns into the motorcycle's path.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.front: When a motorcyclist shifts toward one side of a lane, why shouldn't you assume a turn is next?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.expected_back: Do not assume what a rider intends, since a rider may move to one side to avoid a hazard or to be seen, not only to get ready to turn.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.front: Which three surface hazards can force a motorcyclist to swerve unexpectedly toward your lane?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.expected_back: Motorcyclists may shift within their lane to avoid oil, potholes or debris, so a motorcycle may come into your lane unexpectedly.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.front: Why must you confirm a motorcyclist is genuinely slowing to turn before pulling out in front of a blinking signal?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.expected_back: Motorcycle turn signals do not cancel themselves, so be certain of the rider's plan before you pull into the motorcycle's path.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.front: How much lane width belongs legally to a motorcycle, and what does that forbid?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.expected_back: A motorcycle is entitled to the full width of a lane, so never squeeze into the same lane as a motorcycle.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.front: What danger do you create by cutting back into a lane too quickly after overtaking a motorcycle?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.memory_hook: Forces rider into traffic or shoulder
sec15-card-sec15-F31.expected_back: After passing a motorcycle, cutting back into your lane too early can push the rider to swerve into other traffic or off the road.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: Why can both a rider's lateral shift and a flashing motorcycle blinker fool an impatient driver?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: A rider moving to one side may be avoiding a hazard rather than turning, and a blinking motorcycle signal may simply have been left on after a turn.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.front: Why are heavy commercial trucks vital across Arizona's highway network?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.expected_back: Large trucks matter to the Arizona economy because they carry products people depend on.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.front: How does a heavy truck's stopping distance compare with a passenger car's?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.expected_back: Never cut in front of a truck, because a truck needs twice as long to stop.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.front: What happens to a truck's safety margin if you merge closely ahead and slam your brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.expected_back: If you cut in front of a truck and then brake hard, you cut the truck's available stopping distance in half.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.front: What name describes the large blind spots around trucks and buses, and where do they sit?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.expected_back: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots, called the No-Zone, at the front and along the back sides, so do not linger there.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.front: Why does following closely behind a wide semi-trailer erase your reaction margin?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.expected_back: Follow a truck at a safe distance, since a truck is almost as wide as some lanes and following too closely leaves you no time to react.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.front: Why must you never sneak into the open gap on a truck's right when it prepares to turn right?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.expected_back: Trucks make wide right turns and may leave an open space on their right just before turning, so never pass a truck on the right if it might turn right.

sec15-card-sec15-F38.front: If mechanical trouble forces a breakdown, how far off the highway should you pull and why?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.expected_back: If you break down, pull as far off the highway as you can, because a parked car hit on the shoulder suffers more severe damage.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.front: Measured in passenger cars, how much can a single loaded truck weigh?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.expected_back: A truck can weigh as much as twenty-five cars, so a truck striking a car parked on the shoulder could be tragic.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: How do the phrases twice as long and half the distance pair up in Arizona's truck-safety rules?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: A truck needs twice as long to stop, and cutting in front of it then braking leaves it only half its stopping distance.

sec15-card-sec15-F40.front: How should you set your following gap behind farm machinery or other slow vehicles?
sec15-card-sec15-F40.expected_back: Behind farm machinery and other slow-moving vehicles, keep a safe following distance that gives you a good field of vision.

sec15-card-sec15-F41.front: What typical speed, width, and lighting traits should you expect from farm machinery?
sec15-card-sec15-F41.expected_back: Farm machinery normally moves at twenty-five miles per hour or slower, can occupy more than one lane and may lack signals.

sec15-card-sec15-F42.front: What deceptive move might a farm-machinery operator make right before turning right?
sec15-card-sec15-F42.expected_back: To make a wide turn, a farm machinery operator may pull to the left first and then turn to the right.

sec15-card-sec15-F43.front: What top speed applies to any vehicle wearing a slow-moving emblem, and what must you do?
sec15-card-sec15-F43.expected_back: A vehicle showing the slow-moving vehicle symbol on its back cannot go faster than twenty-five miles per hour, so the symbol is your signal to slow down.

sec15-card-sec15-F44.front: Do slow-moving vehicles hold a legal right to use public roads, and how should drivers respond?
sec15-card-sec15-F44.expected_back: A slow-moving vehicle has a legal right to be on the road, so do not grow impatient when you are behind one.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.front: How does the trap around a semi-truck's wide right turn compare with a farm machine's wide right turn?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.memory_hook: Truck opens right, tractor swings left
sec15-card-sec15-R10.expected_back: A truck's wide right turn may leave open space on its right that you must not pass into, while a farm machine may pull left before turning right.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.front: How does farm machinery's typical pace compare with the strict cap on a slow-moving vehicle emblem?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.expected_back: Farm machinery usually travels at twenty-five miles per hour or less, while a vehicle with the slow-moving vehicle symbol can never exceed twenty-five miles per hour

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: For which two legal purposes does Arizona MVD collect your Social Security number, and does it print as your license number?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: MVD checks identity and child-support compliance behind the scenes while assigning a separate number to your card.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: Which driving roles match Arizona's Class G, Class D, Class M, and Classes A, B, and C licenses?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Every Arizona credential sorts cleanly into teen graduated, adult operator, two-wheel motorcycle, or heavy commercial classes.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: Where does Arizona place your Class M privilege when you combine motorcycle riding with another license class?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Instead of carrying two separate plastic cards, riders get a Class M endorsement added on the reverse side.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.question_text: What vehicles may you drive on a Class D operator license, and what is the minimum age to apply?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.teaching_text: Class D covers everyday cars, pickups, and vans once you turn eighteen—excluding motorcycles and commercial rigs.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.question_text: Which license or endorsement is required for a motorcycle or motor-driven cycle, and how young may you apply?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.teaching_text: Sixteen-year-olds can earn Class M riding privileges two full years before qualifying for a Class D card.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.question_text: Between Arizona's Class D operator license and Class M motorcycle license, which opens at sixteen and which waits for eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.teaching_text: Teens under eighteen drive cars on Class G, so Class D waits until eighteen while Class M starts at sixteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.question_text: What permit hold time—and which two training or practice options—must an under-eighteen Class M applicant complete?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.teaching_text: Teen riders hold a motorcycle permit six months and finish either an approved MVD course or thirty parent-certified hours.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.question_text: Which license classes cover commercial motor vehicles, and where are their testing rules published?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.teaching_text: Heavy trucks and buses fall under Classes A, B, and C inside Arizona's separate Commercial Driver License manual.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: How old must you be for a graduated or motorcycle instruction permit compared with an operator instruction permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Fifteen years and six months opens both teen and motorcycle permits, whereas adult operator permits start at eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: Which Arizona instruction permit waits until age eighteen while the other two open at fifteen years and six months?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Because Class D itself begins at eighteen, its matching operator instruction permit also requires turning eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: Who must sit right beside a graduated or operator permit holder whenever the car is moving?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: A supervisor tucked in the back seat breaks permit law—they need Class A, B, C, or D at twenty-one-plus up front.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: For how many months do Arizona graduated and operator instruction permits stay valid?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: One twelve-month permit gives plenty of runway to finish your required six-month hold and thirty practice hours.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: Which passenger, highway, and lighting restrictions bind an Arizona motorcycle instruction-permit rider?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Learner riders stay solo off interstates and park between sunset and sunrise or whenever five-hundred-foot visibility drops.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: How long does an Arizona motorcycle permit last, and what cap limits renewing it?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Unlike year-long car permits, motorcycle permits expire after seven months with just one renewal per twenty-four months.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: How does the lifespan of a graduated or operator permit compare with a motorcycle permit?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Keep twelve and seven apart—car permits run a full year while motorcycle permits run seven months.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: Where online does Arizona MVD host practice material for the written permit check?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Reviewing sample items directly at azdot dot gov slash mvd builds confidence before visiting an MVD counter.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: What check must you pass before MVD issues an Arizona instruction permit—and which commercial permit is excluded?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Every standard Arizona learner permit requires clearing the Division written check first, whereas Commercial Learner's Permits follow separate rules.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: Does the standard rule requiring the Division written check before an instruction permit cover Commercial Learner's Permits?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Commercial truck trainees follow federal-state CDL testing rules rather than the passenger-manual permit rule.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: If you held a learner's permit in another state before moving, how does Arizona treat those months?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Arizona credits documented permit time earned in your prior state toward your six-month graduated requirement.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Which age bracket receives an Arizona Class G graduated license, and what vehicles does it cover?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Class G bridges ages sixteen and seventeen for standard passenger vehicles that need neither motorcycle nor CDL credentials.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: During the first six months on Class G, which overnight hours are off-limits—and who in the front seat lifts curfew?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Late-night solo driving stops from midnight to five a.m. unless a licensed parent or guardian rides up front.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: What exact clock window and how many initial months define Arizona's Class G nighttime restriction?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: After completing those initial six solo months—or reaching your eighteenth birthday—that overnight driving ban lifts.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: Which four solo trip purposes let a first-six-months Class G teen drive legally between midnight and five a.m.?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Driving straight between home and sanctioned school events, employment, religious services, or family emergencies stays legal.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: How does who may supervise an instruction permit differ from who lifts the Class G night restriction?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: An older cousin at twenty-one can supervise your permit, yet only a licensed parent or guardian lifts Class G curfew.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: During the first six Class G months, how many non-sibling passengers under eighteen may ride without a licensed parent up front?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Stacking multiple teen friends multiplies crash odds, capping non-sibling minors at one during your first six months.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: Do your own brothers and sisters under eighteen count against Arizona's one-teen Class G passenger cap?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: You can drive younger siblings to school freely—only non-sibling passengers under eighteen trigger the one-rider limit.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: How long must you hold an Arizona instruction permit before applying for Class G, and what status must it have?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Showing up with six months logged on an expired permit fails—the permit itself must remain active on application day.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: How do the two separate six-month periods in Arizona's teen licensing timeline differ?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: First comes six supervised months on your learner permit, followed by six restricted solo months on Class G.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: Alongside six permit months, which two training alternatives qualify a teen for a Class G license?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Completing state-approved driver schooling waives the written parental practice log, while skipping class makes parent sign-off mandatory.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: How many total and night supervised hours must a parent certify—and what reduced option exists after specific safety courses?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Standard parent logs require thirty hours including ten at night, dropping to twenty and six after Survival or Defensive courses.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Which two specific courses reduce supervised Arizona teen practice from thirty-and-ten hours down to twenty-and-six?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Finishing either of those two safety programs trims ten total practice hours and four night hours off parental certification.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: Who may MVD excuse from Arizona's six-month permit, driver ed, and practice-hour requirements?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Teens moving in with an active license from another state may bypass repeating learner requirements.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: Does Arizona force a Class G driver to swap for a Class D operator card upon turning eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Your Class G plastic remains valid past your eighteenth birthday, though you may upgrade to Class D if desired.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: Why should you read the fine print included with an Arizona traffic citation right away?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Checking your ticket packet promptly ensures you never miss deadlines for Arizona's court-run defensive driving course.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: What mandatory consequence hits an under-eighteen Class G driver after a first traffic-violation conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Conviction number one goes onto your driving record and orders you into Traffic Survival School.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: What suspension lengths hit an under-eighteen Class G driver on a second traffic conviction and on a third?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Conviction two grounds you for three months, and conviction three doubles that suspension to six full months.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: At which conviction number do license suspensions start for an under-eighteen Class G driver?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Do not pick suspension on strike one—Traffic Survival School comes first before three- and six-month suspensions follow.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: What happens when a Class G teen gets caught breaking the midnight curfew or one-friend passenger rule?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Breaking night or passenger rules adds fines and stretches your restricted period beyond the original six months.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: How many curfew or passenger convictions trigger suspension—and what else suspends a teen's privilege?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Three curfew or passenger convictions—or other serious or alcohol-related offenses—pull your driving privilege.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: Who must sign an Arizona instruction permit or license application when the applicant is under eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Minors under eighteen cannot self-sign at MVD without an eligible adult signature backing the application.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: What legal responsibility does an adult accept by signing a minor's permit or license application?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: If that teen causes a crash through careless or willful driving, legal financial liability lands on the adult signer.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: How many parents sign when parents are married, unmarried with joint custody, or holding sole custody?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Unmarried parents sharing joint custody need both signatures, whereas married couples or sole-custody parents need one.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: Why must unmarried parents with joint custody bring two signatures when married parents need only one?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Arizona treats married households as one signing unit while requiring separate consent from both unmarried joint-custody parents.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: When parents do not sign, which three documented adults—including an employer—may sign for a minor?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Legal guardians and live-in foster parents show custody proof, while an employer can sign only with parental death certificates.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: Who must witness adult signatures for a minor, and does signing the permit cover the later license?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Every adult signature needs an MVD counter witness or notary stamp, and upgrading from permit to license requires signing again.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: Which three identifying facts must appear on a request to cancel a minor's driver license?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: Listing the exact credential number, full name, and birth date ensures MVD cancels the right minor record.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.question_text: Who does federal law require to register with Selective Service, and within what window around age eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.teaching_text: Male U.S. citizens and male resident non-citizens must register within thirty days of their eighteenth birthday.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.question_text: For a male applicant under twenty-six, which three MVD transactions carry automatic Selective Service consent—and which stays optional?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.teaching_text: Applying for a first, renewed, or reinstated card triggers consent automatically, whereas ordering a duplicate card leaves it optional.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: Which single MVD card request lets a male under twenty-six treat Selective Service registration as optional?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Spot the duplicate carve-out—originals, renewals, and reinstatements all bundle Selective Service consent automatically.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.question_text: How does MVD handle Selective Service data for eighteen-to-twenty-five-year-olds versus teens under eighteen—and does it enlist you?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.teaching_text: Adult filings transmit right away while teen filings wait until eighteen, and registering never joins the military.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: Where must you position your car if forced to leave it along an uncurbed highway versus a curbed street?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Pulling as far off live lanes or flush against the curb protects passing traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: Which three brake, transmission, and ignition steps secure a vehicle before you step out?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Anchoring both parking brake and Park or manual gear stops runaway rollaways.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: After securing a disabled car roadside, what should you place outside and where should you wait if safe?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Remaining with a well-marked car helps responders find you and beats wandering along shoulders.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: What simple security step belongs whenever you have no choice except walking away from your stopped vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Locking up protects valuables and keeps your cabin secure until a tow arrives.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: Name three everyday access or crossing zones where parking is always illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Parking across walkways, aprons, or corner boxes traps pedestrians and blocks turns.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Besides parking directly on a crosswalk, within how many feet of an intersection crosswalk is parking banned?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Keeping twenty feet clear lets approaching drivers spot pedestrians stepping off the curb.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Under what sole circumstance is parking permitted along a freeway or interstate highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: High-speed shoulders are emergency refuge strips, never rest stops for checking texts.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: When a genuine breakdown forces a freeway stop, which four securing and warning steps still apply?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Emergency permission never waives pulling far onto the shoulder, setting the brake, shutting off, and warning traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: Even away from hydrants or crosswalks, what two broad conditions make parking unlawful anywhere?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Leaving your car sticking into a blind curve creates an illegal hazard even without a red sign.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: Within how many feet of a fire hydrant is parking prohibited in Arizona?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Fire crews need fifteen unobstructed feet on both sides to couple heavy supply hoses fast.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: Within how many feet of a railroad crossing is parking illegal in Arizona?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Parked cars closer than fifty feet hide flashing crossbucks and approaching locomotives.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Line up Arizona's three no-parking distances from shortest to longest — hydrant, crosswalk, and railroad?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Climbing fifteen, twenty, fifty locks all three Arizona curb-distance test numbers in order.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: May a driver park on a bridge span or inside a highway tunnel?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Zero shoulder width on bridges and inside tunnels turns any parked car into a bottleneck trap.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: What traffic mission are freeways and interstate highways engineered to handle?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Wide lanes, barriers, and grade-separated ramps move high speeds without cross-traffic stops.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: Between drivers already cruising on the freeway and drivers entering from an on-ramp, who must yield?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Through freeway traffic holds priority, placing safe merge timing squarely on the entering driver.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Walk through the speed, signal, check, and merge sequence for joining a freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Accelerating on the ramp to match right-lane speed prevents dangerous slow pull-outs.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: Which painted stripe and ramp zone must you never cut across while entering a freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Cutting across solid white lines or the painted gore triangle surprises sixty-five-mph right-lane cars.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: How do solid white lines and gore areas restrict both freeway entries and freeway exits?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Solid white ramp channel lines and gore wedges stay off-limits whether joining or leaving.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: What communication step is mandatory before peeling off onto a freeway exit?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Early right blinkers warn trailing highway cars before you move into the exit lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: What dedicated lane helps you leave most freeways without slowing main traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Waiting until you enter the deceleration lane keeps high-speed through lanes flowing safely.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: Contrast how you manage speed on a freeway entrance ramp versus a freeway exit lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: On-ramps build speed up to right-lane flow, whereas deceleration lanes shed speed smoothly off-line.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: Which two habits prevent crashes when queueing onto a busy, backed-up freeway exit?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Exit ramps stack up abruptly at rush hour, punishing tailgaters and last-second solid-line cutters.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: What roadway layout defines a divided highway or freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Splitting opposing traffic flows onto separate multi-lane roadways prevents deadly head-on highway crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: What distinguishes a controlled-access expressway or freeway from an ordinary highway with traffic lights?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Removing cross-street lights and driveways lets freeway traffic cruise uninterrupted between ramps.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: When should you move into the target lane for entering or leaving a highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Diving across three freeway lanes at the last hundred yards causes multi-car sideswipes.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: At what point relative to the exit ramp must your turn signal already be flashing?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Flicking the lever only after crossing onto the ramp fails to warn highway followers.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Combine your right-of-way duty and throttle goal as you join a fast highway lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Yielding to occupied gaps while matching speed blends you seamlessly into traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: What two dangerous reactions are banned if you miss your exit, and what is the right fix?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Stopping or backing on a sixty-five-mph shoulder invites catastrophic high-speed rear impacts.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: How do you legally get back to your destination after sailing past your highway exit?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Using the next overpass interchange turns you around safely without illegal reversing.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.question_text: May you ever shift into reverse on a freeway shoulder to catch an exit you just passed?
sec08-card-sec08-F41.teaching_text: Arizona tests this twice because backing toward an off-ramp causes deadly freeway wrecks.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: On any roadway with two or more lanes, which half belongs to your travel — and what two exceptions apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Keeping right preserves predictable lane order unless overtaking or following overhead lane signs.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: On a highway with three or more lanes one way, why can the far right lane move either slower or faster?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Merging cars punch the gas while exiting cars ease off, making right-lane pace fluctuate.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: Don't assume the right lane of a three-lane freeway is only slow — what two movements make it faster too?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Brisk ramp mergers and eager exiters make far-right speeds swing both below and above center lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: During heavy rush hour on a multi-lane freeway, why do through drivers often leave the right lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Cruising in center lanes opens gaps in the right lane for constant on-ramp and off-ramp streams.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: Which four merge, signal, speed, and spacing habits keep multi-lane highway cruising safe?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Tracking ramp cars while signaling shifts, obeying speed signs, and avoiding tailgating keeps traffic smooth.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: What is a freeway gore area, and which two vehicle actions inside it violate Arizona law?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Arizona strictly tickets both cutting across and parking inside the striped triangle between ramp and mainline.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: Pinpoint where the gore area sits on a freeway and both unlawful uses of it?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Debris collects inside that triangular wedge, and swerving over it causes high-speed collisions.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: Where should you pull over if your car breaks down on a freeway — and what spot must you avoid?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Stopping on curved entrance or exit ramps hides your car where merging drivers accelerate.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: Which two daytime signals and two after-dark additions show you need help on a freeway shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Raised hoods vanish after sunset, so add your interior dome light or portable flares and triangles.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: Contrast daytime freeway help signals with what you add once darkness falls?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Adding cabin dome glow and roadside flares makes a dark shoulder car visible at seventy miles per hour.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: While waiting for roadside assistance on a freeway, where should you stay and what is banned?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Pedestrians walking along high-speed interstate shoulders face extreme danger from drifting traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: What three protective steps apply when you spot a broken-down vehicle ahead on the freeway shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Giving a wide adjacent lane protects stranded motorists or tow crews working beside traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: What painted pavement symbol identifies High Occupancy Vehicle lanes in Arizona?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Spotting white diamond stencils alerts solo drivers immediately before entering restricted carpool lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: During posted weekday HOV hours, what minimum headcount — or which two vehicle types — may use the lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Solo cars stay out during posted weekday windows while two-plus carpools, motorcycles, and buses roll.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: Does Arizona's two-person HOV minimum include the driver, and does it apply 24/7 or at posted weekday times?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: One passenger plus you equals two, and outside posted weekday hours general traffic may enter.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: What awaits a solo motorist caught cheating Arizona's HOV restriction during posted hours?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Arizona sets steep HOV fines so solo commuters don't clog express carpool lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.question_text: How should you cross the solid white line separating an Arizona HOV lane from regular lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.teaching_text: Speed differences between clogged main lanes and open HOV lanes demand clear blinkers and mirror checks.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: Pair the three vehicle groups eligible during restricted HOV hours with how they enter or exit?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Even eligible two-plus cars, motorcycles, and buses must signal carefully across the white HOV stripe.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.question_text: Which two turnaround moves across a freeway median or divider are strictly illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.teaching_text: Paved emergency turnarounds in medians belong strictly to patrol and rescue vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.question_text: What lane-change rule and entry-point rule govern every Arizona freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.teaching_text: Cutting onto a freeway from dirt frontage strips or switching lanes unannounced causes high-speed wrecks.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.question_text: Where is non-emergency stopping allowed along a freeway, and when may you use the shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.teaching_text: Rest areas handle breaks, keeping live freeway shoulders reserved strictly for emergencies.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Contrast where you may take a routine freeway break against when shoulder parking becomes legal?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Phone calls or driver swaps belong in designated rest areas, never on emergency shoulders.

sec08-card-sec08-F42.question_text: What two mechanical capabilities should you verify before taking a vehicle onto a high-speed highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F42.teaching_text: Limping onto an interstate in an overheating or underpowered car creates a rolling hazard.

sec08-card-sec08-F43.question_text: What is the general left-lane rule, and how do the far right and far left lanes split jobs on a three-lane highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F43.teaching_text: Camping slowly in the far left lane blocks overtaking and sparks unsafe right-side weaving.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: Match the far right lane and far left lane of a three-lane highway to their designated roles?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Sorting slower through cars right and overtakers left keeps center-lane cruising smooth.
sec08-card-sec08-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Far right slower, far left passes

visual_sync.text_span: Far right slower, far left passes

sec08-card-sec08-F44.question_text: Where between painted lines should your tires track, and which two tools pair for lane changes?
sec08-card-sec08-F44.teaching_text: Hugging stripes crowds neighboring mirrors, while checking rearview and signaling keeps moves predictable.

sec08-card-sec08-F45.question_text: Which three visual systems regulate road traffic and require complete driver understanding?
sec08-card-sec08-F45.teaching_text: Instant fluency across overhead bulbs, roadside signs, and painted lines keeps highway decisions automatic.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: What two aspects of intersection traffic do red, yellow, and green signal lights regulate?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Coordinated three-color signals prevent competing streams of vehicles from colliding inside busy intersections.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Alongside motor-vehicle drivers, which three other groups on the road are legally bound by traffic lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Stepping off a curb or pedaling through a red signal violates traffic law just like running one in a car.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Under what sole exception may you disobey what an intersection signal light displays?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Crashes, parades, or power emergencies put live officer hand signals ahead of overhead bulbs.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: If a traffic officer waves you through a red light, whose command takes priority?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Stopping for red when an officer waves you forward stalls emergency traffic clearing behind you.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: What condition must be met before you move through an intersection on a steady green light?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Green grants permission to go when clear rather than a blind guarantee that cross-lanes are empty.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: Why must you check left and right before accelerating into an intersection on a green light?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: T-bone crashes hit hardest in the opening seconds of green when impatient cross-drivers try beating late reds.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: When your signal flips to green, which vehicles still hold priority ahead of you?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Left-turners or slow trucks caught mid-box during the signal change need space to clear the intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: What upcoming signal change does a steady yellow traffic light announce?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Yellow clears the intersection before cross-traffic gets green, never inviting drivers to floor the gas.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: How does your legal duty on a steady yellow light depend on whether you have entered the intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Slamming brakes mid-intersection traps you in cross-traffic, whereas stopping before the line keeps the box open.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: How does Arizona law treat accelerating to beat a yellow light before it turns red?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Gunning the throttle toward a stale yellow risks entering on red right as opposing left-turners clear the box.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Where must you come to a full stop for a steady red light, and how long must you wait?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Creeping past the stop bar or crosswalk edges your bumper into pedestrian and cross-street paths.
sec09-card-sec09-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Stop before line; wait out red

visual_sync.text_span: Stop before line; wait out red

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: How does the stopping duty on a steady yellow light differ from a steady red light?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Yellow asks for a safe stop before entry, while red demands a dead stop and waiting.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: Under what three conditions may you turn right against a steady red traffic light?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Rolling through a right-on-red without stopping first causes frequent crosswalk strikes and citations.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: What mandatory action and sign check govern every right turn on a steady red signal?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Even when cross-traffic looks empty, a posted No Turn On Red sign or rolling stop earns a ticket.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: When leaving a freeway, where must you brake and shed speed instead of slowing on the main lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Braking early on seventy-mile-per-hour through lanes invites high-speed rear-end collisions behind you.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: Which roadside traffic sign carries the exact same legal rule as a flashing red signal light?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Treat every flashing red bulb with a dead stop first, then move cautiously once cross-traffic clears.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: How should you handle an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Unnecessary panic stops under a flashing yellow surprise drivers behind you—ease off the gas and scan carefully instead.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: How does your required action at a flashing red signal contrast with a flashing yellow signal?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Exam questions pair two-way intersections where side streets get flashing red stops while main roads get flashing yellow caution.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: May you turn after stopping when facing a lighted red arrow in your turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Unlike a circular red where right-on-red may apply, a lighted red arrow locks out that turn until green.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: What signal transition does a lighted steady yellow arrow announce?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Protected turn time is ending, meaning oncoming through lanes are moments away from getting green.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: Facing a steady yellow arrow, what should you do before entering versus once already inside the intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Stopping behind the line avoids running the red arrow, while finishing an active turn clears cross-lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: Why should a driver already past the stop bar keep turning when the arrow flips to steady yellow?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Freezing or reversing inside the box leaves your side doors exposed when cross-traffic launches on green.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: What steps let you turn legally under a flashing yellow arrow?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: A flashing yellow arrow means opposing traffic also has green, so misjudging an oncoming car's speed causes head-on wrecks.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: How does a lighted red arrow differ from a flashing yellow arrow for turning drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Red arrows hold turns until green appears, whereas flashing yellow arrows allow permissive turns through safe gaps.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: When a green arrow lights up alone or beside another bulb, what must be true before you go?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Cutting across from a through lane to grab a green arrow clips cars turning legally from the turn bay.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: How must every driver treat an intersection when its traffic signal lights are dark or out of order?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Blowing through an unlit signal during a power outage causes severe broadside crashes when cross-streets expect stops.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: When two cars reach a dark signal at roughly the same moment, who stops and who yields?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Remembering that the driver on the right goes first settles simultaneous four-way arrivals without hesitation.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: At an inoperative traffic light, which driver wins a simultaneous-arrival tie after both come to a stop?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Yielding to the vehicle on your right breaks deadlocks cleanly without awkward hand-waving.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: At an unmarked T-intersection, which street's drivers must yield the right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Drivers on the terminating stem must wait for clear gaps on the continuing crossroad.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: Between the terminating road and the continuing cross street at a T-intersection, who yields?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Even if you approach from the right on the ending stem, the T-intersection rule makes the ending street yield.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: What guides your stopping and yielding duties at a controlled intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Installed traffic lights, stop signs, and yield triangles always override default uncontrolled-corner right-of-way rules.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: Why isn't having the legal right-of-way enough by itself to pull straight into an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Legal priority never stops a distracted driver or jaywalker from stepping into your path.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: Where do you bring your vehicle to a halt at a controlled intersection with pavement markings?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Stopping cleanly at the painted bar keeps crosswalks open and gives cross-turners full turning clearance.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: How does Arizona treat an open intersection that has no signals, stop signs, or yield signs?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Residential grid corners without signs require a complete stop in Arizona rather than a rolling slow-down.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: What rule links an intersection with a blacked-out traffic signal and an intersection with no controls at all?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Pairing dark signals with unsigned residential intersections under one four-way-stop habit prevents right-of-way guesswork.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: Does Arizona traffic law grant right-of-way to a driver, or specify who must yield?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: This classic MVD wording question tests that nobody ever owns the road—statutes only assign yielding duties.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: When is every driver barred from insisting on taking the right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Even when another driver breaks the yield rule, you must brake or steer safely to avoid colliding.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: At which types of crosswalks are drivers required to yield to crossing pedestrians?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Every street-corner extension forms a legal crosswalk whether crews painted white bars there or not.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: Once your traffic light turns green, what duty do you still owe people or cars finishing in the intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Slower seniors or parents with strollers caught mid-street when the signal flips keep priority until safely across.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: What does Arizona law require at a school crossing while any person is inside the crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Unlike ordinary yielding, occupied school crosswalks require a dead stop until the entire crosswalk clears.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: May you pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian if your adjacent lane looks clear or your signal is green?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: The stopped car's hood hides the walker stepping directly in front of your moving lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: How do Arizona's occupied school-crosswalk rule and its stopped-for-pedestrian passing rule protect walkers?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Both rules eliminate multi-lane blind-spot tragedies where one driver stops and the next lane barrels past.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: For safety, whom does the Arizona manual advise yielding to whenever someone is crossing any street?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Giving space even when someone crosses outside a crosswalk prevents irreversible pedestrian fatalities.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: On a pedestrian-activated crosswalk beacon, what do flashing yellow and solid yellow each signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Arizona uses HAWK pedestrian beacons widely—flashing yellow wakes drivers up, then solid yellow transitions to red.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: How does flashing yellow differ from solid yellow on a pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Recognizing solid yellow early lets you brake smoothly before the dual solid red stop lamps illuminate.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: What must you do when solid red lights illuminate on a pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Solid red on a pedestrian beacon matches an intersection red light while walkers cross the roadway.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: What does flashing red allow on a pedestrian crosswalk beacon once you have stopped?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Once the walker clears your half of the roadway and no others enter, flashing red works like a stop sign.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: On a pedestrian-activated signal, how does solid red differ from wig-wagging flashing red?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Permit questions target this exact beacon distinction because solid red holds you while flashing red lets you proceed once clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Which three real-world factors determine a roadway's proper speed limit, and how strictly must posted signs be obeyed?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Engineers set posted caps from actual crash history and sightlines rather than guesswork, making every posted sign binding.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: When no speed sign is posted, what is Arizona's legal limit approaching a school crosswalk?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Arizona sets its lowest default speed at fifteen miles per hour right where students step off curbs.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: What default speed limit applies inside an unsigned business or residential district?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Driveways, parked cars, and storefront foot traffic keep unposted neighborhood and downtown streets capped at twenty-five.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: How does Arizona's unposted school-crosswalk speed limit compare with its unposted business or residential limit?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Driving twenty-five miles per hour through neighborhood streets still requires dropping to fifteen whenever you approach an unposted school crosswalk.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Where no speed limit is posted, what limit governs open highways and city freeways?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Before assuming sixty-five or seventy-five, note that unsigned open highways and urban freeways default to fifty-five.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: What default speed limit applies on designated open highways when no sign posts otherwise?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Watch the word designated on MVD questions—adding designated bumps an open highway's unposted limit from fifty-five to sixty-five.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: When no sign is posted, what is the speed limit along Arizona's rural freeways?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Wide interstate sightlines outside urban metro areas carry Arizona's top seventy-five-mile-per-hour unposted default speed.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How do Arizona's unposted highway limits step up across open/city, designated open, and rural freeways?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Climbing cleanly in ten-mile-per-hour steps makes matching fifty-five, sixty-five, and seventy-five effortless on test day.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: What category of sign is a white speed sign with black lettering, and what does it set?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Exceeding a black-on-white speed limit breaks state traffic law even on clear, dry pavement.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: What does an orange sign with black numbers communicate at a curve, hill grade, or special spot?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Carrying highway speed past an orange advisory number risks skidding wide on tight temporary alignments.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: How does a black-on-white speed sign differ from a black-on-orange speed sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: White enforces the statutory ceiling, while orange warns what speed keeps your tires planted through a spot hazard.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What weather and road baseline do posted speed limits assume, and how must you adjust in storms?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Driving the posted fifty-five through blinding monsoon rain can still earn an unsafe-speed citation.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: How must your speed change whenever pavement turns wet, snowy, or icy?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Water, slush, and ice slash tire friction so stopping distances stretch far past dry-pavement norms.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: Along with dropping speed, how should you adjust your following distance in bad weather?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Giving twice the space ahead prevents chain-reaction rear-end crashes when spray hides brake lights.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Why isn't merely easing off the gas enough by itself when driving in bad weather?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Arizona's manual pairs slower speed with twice the following distance—picking only one misses half the safety rule.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: How dangerous is driving far too slowly compared with speeding?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Creeping well below freeway flow triggers sudden braking and risky last-second lane weaves behind you.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: Which lane belongs to you whenever you are traveling slower than surrounding traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Camping in left lanes forces faster drivers to pass on the right where blind spots run widest.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: What two core purposes do roadside traffic signs serve?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Every highway sign either enforces a traffic rule, warns of hazards, or guides your route.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: How much meaning does a traffic sign's outer shape carry compared with its color or lettering?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Standardized silhouettes let your brain recognize stop, yield, or hazard rules in a split second.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: In which three Arizona visibility hazards might a sign's silhouette be the only clue you can see?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Blowing desert dust, thick fog, or sheets of monsoon rain can obscure lettering while leaving the outline visible.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Which single traffic sign uses an eight-sided octagon, and what action does it demand?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Even from behind or caked in mud, an eight-sided outline never means anything except a complete stop.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: What duty does a downward-pointing triangle sign place on you?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Slow as you approach the inverted triangle and prepare to stop if cross or merging traffic is close.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: How does an eight-sided octagon sign differ from a three-sided triangle sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Octagons require stopping every single time, while triangles let you roll cautiously when conflicting lanes are clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: What do rectangular regulatory signs govern, and what turn rules commonly appear on them?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Vertical and square rectangles post enforceable commands like speed limits, mandatory lanes, and prohibited turns.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: What upcoming roadway feature do turn, curve, and winding-road signs alert you to?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Shed speed before steering into the bend rather than braking hard mid-curve where tires lose lateral grip.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: What does a small square yellow plaque mounted beneath a curve warning sign indicate?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: That smaller yellow square translates the bend's tightness into a concrete target speed before turn-in.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: On a curve warning assembly, how do the upper curve sign and the small lower yellow square split duties?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Read both pieces together so you know both which way the road bends and how much speed to drop.
sec11-card-sec11-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Diamond warns bend, square sets speed

visual_sync.text_span: Diamond warns bend, square sets speed

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: What zone begins at a sideways pennant-shaped sign?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Mounted on the left side of two-lane highways, the yellow pennant stays visible even behind tall trucks.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: What general message do yellow diamond-shaped signs deliver?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Whenever a yellow diamond appears, scan ahead and cover the brake for merges, crossings, dips, or curves.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: How does a sideways yellow pennant sign differ from a yellow diamond sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Exam shape matchers love pairing these two yellow signs—pennants strictly start no-passing zones while diamonds flag general hazards.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: What shape is a permanent school crossing warning sign, and when might children be crossing there?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: After-school clubs, sports, and neighborhood play mean children use school crosswalks well past morning and afternoon bells.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: Which two background colors are used on Arizona school crossing signs?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Bright fluorescent yellow-green stands out sharply at dawn, dusk, and shaded neighborhood crossings.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: When portable school signs stand in the roadway, what is the speed limit and where does that zone run?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Arizona school crews place roll-out signs right on the centerline—hold fifteen all the way past the crosswalk.
sec11-card-sec11-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Fifteen from first sign past crossing

visual_sync.text_span: Fifteen from first sign past crossing

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: Which speed limit governs the street once portable school-zone signs have been taken off the roadway?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Portable roll-out zones enforce fifteen only while set out, though you must still watch for kids near permanent pentagons.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: How do portable school signs turn Arizona's fifteen-mile-per-hour school zone on and off?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Hold fifteen from the first portable marker until past the crossing sign, then resume normal limits when crews remove them.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: Is passing another vehicle ever legal inside an Arizona school crossing zone?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Swinging around a slowed or stopped car near a school crosswalk blinds you to children stepping past its bumper.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: What two duties apply at a school crosswalk staffed by a crossing guard?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Wait until both the crossing children and the adult guard have cleared the roadway before easing forward.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: What single hazard ahead is announced by a circular traffic sign?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Round yellow RXR signs give advance notice so you can quiet the radio, look both ways, and cover brakes.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: Which sign silhouette warns of a school crossing, and which warns of an upcoming railroad crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Picture a five-sided schoolhouse roof for pentagons and a round locomotive wheel for circles.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: While the round sign warns ahead, what does the railroad crossing sign itself mark?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: White X-shaped crossbucks stand right beside the rails so you know exactly where the track bed crosses.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: How far back from the nearest rail must you stop when lights, bells, gates, or a flagger warn of rail traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Locomotives overhang wider than steel rails, so stopping closer than fifteen feet puts your bumper in the strike zone.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: Do gates have to come down before you stop fifteen feet from a railroad track, or does any single warning count?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Many rural crossings lack gates altogether—flashing reds, bells, or a flagger alone each require a fifteen-foot stop.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: Which two Arizona rules both use the number fifteen while measuring speed versus distance?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: Pairing fifteen miles per hour at schools with fifteen feet from rails locks two high-yield numbers at once.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: After a train passes, what must happen with crossing signals and gates before you drive onto the tracks?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: On double-track lines a second train from the opposite direction often hides behind the departing caboose.
sec11-card-sec11-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Every signal off, gate fully up

visual_sync.text_span: Every signal off, gate fully up

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: Is weaving around or ducking beneath a lowered railroad gate ever legal?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Trains look slower than they really travel and need over a mile to stop—gate-runners rarely get a second chance.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: What should you always assume whenever you approach any railroad track at any time?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: Freight trains and maintenance railcars run irregular hours outside commuter schedules on every active rail line.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: Why must you check traffic space on the far side before rolling onto a railroad crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: Stopping with your rear bumper hanging over rails behind a red-light queue leaves zero escape if gates drop.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.question_text: What immediate action does the Arizona manual instruct if your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.teaching_text: Never stay buckled inside cranking a dead starter—evacuate everyone out of the car right away.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: Above everything else, what simple rule does Arizona's manual stress when a car dies on railroad tracks?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Cars can be replaced by insurance, whereas hesitating inside a stalled cabin on active rails costs lives.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: Why must you never try to beat an approaching train or rail vehicle across a grade crossing?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Large locomotives create an optical illusion that makes their closing speed look deceptively slow until impact.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Which two types of large vehicles should you expect to stop at railroad tracks even without flashing lights?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Leaving extra room behind transit buses, school buses, and fuel tankers prevents rear-ending them when they halt at tracks.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: Why should you stay ready to brake behind the vehicle ahead whenever approaching railroad tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Tailgating a bus or fuel truck toward an open crossing causes rear-end collisions when it makes its mandatory stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: What extra railroad hazard must you scan for when driving at night?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Rural crossings often lack overhead lamps or active flashers, leaving only headlight reflection off passive signs.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: Which three highway networks have route markers included among highway guide signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Distinctive shield shapes let travelers tell interstate freeways from U.S. highways and Arizona state routes at a glance.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: What distinguishes Arizona's highway mileage-marker coverage compared with most other states?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Posting markers along every state route gives desert and mountain travelers pinpoint location references statewide.
sec12-card-sec12-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Mile markers on every state highway

visual_sync.text_span: Mile markers on every state highway

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: How far off the right highway shoulder are Arizona mile posts positioned?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Setting posts two feet outside the right shoulder edge keeps them visible in headlights without crowding breakdowns.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Roughly how far apart are Arizona highway mile posts set along a route?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Counting consecutive posts lets you track distance to exits and gauge emergency positions between remote towns.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: For Arizona highway mile posts, what do two feet and one mile each measure?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Practice distractors often swap those two numbers because posts stand two feet off the shoulder at one-mile spacing.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: In which three roadside emergencies does reading a nearby mile post help rescuers find you?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Giving 911 or roadside assistance an exact milepost cuts response time dramatically on featureless desert stretches.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: Whenever you are forced to pull over along a highway, which two location facts should you note?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Knowing only Milepost 112 helps little unless dispatchers also know which highway number you are on.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: What two durations and sign setups can highway work zones take?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: A pothole or utility crew using portable roll-out signs for two hours carries the same danger as multi-month rebuilds.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: How does signage differ between a long-term highway project and a short few-hour maintenance zone?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Both permanent posts and temporary tripod stands carry full work-zone authority while displayed.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: What three crash types happen most frequently inside highway work zones?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Speeding tailgaters slam into slowed queues or concrete barriers, putting both motorists and road crews in danger.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: What mindset and braking readiness do changing work-zone conditions and milled surfaces demand?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Grooved asphalt, uneven lane edges, and abrupt flagger halts leave zero margin for daydreaming.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: Where might construction crews and heavy equipment operate or pull out inside a work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Dump trucks and graders accelerate slowly when merging out from behind cones into live traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: Which three groups are protected or guided by construction warning and channelizing devices?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Barrels, signs, and pedestrian detours shield crews on foot while steering cars and walkers clear of trenches.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: Which standard background color identifies road construction and maintenance warning devices?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Spotting bright orange ahead immediately cues you to drop speed, widen your gap, and scan for lane shifts.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: What three rules apply every time you pass through a construction site?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Combining lower speed, heightened scanning, and strict compliance with temporary limits prevents work-zone tragedies.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: Whose lives are protected by reduced work-zone speed limits?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Data shows drivers and passengers actually suffer the majority of injuries in high-speed work-zone crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: How does Arizona penalize speeding inside a work zone when work-zone signs are posted?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Whenever construction speed signs stand posted along a work zone, speeding fines automatically double to protect crews.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: What exact condition triggers Arizona's doubled speeding fine in a work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Watch exam distractors claiming workers must be standing two feet away—posted work-zone signs trigger doubled speeding fines.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: What three traffic-control actions do human flaggers perform in road work zones?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: One-lane alternating work zones rely on flaggers at each end to keep opposing queues from meeting head-on.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: What high-visibility gear do flaggers wear, and what handheld tools do they use to direct you?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: A flagger's STOP/SLOW paddle carries full legal authority just like a regulatory sign.
sec12-card-sec12-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Orange gear; red flags or paddles

visual_sync.text_span: Orange gear; red flags or paddles

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: What general purpose do construction and maintenance signs serve?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Advance orange signs alert you hundreds of feet ahead before lanes narrow or pavement drops.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: Which geometric shape is used for most warning signs inside street and highway work zones?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Street and highway work zones pair the standard hazard-warning diamond silhouette with high-visibility construction orange.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: Why do crews deploy large flashing arrow panels day and night ahead of work zones?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Bright sequential bulbs cut through daytime sun glare and nighttime darkness miles before the lane closes.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: What two steps should you take as soon as you spot a flashing work-zone arrow panel ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Merging early prevents bottleneck standstills and last-second cone strikes at the taper.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: What four kinds of advance alerts appear on changeable electronic highway message signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Reading overhead or trailer LED boards early lets you take alternate exits before hitting a closure.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: How do cones, drums, and barricades help drivers through a work zone—including after dark?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Follow the smooth line of reflective drums and night flashers rather than faded old lane paint underneath.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: How does a human flagger's role differ from a lighted flashing arrow panel?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Flaggers can stop, slow, or wave traffic through, whereas a flashing arrow board specifically closes a lane.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: How does a flashing arrow panel differ from an electronic text message sign?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Arrow panels command a directional lane shift right ahead, while text boards broadcast closures, detours, or weather.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: How do advance construction signs and channelizing cones, drums, or barricades divide the job?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Orange diamonds prepare you before the zone starts, then barrels physically trace your path past crews.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: What three functions do painted pavement markings perform for traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Just like upright signs, painted lines and symbols combine guidance, hazard warnings, and enforceable rules.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: Which two colors make up standard lane markings, and what happens when solid and broken lines combine?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Pairing solid with broken stripes creates directional rules depending on which stripe sits nearest your tires.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: What traffic pattern do yellow centerlines indicate?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Seeing yellow on your left reminds you that crossing it puts you face-to-face with opposing traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: Besides dividing same-direction lanes, what three roadway features do white lines mark?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: White paint handles same-direction lane splits, right-side shoulder edges, intersection stop bars, and pedestrian walkways.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: What core directional split separates yellow lane stripes from white lane stripes?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Checking line color right after turning onto an unfamiliar street immediately confirms whether oncoming cars share the road.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: Why does passing across a single broken yellow line demand extreme caution even when legal?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: You are borrowing an active opposing lane where closing speeds double any misjudged gap.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: How many traffic directions are allowed to pass where a broken yellow line parallels a solid yellow line?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Hills and curves open sight distance for one direction before the other, restricting passing to one side.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: When the broken yellow stripe of a combo centerline sits on your side, when may you pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Having the broken stripe next to your left tires grants permission only once oncoming sight distance is clear.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: May you cross to pass when the solid yellow stripe sits closest to your travel lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: That unbroken stripe warns that a crest, curve, or intersection ahead hides oncoming vehicles from your angle.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: Along a combination yellow centerline, how does the stripe touching your lane govern passing?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Ignore what opposing traffic gets on the far side and read only the yellow line bordering your lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: While double solid yellow lines ban passing both ways, what single maneuver lets you cross them?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: Turning left into a driveway, alley, or side street stays legal across double yellow unless signs forbid it.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: How does crossing double solid yellow lines contrast with crossing broken white lines?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Double yellow permits only left-turn crossings, whereas broken white permits signaled lane changes.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.question_text: What step must come before crossing a broken white line into a neighboring same-way lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.teaching_text: Signaling before moving gives drivers in adjacent lanes warning before you enter their space.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.question_text: Why are solid white lane lines painted along turn bays and intersection approaches?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.teaching_text: Last-second lane swaps right at stop bars sideswipe queued cars and block turn pockets.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: How do broken white lines and solid white lines differ as you approach an intersection?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Make your lane choice while dashes are still broken rather than cutting across solid white turn-lane paint.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.question_text: What must you do if your lane is painted with a curved arrow and the word ONLY?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.teaching_text: Going straight out of an ONLY lane cuts directly into cars turning beside you or facing narrower through lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.question_text: What choices do you have in a lane marked with a combined straight-and-curved pavement arrow?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.teaching_text: Shared option lanes let traffic either turn at the corner or continue straight ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: How does a curved arrow paired with ONLY differ from a combined curved-and-straight arrow?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Read the pavement early so an ONLY arrow never forces you into an unwanted detour.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.question_text: What does a bicycle symbol painted on the roadway alert drivers to expect?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.teaching_text: Slowing and scanning mirrors around painted bike markings prevents right-hooks and close passes.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.question_text: What does any painted color along a street curb tell a driver looking to park?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.teaching_text: Checking curb paint before shutting off the engine avoids tickets or towing in loading and fire zones.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: What is the sole reason and allowed duration for stopping alongside a white painted curb?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Walking inside a building while leaving your car at a white curb turns a passenger zone into a parking ticket.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: What activity is allowed at a yellow painted curb, and what must the driver do while stopped there?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Leaving your vehicle unattended at a yellow loading curb violates the stay-with-your-car requirement.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: Which three actions are completely forbidden along a red painted curb?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Even sitting in Drive with your foot on the brake breaks the red-curb rule.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: How do Arizona's rules step across white, yellow, and red painted curbs?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Match white to passengers, yellow to attended loading, and red to zero stopping for an instant three-way contrast.
sec13-card-sec13-R01.must_match_memory_hook: White riders, yellow loading, red nothing

visual_sync.text_span: White riders, yellow loading, red nothing

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: Which lane is typically best when driving several blocks straight down a multi-lane one-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Riding the middle lane avoids stop-and-go slowdowns from cars turning off both curbs.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: On a multi-lane one-way street, what traffic uses the far-left and far-right lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Because no oncoming traffic blocks the left curb on a one-way street, left turns launch from the far-left lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: Why does the center lane flow smoother than outer lanes along a multi-block one-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Keeping through traffic centered while turning cars peel off from both edges prevents constant brake-tapping.
