sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: What traffic flow direction is divided by white lane stripes?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Every lane separated by white paint travels in your direction rather than toward you.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: Besides separating same-way lanes, what boundary on the right side of the road can a single white line mark?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Tracking that solid white fog line keeps your tires off soft dirt shoulders in glare or rain.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: What two requirements apply before crossing a broken white line into another lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Checking mirrors and blind spots after signaling ensures no car already occupies that dashed gap.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: Which two places on a roadway use a single solid white line?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Solid white handles both outer shoulder edges and turn-or-HOV lane boundaries heading your way.
sec13-card-sec13-F09.must_match_memory_hook: Right road edge and same-way lanes

visual_sync.text_span: Right road edge and same-way lanes

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: Under what two circumstances may you drive across the solid white line on the right edge of the road?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Shoulders are built for breakdowns and emergency dodges, never for sneaking past backed-up traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: When are Arizona drivers permitted to cross a single solid white stripe bordering an HOV lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Arizona allows crossing a single solid white HOV boundary to enter or exit, unlike prohibited double white barriers.
sec13-card-sec13-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Merging into or out of HOV

visual_sync.text_span: Merging into or out of HOV

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: What direction do lanes on each side of a double solid white line travel, and is crossing allowed?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Double solid white paint forms a legal wall between same-direction lanes where weaving is unsafe.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: How does lane-changing permission differ between a broken white line and a double solid white line?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Signal and check before crossing broken white, and treat double solid white as completely off-limits.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: How does the rule for crossing the right-edge solid white line differ from a single solid white HOV stripe?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Stripe position changes the rule because right-shoulder lines stay emergency-only while single white HOV stripes allow routine merges.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: What traffic directions are separated by yellow lane lines?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Yellow paint always warns that traffic on the other side of the line is coming toward you.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: What fundamental rule separates white lane lines from yellow lane lines?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Every other passing, edge, and reversible marking rule builds directly on this white-versus-yellow split.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: On divided highways and one-way streets, which pavement boundary can a single yellow line mark?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Keeping yellow on your left and white on your right instantly confirms you are traveling the right direction.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: On a divided highway or one-way street, which edge is marked white and which edge is marked yellow?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: If yellow ever sits along your right window on a ramp or freeway, you are heading the wrong way.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: How does a reversible lane operate across the day?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Phoenix commuter arterials flip middle lanes inbound mornings and outbound evenings to ease rush-hour bottlenecks.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: What pavement striping typically borders a reversible lane in Arizona?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Spotting parallel dashed yellow stripes on both sides tells you that lane's flow changes on schedule.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: Where should you look to verify whether you may use a reversible lane right now?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Posted hour plaques and overhead lane signals tell you which direction legally owns the reversible lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: What lane type do double dashed yellow lines signal, and what determines its direction?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Never treat double dashed yellow like an ordinary shared left-turn lane without checking time-of-day signs first.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: Do Arizona turning laws apply only at street intersections, or elsewhere too?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Skipping signals or cutting lanes into a shopping-center driveway breaks turning rules just like at a corner.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: What three basic steps belong in every safe turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Signaling and shedding speed before steering keeps tires settled and warns trailing traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: Which three smaller, harder-to-spot road users must you check for throughout every turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Right-hooks against curb-side bikes or mopeds and left-turn crosswalk strikes happen when drivers scan only for cars.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: Where intersections allow turning from two or more lanes, how do you know which lanes qualify?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Follow your curved lane dashes all the way around so dual-turn cars stay side-by-side without drifting.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: Why must you scan regulatory signs before starting a turn at an unfamiliar corner?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Busy arterials and one-way grids post No Left Turn or No Right Turn restrictions during peak hours or fulltime.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: How close to the right edge should you approach a right turn, and what steering mistake must you avoid?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Swinging left before turning right tricks drivers behind you into squeezing past on your right.
sec13-card-sec13-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Hug right edge; never swing wide

visual_sync.text_span: Hug right edge; never swing wide

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: Where must you come to a complete stop before making a right turn on a red light?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Halt completely ahead of the marked or unmarked crosswalk before creeping forward to check cross-traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: Which specific regulatory sign must you check for before turning right on a red signal?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Missing a No Turn On Red plaque beside the signal head earns an automatic red-light citation.
sec13-card-sec13-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Scan for No Turn On Red

visual_sync.text_span: Scan for No Turn On Red

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: Which three groups hold right-of-way over a driver turning right on red?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Watch not just left-side cross-traffic, also oncoming cars turning left on a protected green arrow.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: Unless signs or markings direct otherwise, which lane must you enter when finishing a right turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Drifting straight across into middle or left lanes cuts off through traffic and opposing left-turners.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: On a two-way street, which lane do you approach a left turn from, and where in the intersection does the turn start?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Starting just left of the intersection's center point keeps two opposing left-turners passing safely in front of each other.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: When completing a left turn onto a two-way road, which lane should you land in and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Finishing in the innermost lane leaves the right curb lane open for oncoming cars turning right simultaneously.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: Where a signed or painted left-turn lane is provided, may you turn left from an adjacent through lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: Turning left from outside a dedicated turn bay broadsides drivers turning legally inside the bay.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: How does a single marked left-turn bay compare with turning from multiple lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Never improvise a second turn lane unless signs and curved arrows explicitly authorize dual turns.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: Which start and finish lanes do you use when turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Hugging left curb to left curb keeps the turn tight without swinging wide across neighboring lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.question_text: Under what exact road combination—after stopping and yielding—is a left turn on red legal in Arizona?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.teaching_text: Turning left on red from or onto a two-way street crosses oncoming lanes and is always illegal.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: How do legal road setups for turning right on red compare with turning left on red?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Right-on-red works on standard streets unless banned, whereas left-on-red applies strictly from one-way onto one-way.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.question_text: Turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street requires which starting and ending lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.teaching_text: Start beside your yellow centerline on the two-way street and land cleanly in the far-left curb lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.question_text: Which lane do you approach in when turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.teaching_text: Because no oncoming traffic uses your one-way street, always set up left turns from the extreme left lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: How does your starting lane for a left turn differ when leaving a two-way street versus a one-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: In both cases you start from the farthest-left legal lane moving your direction—beside yellow or beside the left curb.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: How do the target finish lanes compare between a normal right turn and a left turn onto a one-way street?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Every turn finishes in the nearest legal lane along the curb or centerline you just rounded.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: Into which exact lane must you turn when making a left from a one-way street onto a two-way street?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Landing left of the yellow centerline puts you head-on against opposing traffic, while swinging wide cuts off outer lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: Once you finish turning left onto a two-way road, what two steps precede moving over to the right lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Completing the corner into your nearest lane first keeps your path predictable before signaling a separate lane change.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: Is turning left from a one-way road onto a two-way road ever legal against a red light in Arizona?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Unlike one-way-to-one-way corners, crossing opposing lanes onto a two-way street against red invites a T-bone collision.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: What target-lane rule and red-light restriction govern turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Arizona tests love pairing both halves so you neither drift wide nor treat two-way cross streets like one-way red turns.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: What purpose does the painted middle lane serve along many two-way Arizona streets?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Giving left-turning cars from both directions a dedicated center pocket keeps through lanes flowing smoothly.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: How are the inner and outer yellow lines arranged along each edge of a two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Spotting solid outside and dashed inside tells you immediately that the middle lane is reserved for left turns, not passing.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: Along a shared two-way left-turn lane, which yellow stripe sits next to the center chute and which faces through traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Reversing those two stripes on an exam diagram confuses a shared turn pocket with a reversible or passing lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: Which drivers are legally permitted to occupy a two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Keeping through commuters out of the center chute prevents head-on surprises for drivers setting up turns.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: Which two left-turn maneuvers is a two-way left-turn lane designed to support?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Drivers can either slow safely before turning off the main street or pull into the pocket from a driveway.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: After pulling left from a driveway into a two-way left-turn lane, what merge tactic is strictly prohibited?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Wait inside the pocket for a gap rather than racing down the center chute like a freeway acceleration ramp.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: How does Arizona law treat slowing for a left turn versus overtaking traffic inside a shared center lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Using the center turn pocket to leapfrog slower commuters invites a head-on wreck with an opposing left-turner.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: What communication step is required before steering into a two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Blinking early warns both trailing drivers behind you and opposing drivers eyeing the same center pocket.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: How much of your vehicle belongs inside the two-way left-turn lane once you enter?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Leaving a rear corner hanging out in the through lane clips fast-moving traffic behind you.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: Who else requires close attention whenever you pull into a two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Vehicles from the opposite direction or side driveways can enter the exact same pocket space simultaneously.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: Which three maneuvers must you never perform inside a two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Every foot of forward travel inside a shared center lane without an immediate left turn multiplies head-on crash odds.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: Where in Arizona do Metro light-rail trains operate, and how close is motor vehicle traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Because electric rail cars share surface boulevards right beside automobile lanes, urban drivers interact with tracks constantly.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: Which three street improvements along the Metro corridor help protect pedestrians and discourage jaywalking?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Channeling foot traffic onto timed crossings keeps walkers off live rail beds mid-block.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: What safety upgrade was added at certain school-area crossings along the Metro light-rail route?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Dedicated signals near campuses give students protected phases across busy rail corridors.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: From what kind of lane is a car permitted to turn across Metro light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Signal-phased turn pockets prevent motorists from swinging across live tracks right ahead of a closing train.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: What physical border separates the Metro light-rail trackway from adjacent car lanes?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Raised six-inch curbing keeps distracted motorists from drifting casually onto dedicated rail beds.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: Where are motor vehicles allowed to cross the Metro trackway, and what activates when a train nears?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Special warning signs and signals trigger automatically at controlled intersections whenever a train closes in.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: How do Metro's rules pair turning across the rails with crossing the trackway straight through?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Every legal vehicle path across Valley light rail relies on active signal control rather than guesswork.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: How many access points does each Metro station feature, and how do riders reach them?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Watch for concentrated pedestrian groups stepping into signalized crosswalks at both ends of every station platform.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: How does Metro station platform height compare with the train floor?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Matching platform and car-floor heights lets wheelchairs, strollers, and riders board quickly without stairs.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: How are frontage roads beside Metro tracks controlled, and which heavy vehicles are they engineered to carry?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Expect large delivery rigs and emergency apparatus maneuvering along signalized frontage lanes parallel to the line.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: What safety condition must be met before a Metro light-rail train can pull away from a stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Interlocks keep the train stationary until doors seal, so riders should never pry or block closing panels.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: How are the couplers linking Metro rail cars treated to lower crash injuries?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Cushioning rigid metal hitches helps absorb impact energy if a street collision occurs.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: What triggers the electronic Train Approaching signs mounted at Metro intersections?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Flashing overhead alerts give turning and crossing drivers advance notice before a quiet electric train arrives.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: Why are U-turns permitted at nearly every intersection along the twenty-mile Metro corridor?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Because six-inch trackway curbs block mid-block lefts into businesses, signalized intersection U-turns provide safe access.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: What regulates both left turns and U-turns at light-rail intersections?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Waiting for your dedicated green turn phase prevents turning across silent approaching rail cars.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: How does the flashing Train Approaching sign's job differ from the combined U-turn and left-turn sign?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: One alerts you to an oncoming rail car, while the other designates legal signal-controlled turn movements across tracks.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: What stopping and parking rule applies to both cars and bicycles on light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Trains cannot swerve out of fixed steel rails, turning any paused car or bike into an unavoidable target.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: How must you obey a steady red signal versus a red arrow at a light-rail crossing?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Running a red arrow across parallel tracks puts your side doors square into the path of a passing train.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: At a light-rail junction, what distinguishes a red signal from a red arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Even if through lanes show green, a lit red arrow locks down turning across the trackway.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: What visual check should every driver and cyclist make before crossing light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Double-track lines carry trains from either direction, so scanning both ways catches unexpected approaches.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: May motorists or bicyclists travel along the lane where light-rail trains run?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Treat the curbed rail bed as completely off-limits to private wheels in both directions.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: Because light-rail trains run quietly, which visual and audio cues must you watch and listen for?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Smooth electric motors lack diesel rumble, making active headlight scans and listening essential near crossings.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: Why is relying on engine noise dangerous near light rail, and what replaces it?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: Street traffic easily drowns out electric rail hum until you spot flashing headlamps or hear warning bells.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: Since both ends of a light-rail train look the same, how do its lights show whether it approaches or departs?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Checking lamp color instantly prevents misjudging a closing train as one pulling away from your crossing.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: What do white headlights versus red taillights tell you on a double-ended light-rail car?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Lamp color is your fastest directional cue when identical cab noses offer no front-or-back clue.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: Where must pedestrians avoid walking or standing around light-rail corridors?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Wide train bodies overhang the steel rails slightly, making standing near the track edge hazardous.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: Where and how should pedestrians cross streets carrying light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Signalized crosswalks time pedestrian phases safely around approaching trains and turning cars.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: What shared rule keeps both drivers and pedestrians clear of live light-rail steel?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Whether behind a wheel or on foot, lingering on or beside active urban rails invites disaster.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: What precaution should adults take with young children near tracks and on Metro platforms?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: Toddlers can dart unexpectedly toward flush platform edges before an adult can react.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.question_text: Which three safety steps should children practice anytime they are near light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.teaching_text: Building automatic stop, look, and listen habits protects young walkers from quiet electric trains approaching either way.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.question_text: How should children handle bicycles and skateboards when using a crosswalk near light rail?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.teaching_text: Small skateboard wheels and narrow bike tires can catch inside flanged rail grooves mid-crossing.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: Instead of riding across a light-rail crosswalk, what should kids do with bikes or skateboards?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: Walking wheels across keeps kids upright and alert rather than snagging tires in steel track slots.

sec14-card-sec14-F37.question_text: What rule applies to children playing around light-rail tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F37.teaching_text: Quiet, frequent urban trains leave zero margin for games or distractions anywhere near the trackway.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.question_text: What basic distance reality governs bringing any moving vehicle to a safe, complete stop?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.teaching_text: Respecting how much asphalt vanishes before wheels halt stops drivers from outrunning their forward buffer.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.question_text: Which six human, roadway, and vehicle factors shape your total stopping and braking distance?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.teaching_text: Towing cargo, worn tread, slick asphalt, or extra speed can stretch stopping distance far beyond dry-car estimates.
sec16-card-sec16-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Speed, reaction, road, tires, weight, brakes

visual_sync.text_span: Speed, reaction, road, tires, weight, brakes

sec16-card-sec16-F03.question_text: How does Arizona define perception time, and how many seconds does an average driver take?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.teaching_text: Three quarters of a second ticks by at full highway speed simply while your brain registers trouble ahead.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.question_text: What does reaction time measure, and what is the average driver's figure?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.teaching_text: Even after spotting danger, another zero point seven five seconds passes before your shoe presses the brake pedal.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.question_text: How many seconds on average pass from a roadway threat appearing until braking begins?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.teaching_text: During that one-and-a-half-second pre-braking window, your vehicle rolls forward completely unbraked at its initial speed.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.question_text: How do average perception time and average reaction time combine before your brakes engage?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.teaching_text: Arizona tests both individual zero-point-seven-five figures and their combined one-point-five-second pre-braking total.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.question_text: What practical everyday decision does understanding your vehicle's stopping distance support?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.teaching_text: Matching pace to your true stopping reach ensures you never overdrive blocked curves, traffic, or darkness.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.question_text: Why shouldn't you treat the manual's stopping-distance chart as an exact guarantee for your car?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.teaching_text: Worn pads, aging tires, or dusty asphalt can easily push your real-world roll past textbook chart numbers.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.question_text: What minimum time cushion should you keep behind the vehicle ahead during normal driving?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.teaching_text: Counting three full seconds past a fixed roadside mark gives you time to stop if brake lights flash.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.question_text: To what range should your following gap expand when traffic or visibility grows trickier?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.teaching_text: Adding extra seconds costs almost zero arrival time while multiplying your escape room in heavy or dim conditions.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.question_text: How far should you expand your following gap when pavement turns wet, icy, or slick?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.teaching_text: Six seconds or more gives reduced tire grip enough room to slow smoothly without locking wheels.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.question_text: How does Arizona's standard following-distance floor step up once roads turn slippery?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.teaching_text: Doubling from three seconds to at least six is one of Arizona's highest-yield defensive-driving questions.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.question_text: How does easing your speed help when a trailing driver pulls out to pass you?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.teaching_text: Lifting slightly off the gas gets the passer clear of the oncoming lane faster with room to merge back.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.question_text: Between slowing down and speeding up, which response is right when a vehicle behind moves to overtake?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.teaching_text: Accelerating alongside an overtaking car traps both of you near closing oncoming headlights.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.question_text: How should you adjust your position when a tall semi-trailer ahead blocks your view of the road?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.teaching_text: Widening the gap opens angles past the trailer's edges so brake lights and hazards don't ambush you.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.question_text: How does the crash risk on a quiet, open rural highway compare with busy city streets?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.teaching_text: Higher speeds and relaxed attention on empty stretches turn sudden rural surprises into severe wrecks.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.question_text: Which three hazards commonly ambush drivers along Arizona's rural highways?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.teaching_text: Cresting a blind rise at full highway pace leaves zero room for roaming livestock or flooded low spots.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.question_text: What three habits keep you safe approaching blind curves and hill crests on open country roads?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.teaching_text: Shedding speed before sightlines disappear lets you stop within the pavement you can actually see.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.question_text: Which two driving handicaps almost always strike simultaneously during bad weather?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.teaching_text: Seeing hazards later while needing longer to brake compounds crash risk exponentially at dry-road speeds.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.question_text: How do shifting weather and surface conditions alter your reaction window and vehicle control?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.teaching_text: Slick or gusty shifts demand gentler steering and braking inputs with far less time to recover.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.question_text: What is the number-one rule whenever weather or road conditions deteriorate, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.teaching_text: Dropping speed immediately buys back the sight distance and reaction margin that foul weather steals.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.question_text: During which two daily windows does driving toward the sun create harsh windshield glare?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.teaching_text: Low horizon angles shine straight beneath rooflines into drivers' eyes during commute hours.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.question_text: Which three simple tools or upkeep habits cut down blinding sun glare?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.teaching_text: Dusty or streaked windshields scatter low sunlight into an opaque sheet until cleaned.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.question_text: What hidden danger exists even when the low sun sits comfortably behind your back?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.teaching_text: Approaching motorists staring into that glare can easily miss your car or turn signals.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.question_text: How does the victim of sun glare flip depending on whether the sun sits ahead or behind you?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.teaching_text: Switching on low beams when the sun is behind you helps glare-blinded oncoming drivers spot your silhouette.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.question_text: Which wind direction creates the sharpest steering challenge for drivers?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.teaching_text: Broadside gusts push directly against door panels and fenders, shoving vehicles off their line.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.question_text: Which four vehicle or towing categories suffer the worst instability in strong winds?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.teaching_text: Tall boxy sides act like sails while lightweight cars have less mass resisting lateral gusts.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.question_text: What immediate speed adjustment gives you firmer control in strong wind?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.teaching_text: Lower speeds give you more time to counter sudden gusts before drifting across lane stripes.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.question_text: What happens as your vehicle exits a canyon, bridge cut, or tree line into open terrain?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.teaching_text: Anticipating lateral shoves toward the shoulder or centerline keeps you from overcorrecting in surprise.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.question_text: Where do sudden crosswinds hit hardest, and which two directions can they push your car?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.teaching_text: Gusts emerging past windbreaks can shove you either off the shoulder or across into opposing traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.question_text: What dangerous motion can wind trigger behind a vehicle towing a trailer?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.teaching_text: Side-to-side trailer fishtailing builds rapidly at high speed if gusts catch long side panels.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.question_text: What effect can air turbulence from passing semi-trucks or buses have on your car?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.teaching_text: Bow waves off large rigs shove smaller cars away and then pull them back as the cab passes.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.question_text: What severe folding crash can strong wind currents trigger when pulling a trailer?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.teaching_text: Unchecked sway can whip a trailer sideways around the hitch until tow vehicle and trailer fold.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.question_text: When towing a trailer and a truck or bus overtakes on your left, what three-part sequence keeps the trailer straight?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.teaching_text: Gentle acceleration as the rig clears pulls tension back onto the hitch so the trailer tracks straight.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.question_text: In what exact order do slowing down and gently speeding up occur when a semi passes your trailer?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.teaching_text: Speeding up too early worsens buffeting; wait until the rig passes to apply light stabilizing throttle.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.question_text: Which two effects will you feel when driving straight into a strong headwind?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.teaching_text: Pushing against heavy oncoming wind adds drag on the engine while buffeting the front wheels.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.question_text: How does a strong tailwind change your speed and your braking timing?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.teaching_text: Wind pushing from behind adds momentum that stretches stopping rolls if you brake at normal markers.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.question_text: How do your gas and brake adjustments flip between a strong headwind and a strong tailwind?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.teaching_text: Headwinds resist forward motion while tailwinds silently add speed that requires earlier braking.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.question_text: How severely can an Arizona dust storm cut forward visibility?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.teaching_text: Blowing desert walls can turn bright midday highways completely dark within seconds.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.question_text: What are your very first two moves the moment you encounter a dust storm?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.teaching_text: Checking mirrors before shedding speed prevents getting rear-ended by drivers entering the cloud behind you.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.question_text: Why should you leave the roadway right away rather than pressing deeper into a dust storm?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.teaching_text: Waiting until zero visibility hits makes finding a safe shoulder exit without striking ditches or cars nearly impossible.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.question_text: Should you keep driving through thickening dust until you cannot see, or exit the road early?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.teaching_text: Leaving pavement before brownout conditions peak avoids blind lane changes across invisible traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-F35.question_text: Where exactly must you position and stop your vehicle during a severe dust storm?
sec16-card-sec16-F35.teaching_text: Getting clear past the paved edge puts distance between your parked car and disoriented highway traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-F36.question_text: Which two parts of a highway must you never stop inside during a dust storm?
sec16-card-sec16-F36.teaching_text: Blinded motorists routinely drift onto paved emergency shoulders, triggering deadly multi-vehicle chain-reaction pileups.

sec16-card-sec16-F37.question_text: Once parked completely off the highway in a dust storm, what must you do with your lights and brake pedal?
sec16-card-sec16-F37.teaching_text: Glowing taillights or brake lamps trick blinded drivers behind you into steering straight into your trunk.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.question_text: Combine Arizona's severe dust-storm parking spot with the exact lighting and pedal rule?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.teaching_text: Going dark well past the emergency shoulder stops disoriented trailing cars from following taillights into a wreck.

sec16-card-sec16-F38.question_text: Where should everyone remain while waiting for a dust storm to clear, and how?
sec16-card-sec16-F38.teaching_text: Stepping outside into zero-visibility dust exposes you to disoriented cars, while buckled belts protect against impacts.

sec16-card-sec16-F39.question_text: What weather pairing makes heavy rain extra treacherous during thunderstorms?
sec16-card-sec16-F39.teaching_text: Crosswinds shoving your car across standing water multiply hydroplaning and visibility risks.

sec16-card-sec16-F40.question_text: Which nearby vehicles become toughest to spot during a heavy downpour?
sec16-card-sec16-F40.teaching_text: Road spray and wet side glass blur mirrors, demanding extra careful head checks before lane shifts.

sec16-card-sec16-F41.question_text: Why does Arizona suggest waiting briefly after light rain starts before flicking on windshield wipers?
sec16-card-sec16-F41.teaching_text: Letting a few moments of rain wet dusty glass first prevents blades from smearing mud across your view.

sec16-card-sec16-F42.question_text: To what minimum time gap should you drop back when driving in rain?
sec16-card-sec16-F42.teaching_text: Doubling your dry-road gap to six seconds covers slick wet-pavement braking rolls.

sec16-card-sec16-F43.question_text: Why are the opening thirty minutes of a rainstorm the slickest on Arizona roads?
sec16-card-sec16-F43.teaching_text: Built-up desert oil and road grime float onto fresh rainwater before heavier rain washes them away.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.question_text: What do six seconds and thirty minutes each represent in Arizona rain-driving rules?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.teaching_text: Pair your six-second wet cushion with peak vigilance during the oily opening half hour.

sec16-card-sec16-F44.question_text: At what highway speed can good tires lose all pavement contact on a heavy film of water?
sec16-card-sec16-F44.teaching_text: By fifty miles per hour, water wedges completely beneath tire treads, leaving zero steering or braking bite.

sec16-card-sec16-F45.question_text: Which three tire conditions trigger hydroplaning well below fifty miles per hour?
sec16-card-sec16-F45.teaching_text: Shallow tread grooves and soft pressure cannot channel water out, floating tires even at city speeds.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.question_text: Compare the hydroplaning threshold of healthy tires against worn, bald, or soft tires?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.teaching_text: Even brand-new rubber can plane at fifty, while neglected tires break loose at far slower speeds.

sec16-card-sec16-F46.question_text: What single driver action is the best defense against hydroplaning?
sec16-card-sec16-F46.teaching_text: Shedding speed lets tire grooves press water aside and stay planted against the asphalt.

sec18-card-sec18-F01.question_text: Why should you rehearse an action plan in advance for encountering a wrong-way vehicle?
sec18-card-sec18-F01.teaching_text: Pre-deciding your throttle lift and clear-side escape eliminates fatal hesitation when headlights appear dead ahead.

sec18-card-sec18-F02.question_text: Which four substance categories never mix with driving because they cause crashes, injuries, and death?
sec18-card-sec18-F02.teaching_text: Every chemical category that alters brain chemistry turns routine traffic into a life-or-death hazard.

sec18-card-sec18-F03.question_text: Which two peak human abilities does safe driving demand—and every impairing substance erode?
sec18-card-sec18-F03.teaching_text: Losing sharp judgment makes risky maneuvers look harmless right when physical steering precision is dropping.

sec18-card-sec18-F04.question_text: Beyond illegal substances, which legal doctor-ordered and drugstore remedies can impair your driving?
sec18-card-sec18-F04.teaching_text: Drowsy antihistamines and prescription painkillers slow behind-the-wheel reaction times just as severely as alcohol.

sec18-card-sec18-F05.question_text: What check must you perform on any medication container before getting behind the wheel?
sec18-card-sec18-F05.teaching_text: Checking drowsiness and heavy-machinery warnings upfront prevents discovering dangerous side effects mid-freeway.

sec18-card-sec18-R04.question_text: Why must you read warning labels on non-prescription cold or allergy pills just like prescriptions?
sec18-card-sec18-R04.teaching_text: Buying an allergy box without a doctor's note never guarantees it leaves your reflexes clear.

sec18-card-sec18-F06.question_text: Which three critical driving defenses do alcohol and drugs severely cut down?
sec18-card-sec18-F06.teaching_text: Spotting danger late while hands and feet react sluggishly removes every layer of crash protection.

sec18-card-sec18-F07.question_text: What dangerous mental illusion do alcohol or drugs create even when you feel sober?
sec18-card-sec18-F07.teaching_text: Impairment dulls self-awareness first, fooling buzzed drivers into believing their steering is sharp.

sec18-card-sec18-F08.question_text: Who inside a passenger compartment may drink from or hold an open liquor container on public roads?
sec18-card-sec18-F08.teaching_text: Arizona's open-container ban covers every occupant inside standard cabins, not just the person steering.

sec18-card-sec18-F09.question_text: Riding in which four commercial or living-space vehicles exempts passengers from the open-container ban?
sec18-card-sec18-F09.teaching_text: Hired passenger cabins and RV living quarters exempt riders in back while keeping the driver strictly sober.

sec18-card-sec18-F10.question_text: Which storage spots and coolers count legally as part of the passenger compartment?
sec18-card-sec18-F10.teaching_text: Stashing an unsealed bottle inside an unlocked glovebox or reachable console still triggers an open-container citation.

sec18-card-sec18-F11.question_text: Which two vehicle areas sit legally outside the passenger compartment for transporting unsealed containers?
sec18-card-sec18-F11.teaching_text: SUVs and hatchbacks without trunks must stow resealed bottles all the way behind the rearmost upright seat.

sec18-card-sec18-R02.question_text: Contrast an unlocked reachable console with a trunk or cargo bay under Arizona's open-container law?
sec18-card-sec18-R02.teaching_text: Exam questions test whether an unlocked glovebox shields an open bottle—it never does.

sec18-card-sec18-R03.question_text: Does the bus, taxi, limo, or motorhome open-container exception ever extend to the person driving?
sec18-card-sec18-R03.teaching_text: Even behind the wheel of a party limo or motorhome, the operator remains under total open-container prohibition.

sec18-card-sec18-F12.question_text: What alcohol standard governs every Arizona driver under age twenty-one?
sec18-card-sec18-F12.teaching_text: Arizona allows zero alcohol margin for drivers who have not yet turned twenty-one.

sec18-card-sec18-F13.question_text: Up to how long can your license be suspended on a first conviction for buying or giving liquor to a minor?
sec18-card-sec18-F13.teaching_text: Even without driving anywhere, furnishing alcohol to someone underage puts your own driver license on the line.

sec18-card-sec18-F14.question_text: What maximum license suspension applies after a second or subsequent conviction for supplying liquor to a minor?
sec18-card-sec18-F14.teaching_text: A repeat furnishing conviction multiplies the potential license loss sixfold up to half a year.

sec18-card-sec18-R01.question_text: Compare the license suspension ceilings for a first versus a repeat conviction of giving liquor to a minor?
sec18-card-sec18-R01.teaching_text: Keep thirty days for offense one and six months for repeat offenses sharp for penalty questions.

sec18-card-sec18-F15.question_text: Which age category of drivers is involved in collisions far more frequently than any other?
sec18-card-sec18-F15.teaching_text: Limited behind-the-wheel experience makes teen and young-adult drivers disproportionately vulnerable to costly mistakes.

sec18-card-sec18-F16.question_text: Which age bracket accounts for the highest rate of alcohol involvement in vehicle crashes?
sec18-card-sec18-F16.teaching_text: Crash statistics show alcohol-involved vehicle wrecks peak inside the twenty-one-to-thirty-four age window.

sec18-card-sec18-F17.question_text: According to survey data, which adult age range is most likely to drive after drinking?
sec18-card-sec18-F17.teaching_text: Note the narrower survey bracket—twenty-one to twenty-nine—distinct from the broader thirty-four crash figure.

sec18-card-sec18-R08.question_text: What exact nine-year adult span tops surveys for driving after drinking?
sec18-card-sec18-R08.teaching_text: Exam questions verify that twenty-nine—rather than thirty-four—caps the survey self-report age bracket.

sec18-card-sec18-F18.question_text: How does Arizona classify impaired driving, and in which direction are penalties moving?
sec18-card-sec18-F18.teaching_text: Impaired driving is a serious crime carrying escalating jail, fine, and interlock consequences.

sec18-card-sec18-F19.question_text: What personal rule is the only guaranteed way to avoid alcohol crashes, injuries, fines, and jail?
sec18-card-sec18-F19.teaching_text: Skipping alcohol completely before taking the keys eliminates every risky guesswork miscalculation.

sec18-card-sec18-F20.question_text: What license suspension hits a driver under twenty-one caught with even a trace of an impairing substance?
sec18-card-sec18-F20.teaching_text: Any detectable alcohol, marijuana, impairing medication, or illegal drug costs an underage driver two full years.

sec18-card-sec18-F21.question_text: Does testing below zero point zero eight BAC shield an Arizona driver from a DUI arrest?
sec18-card-sec18-F21.teaching_text: Arizona's slightest-degree law lets officers arrest any driver impaired below zero point zero eight.

sec18-card-sec18-F22.question_text: What do driving studies show about impairment below zero point zero eight BAC?
sec18-card-sec18-F22.teaching_text: Divided attention, tracking, and braking begin slipping after the very first drink.

sec18-card-sec18-R07.question_text: Pair Arizona's under-twenty-one trace penalty with its adult rule below zero point zero eight BAC?
sec18-card-sec18-R07.teaching_text: Minors lose licenses two years for any trace, and adults can still face DUI below point-oh-eight.

sec18-card-sec18-F23.question_text: What combination of speeding, extra violations, and danger defines an aggressive driving citation?
sec18-card-sec18-F23.teaching_text: In one continuous stretch, speeding combined with two listed infractions creating an immediate hazard triggers the charge.

sec18-card-sec18-F24.question_text: Which five specific traffic violations count toward Arizona's aggressive driving offense?
sec18-card-sec18-F24.teaching_text: Blowing controls, passing illegally on the right, cutting lanes, tailgating, or ignoring sirens supply the two extra acts.

sec18-card-sec18-R06.question_text: Can speeding by itself or speeding plus one violation qualify as aggressive driving?
sec18-card-sec18-R06.teaching_text: Test distractors try speeding plus one, whereas the statute demands speeding plus at least two listed violations.

sec18-card-sec18-F25.question_text: What mandatory course and potential suspension follow a first aggressive driving conviction?
sec18-card-sec18-F25.teaching_text: Offense number one mandates Traffic Survival School and opens the door to a thirty-day license suspension.

sec18-card-sec18-F26.question_text: What criminal charge and mandatory suspension hit a second aggressive driving offense within twenty-four months?
sec18-card-sec18-F26.teaching_text: Repeating within two years escalates to a Class one criminal misdemeanor and a full year off the road.

sec18-card-sec18-R05.question_text: Compare the consequences of a first aggressive driving offense with a second inside twenty-four months?
sec18-card-sec18-R05.teaching_text: Going from school and thirty possible days up to a Class one misdemeanor and twelve months is steep.

sec18-card-sec18-F27.question_text: Which four strong emotional states keep a person from driving well?
sec18-card-sec18-F27.teaching_text: Intense moods hijack focus and impulse control whether the feeling is frustration, hype, anxiety, or sadness.

sec18-card-sec18-F28.question_text: Which single emotion hits motorists most frequently, particularly in congested traffic?
sec18-card-sec18-F28.teaching_text: Gridlock frustration sparks anger fast, tempting calm people into tailgating or retaliatory lane cuts.

sec18-card-sec18-F29.question_text: How should you handle driving decisions when strong emotions are running high?
sec18-card-sec18-F29.teaching_text: Taking ten minutes to cool down parked beats letting anger steer a two-ton vehicle.

sec18-card-sec18-F30.question_text: What severe real-world outcomes can distracted driving cause?
sec18-card-sec18-F30.teaching_text: Looking away for even a couple seconds at highway speed covers half a football field blind.

sec18-card-sec18-F31.question_text: What personal factor outweighs every external road or weather hazard you could meet?
sec18-card-sec18-F31.teaching_text: A sharp, healthy driver adapts to storms, whereas poor personal condition turns dry daylight dangerous.

sec18-card-sec18-F32.question_text: Can routine ailments like a simple headache or common cold hurt your safe driving?
sec18-card-sec18-F32.teaching_text: Sneezing fits, watery eyes, and throbbing pain steal attention and milliseconds right when traffic brakes.

sec18-card-sec18-F33.question_text: What two choices should you make if honest self-check shows illness is hurting your fitness to drive?
sec18-card-sec18-F33.teaching_text: Delaying errands or handing keys to a healthy driver beats toughing out fever behind the wheel.

sec18-card-sec18-F34.question_text: Which health conditions must be reported to Arizona's Motor Vehicle Division?
sec18-card-sec18-F34.teaching_text: Self-reporting medical changes lets licensing specialists verify safe control before a blackout crash happens.

sec18-card-sec18-F35.question_text: Within what pre-application timeframe must a license applicant report having had a seizure?
sec18-card-sec18-F35.teaching_text: Any seizure inside the ninety days leading up to an application requires mandatory disclosure.

sec18-card-sec18-F36.question_text: Which three steps apply if an already licensed driver experiences a seizure or impairing medical episode?
sec18-card-sec18-F36.teaching_text: Park immediately, notify the state, and complete a physician evaluation sent directly to licensing officials.

sec18-card-sec18-R09.question_text: Contrast the seizure rule for new license applicants with the rule for drivers who already hold a license?
sec18-card-sec18-R09.teaching_text: Applicants disclose ninety-day history, while current holders halt driving immediately pending medical clearance.

sec18-card-sec18-F37.question_text: What does noticing yourself starting to feel sleepy behind the wheel tell you?
sec18-card-sec18-F37.teaching_text: By the moment yawns and heavy eyelids register consciously, reaction speed has already deteriorated.

sec18-card-sec18-F38.question_text: How does fatigue impair your brain and behind-the-wheel responses?
sec18-card-sec18-F38.teaching_text: Exhausted drivers both misread closing speeds and fumble steering or braking responses.

sec18-card-sec18-F39.question_text: Which five groups carry elevated crash risk from drowsy driving?
sec18-card-sec18-F39.teaching_text: Irregular schedules, long miles, untreated sleep apnea, and young sleep habits all spike fatigue wrecks.

sec18-card-sec18-F40.question_text: How does drowsy driving compare with drunk driving in danger and detectability?
sec18-card-sec18-F40.teaching_text: Exhaustion wrecks vehicles just as violently as alcohol even though no breathalyzer flags sleep debt.

sec18-card-sec18-F41.question_text: What is the single safe cure for driver fatigue?
sec18-card-sec18-F41.teaching_text: Caffeine and cold air only mask sleepiness briefly; genuine sleep is the sole cure.

sec18-card-sec18-F42.question_text: Which two planning habits prevent fatigue before a long road trip?
sec18-card-sec18-F42.teaching_text: Starting rested during normal waking hours avoids battling your body's natural circadian dip.

sec18-card-sec18-F43.question_text: What should you do during frequent road-trip rest stops to recharge alertness?
sec18-card-sec18-F43.teaching_text: Getting out to walk and breathe deeply clears cabin sluggishness far better than sitting parked.

sec18-card-sec18-F44.question_text: How do you prevent locking into a hypnotic fixed forward stare while driving?
sec18-card-sec18-F44.teaching_text: Moving your gaze regularly between far horizon, side mirrors, and dash instruments keeps visual cortex active.

sec18-card-sec18-F45.question_text: Which four simple habits help keep drivers engaged between rest stops?
sec18-card-sec18-F45.teaching_text: Cracking windows, singing along, chewing gum, and rotating drivers stave off monotony before tiredness hits.

sec18-card-sec18-R11.question_text: How do fresh air, music, gum, and stretch breaks differ from genuine rest?
sec18-card-sec18-R11.teaching_text: Exam questions love testing that alertness tricks help prevent drowsiness, whereas true fatigue requires sleep.

sec18-card-sec18-F46.question_text: What two outcomes define Arizona's Driver Improvement program for irresponsible motorists?
sec18-card-sec18-F46.teaching_text: Identifying problem records early lets the state retrain unsafe habits or pull licenses before fatal wrecks.

sec18-card-sec18-F47.question_text: What is license revocation, and when does Arizona law mandate it?
sec18-card-sec18-F47.teaching_text: Unlike a temporary suspension, revocation terminates your driving privilege following serious statutory convictions.

sec18-card-sec18-F48.question_text: Does your right to drive return automatically the day a revocation period expires?
sec18-card-sec18-F48.teaching_text: Driving the morning after your calendar date without official clearance and reinstatement is still driving revoked.

sec18-card-sec18-F49.question_text: Which two fees and potential insurance filing are required to reinstate after revocation?
sec18-card-sec18-F49.teaching_text: Expect both the license application fee and twenty-dollar reinstatement fee, plus high-risk SR-twenty-two proof.

sec18-card-sec18-F50.question_text: Which three exams can Arizona require you to pass again when reinstating from revocation?
sec18-card-sec18-F50.teaching_text: Because revocation cancels your former license completely, officials can retest knowledge, sight, and driving.

sec18-card-sec18-R10.question_text: Pair the investigation rule with the exact fee structure required after a revocation period ends?
sec18-card-sec18-R10.teaching_text: Both clean investigation clearance and paying the application plus twenty-dollar reinstatement fee precede legal driving.

sec20-card-sec20-F01.question_text: Beyond losing your driving privilege, what two criminal penalties can underage false-ID nitrous oxide offenses carry?
sec20-card-sec20-F01.teaching_text: Using fake ID to obtain nitrous oxide doesn't stop at MVD suspension—courts can add fines or jail time.

sec20-card-sec20-F02.question_text: Where is nitrous oxide legitimately used, and what severe risks come from abusing it?
sec20-card-sec20-F02.teaching_text: Doctors and dentists use laughing gas safely as anesthesia, whereas recreational abuse becomes addictive and causes severe harm or death.

sec20-card-sec20-F03.question_text: How long is your Arizona driving privilege suspended for a first nitrous oxide offense?
sec20-card-sec20-F03.teaching_text: A first false-ID nitrous oxide conviction sidelines your Arizona driving privilege for six full months.

sec20-card-sec20-F04.question_text: How long is your Arizona driving privilege suspended for a second or later nitrous oxide offense?
sec20-card-sec20-F04.teaching_text: Picking up a second or subsequent nitrous oxide conviction doubles the license suspension to twelve months.

sec20-card-sec20-R03.question_text: How does the suspension length jump from a first nitrous oxide offense to a repeat offense?
sec20-card-sec20-R03.teaching_text: Nitrous oxide suspensions double cleanly—six months on your first conviction and twelve months on any repeat.

sec20-card-sec20-F05.question_text: Which five invalid or fake card statuses make displaying a driver license unlawful?
sec20-card-sec20-F05.teaching_text: Showing any license you know is canceled, revoked, suspended, fake, or tampered with breaks Arizona law.

sec20-card-sec20-F06.question_text: What mandatory and possible penalties follow altering a driver license or obtaining a false one?
sec20-card-sec20-F06.teaching_text: Tampering with a real license or getting a counterfeit one suspends your privilege and risks court fines or jail.

sec20-card-sec20-F07.question_text: Under the influence of alcohol, marijuana, medications, or illegal drugs, what two vehicle roles are forbidden?
sec20-card-sec20-F07.teaching_text: Even sitting behind the wheel in actual physical control while impaired—including prescription meds or marijuana—is illegal.

sec20-card-sec20-F08.question_text: What chemical-testing agreement do you accept automatically under Arizona's Implied Consent Law?
sec20-card-sec20-F08.teaching_text: Applying for and holding an Arizona driving privilege pre-agrees to alcohol and drug testing if arrested for DUI.

sec20-card-sec20-F09.question_text: Which four types of bodily samples can an officer request when DUI is suspected?
sec20-card-sec20-F09.teaching_text: Arizona officers aren't limited to breathalyzers—reasonable DUI grounds cover blood, breath, urine, or other bodily tests.

sec20-card-sec20-F10.question_text: At what blood-alcohol concentration do ordinary adult drivers lose their Arizona privilege on the spot?
sec20-card-sec20-F10.teaching_text: Testing at zero point zero eight percent or higher triggers immediate roadside loss of your driving privilege.

sec20-card-sec20-F11.question_text: At what alcohol concentration does someone driving a commercial vehicle requiring a CDL lose driving privileges on the spot?
sec20-card-sec20-F11.teaching_text: Operating a CDL-class rig cuts the threshold in half—zero point zero four costs privileges immediately.

sec20-card-sec20-F13.question_text: What alcohol concentration can suspend the license of a driver under twenty-one in Arizona?
sec20-card-sec20-F13.teaching_text: Arizona enforces total zero tolerance—any alcohol concentration whatsoever can suspend an under-twenty-one driver's license.

sec20-card-sec20-R01.question_text: How do Arizona's alcohol cutoffs compare across ordinary drivers, commercial-vehicle drivers, and drivers under twenty-one?
sec20-card-sec20-R01.teaching_text: Keep all three tiers crisp—point zero eight standard, point zero four in CDL vehicles, and any trace under twenty-one.

sec20-card-sec20-F12.question_text: Can an Arizona court convict you of driving while intoxicated if your BAC measured below zero point zero eight percent?
sec20-card-sec20-F12.teaching_text: Arizona prosecutes impairment to the slightest degree—blowing under point zero eight never shields an impaired driver from conviction.

sec20-card-sec20-R04.question_text: Why isn't a BAC reading below zero point zero eight percent a legal defense to driving while intoxicated?
sec20-card-sec20-R04.teaching_text: Point zero eight triggers automatic per-se loss, yet any noticeable impairment below that mark still supports a guilty verdict.

sec20-card-sec20-F14.question_text: What automatic suspension hits a first DUI test refusal versus a second refusal within eighty-four months?
sec20-card-sec20-F14.teaching_text: Refusing or failing to finish post-arrest tests automatically suspends twelve months first, or twenty-four months inside eighty-four months.

sec20-card-sec20-R02.question_text: Across an eighty-four-month window, how do first and second DUI test-refusal suspensions compare?
sec20-card-sec20-R02.teaching_text: Eighty-four months equals seven years—a second refusal in that span doubles automatic loss from twelve to twenty-four months.

sec20-card-sec20-F15.question_text: Alongside criminal court sentences, what happens automatically to your license on a second or third DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F15.teaching_text: Repeat DUI convictions automatically revoke your driving privilege on top of every jail day and court fine.

sec20-card-sec20-F16.question_text: What is the minimum consecutive jail sentence for a first ordinary DUI in Arizona?
sec20-card-sec20-F16.teaching_text: Even a first-time standard DUI carries a mandatory minimum of ten straight days behind bars.

sec20-card-sec20-F17.question_text: What minimum license suspension and minimum dollar fine apply to a first ordinary DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F17.teaching_text: First-offense DUI suspends your license at least ninety days and starts fines at twelve hundred fifty dollars.

sec20-card-sec20-F18.question_text: Beyond jail, fine, and suspension, what classes, service, and optional device accompany a first ordinary DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F18.teaching_text: Offenders must complete alcohol screening, education/treatment or psychotherapy, plus community service—and judges may order an interlock.

sec20-card-sec20-F19.question_text: What minimum jail time, minimum fine, and license revocation hit a second or later ordinary DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F19.teaching_text: A second standard DUI jumps to ninety days minimum jail, three thousand dollars minimum fine, and twelve-month revocation.

sec20-card-sec20-F20.question_text: Besides jail, fine, and revocation, what rehabilitation, service, and device provisions apply to a repeat ordinary DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F20.teaching_text: Repeat offenders still owe mandatory substance screening, counseling or therapy coursework, and community service—plus a judge-ordered interlock remains possible.

sec20-card-sec20-R05.question_text: How do minimum jail time and license loss escalate from a first ordinary DUI to a second DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-R05.teaching_text: Jail multiplies ninefold from ten days to ninety days while ninety-day suspension turns into twelve-month revocation.

sec20-card-sec20-F21.question_text: At what blood-alcohol concentration does an offense cross into Arizona's Extreme DUI category?
sec20-card-sec20-F21.teaching_text: Nearly double the standard point-oh-eight limit—zero point one five or above triggers harsh Extreme DUI penalties.

sec20-card-sec20-F22.question_text: What minimum consecutive jail time and minimum fine hit a first Extreme DUI at point one five?
sec20-card-sec20-F22.teaching_text: A first Extreme DUI triples base jail to thirty straight days and doubles the base fine to twenty-five hundred dollars.

sec20-card-sec20-F23.question_text: If a first Extreme DUI reaches zero point two zero or higher, what jail floor and sentencing rule apply?
sec20-card-sec20-F23.teaching_text: Blowing point two zero or higher on a first offense locks in forty-five jail days with suspended sentences barred.

sec20-card-sec20-F24.question_text: Along with treatment and service, what vehicle device is mandatory after even a first Extreme DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F24.teaching_text: Unlike ordinary first DUI where interlocks are discretionary, a first Extreme DUI mandates a Certified Ignition Interlock Device.

sec20-card-sec20-F25.question_text: What minimum fine and license loss apply to a second or later Extreme DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F25.teaching_text: Repeat Extreme DUI pushes the minimum fine to three thousand two hundred fifty dollars alongside a one-year revocation.

sec20-card-sec20-F26.question_text: What minimum jail term and sentencing restriction apply to a repeat Extreme DUI at zero point two zero or higher?
sec20-card-sec20-F26.teaching_text: A repeat offense at point two zero or above mandates at least one hundred eighty jail days without sentence suspension.

sec20-card-sec20-F27.question_text: Besides jail, fine, and revocation, what four program, device, and service items accompany a repeat Extreme DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F27.teaching_text: Every repeat Extreme DUI requires alcohol screening, education or treatment, a mandatory ignition interlock, and community service.

sec20-card-sec20-R07.question_text: Where does Extreme DUI start, and how does the point-two-zero sub-tier raise mandatory jail on first and repeat offenses?
sec20-card-sec20-R07.teaching_text: Extreme starts at point one five, while point two zero locks in forty-five first-offense or one-eighty repeat jail days unsuspended.

sec20-card-sec20-R06.question_text: In ascending dollar order, what are the minimum fines for first DUI, first Extreme, second DUI, and second Extreme?
sec20-card-sec20-R06.teaching_text: Watch the clean stair-step—twelve fifty first, twenty-five hundred first Extreme, three thousand second, and thirty-two fifty second Extreme.

sec20-card-sec20-R08.question_text: How does the ignition-interlock rule on an ordinary first DUI differ from a first Extreme DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-R08.teaching_text: Judges have discretion on an ordinary first DUI, whereas a first Extreme DUI makes the certified interlock mandatory.

sec20-card-sec20-F28.question_text: Which three license, repeat-count, or passenger situations turn a DUI into Aggravated DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F28.teaching_text: Driving impaired while suspended/revoked, catching a third DUI in seven years, or carrying anyone under fifteen triggers felony Aggravated DUI.

sec20-card-sec20-F29.question_text: What DUI charge applies if someone already under a Certified Ignition Interlock order commits another DUI or Extreme DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F29.teaching_text: Catching a new DUI or Extreme DUI while already subject to a mandatory interlock automatically elevates to Aggravated DUI.

sec20-card-sec20-F30.question_text: What prison exposure and license revocation come with an Aggravated DUI conviction?
sec20-card-sec20-F30.teaching_text: Aggravated DUI shifts punishment from county jail to state prison for up to two years plus one-year revocation.

sec20-card-sec20-F31.question_text: Alongside prison and revocation, what treatment and vehicle requirements follow Aggravated DUI?
sec20-card-sec20-F31.teaching_text: Convicted drivers must complete alcohol screening, education, treatment or psychotherapy, and equip any driven car with an interlock.

sec20-card-sec20-R09.question_text: What felony tier and prison cap unite a third DUI within seven years and a DUI carrying a child under fifteen?
sec20-card-sec20-R09.teaching_text: Both scenarios cross straight into Aggravated DUI, exposing the driver to state prison for up to two years.

sec20-card-sec20-F32.question_text: What is a Certified Ignition Interlock Device and what vehicle systems does it connect into?
sec20-card-sec20-F32.teaching_text: A handheld alcohol breath analyzer wires directly into your starter and electrical system to gate engine operation.

sec20-card-sec20-F33.question_text: What must you do before turning the key on an interlock-equipped car, and when does it block starting?
sec20-card-sec20-F33.teaching_text: You provide a breath sample before cranking, and the starter stays locked whenever breath alcohol exceeds the preset limit.

sec20-card-sec20-F34.question_text: Does ignition-interlock testing end once the engine starts, or when else must you blow?
sec20-card-sec20-F34.teaching_text: Preventing sober-friend workarounds or mid-drive drinking requires drivers to blow again at random intervals while running.

sec20-card-sec20-R10.question_text: At which two stages of a trip does a Certified Ignition Interlock Device require breath samples?
sec20-card-sec20-R10.teaching_text: Expect breath prompts twice—first to unlock the starter, then randomly along your drive while the engine runs.

sec20-card-sec20-F35.question_text: How soon into most DUI-related Class D or Class G suspensions or revocations can eligible drivers apply for a Special Ignition Interlock Restricted License?
sec20-card-sec20-F35.teaching_text: For most listed DUI suspensions or revocations, Arizona allows applying on day one for a special interlock-restricted credential.

sec20-card-sec20-F36.question_text: Which three ongoing rules bind someone driving on a Special Ignition Interlock Restricted Driver License?
sec20-card-sec20-F36.teaching_text: Keeping that restricted privilege demands strict interlock compliance, completing alcohol treatment classes, and carrying future financial-responsibility proof.

sec20-card-sec20-F37.question_text: Which MVD division conducts hearings when individuals or businesses contest an MVD order?
sec20-card-sec20-F37.teaching_text: Whenever a person or business formally disputes an administrative MVD order, the Executive Hearing Office runs the hearing.

sec20-card-sec20-F38.question_text: What type of MVD action makes up the bulk of Executive Hearing Office cases?
sec20-card-sec20-F38.teaching_text: Traffic-violation orders suspending or revoking a driver license account for the vast majority of Executive Hearing Office dockets.

sec20-card-sec20-R11.question_text: What is the core role of Arizona's Executive Hearing Office, and which orders dominate its calendar?
sec20-card-sec20-R11.teaching_text: It reviews contested MVD administrative orders, led overwhelmingly by appeals of driver-license suspensions and revocations.

sec17-card-sec17-F01.question_text: What must your right foot do with the gas and brake pedals the instant your tires hydroplane?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.teaching_text: Slamming brakes while riding a water wedge locks floating wheels so they spin sideways once rubber touches pavement.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.question_text: How should you manage the steering wheel while your tires are hydroplaning?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.teaching_text: Turning front wheels while planing points your car sideways the moment front tread regains bite.

sec17-card-sec17-F03.question_text: What sudden water hazard does heavy rain routinely trigger across Arizona desert washes?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.teaching_text: Dry low-water crossings can fill with raging runoff within minutes even from storms miles upstream.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.question_text: Which three dangers explain why you must never drive into a flooded Arizona wash?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.teaching_text: Shallow-looking current hides washed-out asphalt holes, drowns air intakes, and floats two-ton cars downstream.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.question_text: How can you estimate the depth of water standing on a roadway?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.teaching_text: Comparing water height against curbs, parked tires, and cautious traffic beats guessing blindly from behind your hood.

sec17-card-sec17-F06.question_text: How should two oncoming drivers coordinate crossing deep standing water, and why?
sec17-card-sec17-F06.teaching_text: Meeting mid-puddle pushes opposing bow waves straight up into engines, stalling one or both vehicles.

sec17-card-sec17-F07.question_text: What financial consequence can follow if rescuers have to pull you or your car from a flooded road?
sec17-card-sec17-F07.teaching_text: Swift-water rescues risk first responders' lives and expensive gear, exposing stranded motorists to recovery bills.

sec17-card-sec17-F12.question_text: What legal liability hits an Arizona driver who drives around flood barricades and gets stranded?
sec17-card-sec17-F12.teaching_text: Bypassing posted road-closed signs triggers strict statutory liability when your swamped car strands occupants.

sec17-card-sec17-F13.question_text: How does Arizona define the emergency-response expenses billed after a flood rescue?
sec17-card-sec17-F13.teaching_text: Every police, fire, or helicopter agency called out tallies its reasonable direct expenses for the rescue.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.question_text: How does general flood-rescue billing compare with bypassing a posted flood barricade?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.teaching_text: Any flooded-road extraction can bring charges, whereas driving around barricades locks in legal liability.

sec17-card-sec17-F08.question_text: How should you manage your speed whenever you must drive through shallow standing water?
sec17-card-sec17-F08.teaching_text: Charging fast splashes water over ignition parts and lifts tires off the pavement.

sec17-card-sec17-F09.question_text: What pedal technique while rolling through water can help keep brake linings dry?
sec17-card-sec17-F09.teaching_text: Gentle friction warms rotors and drums slightly so water sheds instead of soaking pads.

sec17-card-sec17-F10.question_text: Why must you test your brakes right after driving out of standing water?
sec17-card-sec17-F10.teaching_text: Unevenly soaked linings can yank your steering sideways during your next real stop unless checked first.

sec17-card-sec17-F11.question_text: How do you safely dry wet brakes once your wheels are back on dry pavement?
sec17-card-sec17-F11.teaching_text: Brief, light brake drag against slow acceleration heats the pads enough to evaporate trapped moisture.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.question_text: Contrast your brake-pedal rule during hydroplaning with your brake routine after exiting deep puddles?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.teaching_text: Touching brakes mid-hydroplane causes spins, while gentle dragging afterward restores crisp dry stopping.

sec17-card-sec17-F14.question_text: What optical problem do suspended fog droplets create with your own headlights?
sec17-card-sec17-F14.teaching_text: Airborne moisture acts like millions of tiny mirrors, turning upward high-beam light into blinding white glare.

sec17-card-sec17-F15.question_text: Which headlight setting and pavement reference keep you aligned in fog?
sec17-card-sec17-F15.teaching_text: Low beams angle beneath the fog bank while right-edge paint keeps you clear of oncoming traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-F16.question_text: Why does even thin, light fog demand an immediate speed reduction?
sec17-card-sec17-F16.teaching_text: Haze softens contrast so stalled cars and curves sit much closer than your eyes estimate.

sec17-card-sec17-F17.question_text: Why must you keep adjusting speed continuously when driving through fog?
sec17-card-sec17-F17.teaching_text: Rolling from thin mist into a dense pocket can erase sightlines instantly, demanding readiness for sudden stops.

sec17-card-sec17-F18.question_text: What three steps apply when fog grows too dense to continue safely?
sec17-card-sec17-F18.teaching_text: Switching headlights off once safely clear of pavement stops trailing fog-blinded drivers from following your lamps off-road.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.question_text: How does your headlight setting in fog change between driving on the road and waiting off-road?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.teaching_text: Just like Arizona dust storms, moving requires low beams while waiting off-road requires dark lamps.

sec17-card-sec17-F19.question_text: What dual visibility purpose do headlights serve during falling snow?
sec17-card-sec17-F19.teaching_text: White flakes camouflage silver and white cars rapidly unless low beams and taillights glow.

sec17-card-sec17-F20.question_text: How does snow-covered pavement change lane positioning and oncoming clearance?
sec17-card-sec17-F20.teaching_text: Shying away from buried shoulders pushes opposing streams dangerously close near the road center.

sec17-card-sec17-F21.question_text: In the Arizona manual's phrasing, how much does snow or ice add to your needed stopping distance?
sec17-card-sec17-F21.teaching_text: Frozen layers slash tire friction so severely that normal dry-pavement gaps become guaranteed rear-end hits.

sec17-card-sec17-F22.question_text: On slick snow or ice, why does your car respond better to steering than to hard braking?
sec17-card-sec17-F22.teaching_text: Front tires must keep turning freely to steer around trouble; skidding locked rubber slides straight ahead.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.question_text: What tire condition preserves maximum control on slippery surfaces, favoring steering over braking?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.teaching_text: Keeping front treads rolling maintains directional control when icy stopping distances run too long.

sec17-card-sec17-F23.question_text: How should you apply brake pressure when slowing down on ice or slick pavement?
sec17-card-sec17-F23.teaching_text: Progressive squeezing lets weight settle onto the front tires without snapping thin traction.

sec17-card-sec17-F24.question_text: What braking mistake must you never commit on a slippery surface?
sec17-card-sec17-F24.teaching_text: Locked non-rotating tires lose all steering authority and slide like hockey pucks.

sec17-card-sec17-F25.question_text: If your wheels lock up on slick pavement, what pedal cycle restores rolling grip?
sec17-card-sec17-F25.teaching_text: Backing off slightly without lifting completely lets tires rotate freely before reapplying gentle pedal pressure.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.question_text: When tires lock on ice, do you yank your foot completely off the brake or ease off slightly?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.teaching_text: Small controlled pedal modulations recover smooth tire rotation without unsettling your car's icy balance.

sec17-card-sec17-F26.question_text: Which two abrupt driver inputs must you avoid during winter driving?
sec17-card-sec17-F26.teaching_text: Jerky throttle stabs or sharp wheel yanks break fragile cold-weather traction instantly.

sec17-card-sec17-F27.question_text: What must you clear completely off your vehicle before pulling out in winter?
sec17-card-sec17-F27.teaching_text: Driving through a tiny scraped peephole blinds side scans and hides brake lights under crusted snow.

sec17-card-sec17-F28.question_text: Which two benefits do snow tires or tire chains provide on winter roads?
sec17-card-sec17-F28.teaching_text: Biting winter tread compounds and metal links dig into snowpack where summer rubber polishes smooth.

sec17-card-sec17-F29.question_text: What surface does packed snow mimic, and when must you shed speed on it?
sec17-card-sec17-F29.teaching_text: Compressed tire tracks polish quickly into near-ice, punishing anyone who waits until mid-corner to brake.

sec17-card-sec17-F30.question_text: Which two roadway spots ice over earliest, and why do bridges freeze ahead of regular pavement?
sec17-card-sec17-F30.teaching_text: Cold air circulates both above and beneath elevated bridge decks while ground warmth insulates regular roads.

sec17-card-sec17-R09.question_text: Pair Arizona's rule on early-freezing spots with how to treat hard-packed snow?
sec17-card-sec17-R09.teaching_text: High-country trips around Flagstaff test both black-ice bridge awareness and treating packed snow like glaze.

sec17-card-sec17-F31.question_text: During which daytime hazards should you switch on low-beam headlights?
sec17-card-sec17-F31.teaching_text: Daytime low beams make your grille and taillights pop out of desert dust, monsoon spray, or sun glare.

sec17-card-sec17-F32.question_text: How do daytime headlights protect you along open two-lane rural highways?
sec17-card-sec17-F32.teaching_text: Bright headlamps warn distant drivers before they pull into your lane against heat shimmer.

sec17-card-sec17-F33.question_text: Which three visual challenges combine to make nighttime driving hazardous?
sec17-card-sec17-F33.teaching_text: Shrinking sightlines meet blinding opposing lamps right where unlit debris or pedestrians lurk.

sec17-card-sec17-F35.question_text: Between which daily sun markers are headlights legally mandatory, and what caution remains?
sec17-card-sec17-F35.teaching_text: Even during mandatory dark hours, stay alert for forgetful drivers cruising on daytime running lamps or dark hoods.

sec17-card-sec17-R08.question_text: Should you switch on parking lights or full headlights at dusk, and when does the legal mandate run?
