sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Circling three-quarters or all the way around the central island makes U-turns seamless.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: Where in Arizona road networks are diverging diamond interchanges used?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Busy overpass and underpass junctions use diverging diamonds to move heavy ramp volume.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: What unusual lane shift happens to cross-street traffic inside a diverging diamond interchange, and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Crossing temporarily to the left side eliminates left-turn conflicts across opposing lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: Which three standard road guides steer you cleanly through a diverging diamond?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Channelized curbs, arrows, and lights guide you naturally without memorizing complex geometry.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Why doesn't driving briefly on the left inside a diverging diamond require special new maneuvers?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Obeying everyday signals, overhead signs, and lane lines carries you onto the left and back.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: At what exact traffic control feature do the right-to-left and left-to-right crossovers happen in a diverging diamond?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Signalized X-crossings alternate opposing streams safely as you enter and leave the bridge.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: What missing signal phase makes traffic lights simpler inside a diverging diamond?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Eliminating dedicated left-turn arrow phases cuts intersection red-light waiting time in half for everyone.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: Once past the crossover in a diverging diamond, how do drivers turn left onto freeway on-ramps?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Already riding on the left side lets ramp traffic slip directly onto the on-ramp unimpeded.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: Connect where traffic swaps sides in a diverging diamond with how on-ramp left turns work afterward?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Crossing at the traffic light puts the left on-ramp right beside you with zero oncoming cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: Which three problems — involving traffic, sightlines, and legality — must you avoid when parking on a public road?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Parking where you hide a stop sign or pinch a travel lane draws tickets and crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Where does the international symbol of access appear, and what spaces does it reserve?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Matching reserved signs with authorized plates or placards keeps wide ramp spaces open.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: May you park in an accessible stall using a valid family placard when the person it belongs to stayed home?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Accessible parking privileges travel with the issued individual, never the empty car.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: What legal consequence hits anyone who parks unlawfully in a reserved accessible space?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Even quick two-minute errands in blue-marked stalls violate Arizona law and draw fines.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: What fundamental visibility limitation makes backing up a dangerous maneuver?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: High trunk lids and rear pillars hide low objects right behind your bumper.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: What physical check belongs before climbing into the driver's seat to back out — and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Toddlers, pets, and bikes sit below rear glass height where driver-seat views miss them.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: Where must you physically turn and look while backing — instead of relying on mirrors or cameras?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Tiny backup camera lenses miss pedestrians and cross-traffic approaching from wide side angles.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: Put Arizona's pre-entry check and in-seat gaze together for safe reversing?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: Walking behind catches low obstacles before turning over your shoulder tracks live movement.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: At what pace should you always move a vehicle in reverse?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Front-wheel steering swings the nose wide in reverse, making fast backing unstable.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: What traffic check continues throughout parallel parking, and which two skills are the key to nailing it?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Creeping slowly gives your hands time to shape angles while watching passing cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: What two actions kick off step one of parallel parking before you stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Alerting the driver behind you prevents them from pulling too close to let you reverse.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: How do you align your rear bumper and side gap beside the forward car before backing in?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Starting even at a two-foot side gap sets the geometry to clear their rear fender.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: In which direction is Arizona's 'about two feet' parallel-parking setup distance measured?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Stopping two feet alongside the forward parked car keeps mirrors safe as your nose swings out.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: Once in reverse looking over your right shoulder, which way do you turn the steering wheel first?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Turning sharply right angles your rear tires cleanly toward the open curb pocket.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.question_text: At what exact clearance point while parallel parking do you swing the wheel sharply left?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.teaching_text: Waiting until your front bumper clears their back bumper tucks your nose inside without scraping.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: Keep the two sharp steering turns of parallel parking in the right sequence?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Right angles the tail in; left swings the nose parallel once bumpers clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.question_text: Which two final touches finish a clean parallel-parking maneuver?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.teaching_text: Centering inside the space leaves room for parked neighbors ahead and behind to leave.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.question_text: Which way do your front wheels point — and what brake step applies — when parked downhill beside a curb?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.teaching_text: Angling right into the concrete curb blocks forward roll if the parking brake slips.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.question_text: How do you turn and rest your front wheels before setting the brake when parked uphill beside a curb?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.teaching_text: Turning away from the curb lets the back of your right front tire hook the concrete.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.question_text: Uphill or downhill on a road with NO curb, which direction must your front wheels point — and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.teaching_text: Without a concrete lip to catch a tire, pointing right steers any runaway roll off the road.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: Compare front-wheel direction across all three hill cases — downhill curb, uphill curb, and curbless?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Every hill turns right toward the edge EXCEPT uphill WITH a curb, which turns left.
sec07-card-sec07-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Only uphill with curb goes left

visual_sync.text_span: Only uphill with curb goes left

sec07-card-sec07-F42.question_text: Regardless of wheel angle or slope direction, what step applies every time you park on a grade?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.teaching_text: Relying on transmission park pawls alone stresses drivetrains and risks runaway hill rollaways.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: How should you handle a pedestrian-activated crosswalk beacon when all of its lights are dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Unlike a blacked-out intersection traffic signal, a pedestrian HAWK beacon stays intentionally dark until someone presses its button.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Why can someone walking at night, dusk, dawn, or in storms spot an approaching car long before its driver sees them?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Glowing headlamps stand out blocks away while dark pedestrian clothing blends invisibly into wet asphalt and shadows.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What dangerous assumption must a pedestrian never make when a vehicle is approaching?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Glare, A-pillars, or cabin distraction can hide a walker even under a bright streetlight.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: Which two roadway locations should pedestrians choose when crossing a street?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Drivers scan corners and painted walkways far more actively than mid-block gaps between parked cars.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: What visual connection should a pedestrian try to establish with approaching drivers before crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Catching the driver's gaze through the windshield confirms they actually noticed you and are braking.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Why must a pedestrian still look both ways before stepping into a marked crosswalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Physics prevents a two-ton vehicle from stopping on a dime if someone darts off the curb late.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: Which three personal electronics should pedestrians put away or uncover while crossing streets?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Staring at a screen with plugged ears blocks screeching tires, horns, and turning engines.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: What lighting choice and legal duty keep pedestrians safer when crossing streets at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Crossing beneath overhead streetlamps while obeying walk signals gives drivers critical extra yards to spot you.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a stop when pulling out of a driveway or alley?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Rolling straight to the curb cuts across joggers, kids on scooters, and walkers hidden by hedges.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: Once you have stopped before the sidewalk at a driveway or alley, whom must you yield to next?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Check the sidewalk in both directions first, then wait for a clean gap in street traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: How does pulling out of an alley or driveway differ from making a left turn on the road?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Driveway exits demand a full pre-sidewalk stop before yielding, whereas left turns yield without a mandatory stop if clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: Which three oncoming or crossing road users hold priority over a driver turning left?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Drivers scanning only for oncoming cars frequently miss fast through-cyclists or walkers in the far crosswalk.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: What three conditions must all be met before making a U-turn in Arizona?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Even without a No U-Turn sign, swinging around blindly on a hill or forcing cars to brake is illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: Which three factors each make a U-turn illegal on an Arizona roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Failing any one of those three checks—posted sign, clear sight, or smooth traffic clearance—voids the U-turn.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: How must you handle approaching traffic when completing an allowed U-turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: A tight 180-degree arc takes longer than a normal turn, so wait for an extra-wide traffic gap.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: Which court program might a civil red-light ticket let you attend, and where are your options listed?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Reading the court enclosure promptly matters because Defensive Driving eligibility must be completed before your court deadline.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: After receiving a civil traffic or red-light citation, how do you find out if Defensive Driving applies?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Officers attach written court instructions explaining whether school diversion can resolve your civil violation.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Which mandatory course must you complete if convicted of running a steady red or flashing red signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Unlike optional pre-conviction Defensive Driving, a entered red-light conviction brings mandatory Traffic Survival School.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: What happens once you successfully complete Traffic Survival School for a red-light conviction?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: The school transmits your completion straight to MVD, closing the requirement without another courtroom trip.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: Does MVD have discretion to waive Traffic Survival School when a court reports a red-light conviction?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: State statute makes the Traffic Survival School order automatic on every court-reported red-light conviction.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Which agency orders Traffic Survival School after a red-light conviction, and what happens if you ignore it?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Ignoring that MVD letter freezes your license indefinitely until you complete the class and reinstate.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: Alongside mandatory school, what does a red-light conviction place on your Arizona driving record?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Accumulating too many violation points within twelve months can trigger separate MVD suspension action.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: Legally, what does simply mailing in or paying a red-light fine count as?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Many drivers pay a ticket expecting it to vanish, only to receive MVD points and a school order.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: Why doesn't paying a red-light fine quietly keep the ticket off your MVD record?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Only completing pre-conviction Defensive Driving avoids points—paying the fine enters a full conviction.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: What happens to your driving privilege if you fail to finish ordered Traffic Survival School?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: An indefinite suspension stays active with no expiration date until you finish the course.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: How do maximum fines and license suspensions escalate between a life-threatening injury red-light crash and a fatal one?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Causing death doubles both the fine ceiling from five hundred to one thousand dollars and suspension from three to six months.
sec10-card-sec10-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Injury five-hundred three-months; death thousand six

visual_sync.text_span: Injury five-hundred three-months; death thousand six

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: What three penalties can follow causing a crash that kills another driver or passenger?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Courts pair up to a thousand-dollar fine and six-month suspension with ordered community service.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: At which roadway locations must you stay sharpest for approaching emergency vehicles?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Buildings block siren echoes at corners where ambulances and fire trucks may cross against red signals.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: What three steps must you take on an ordinary road when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Remaining stopped at the right curb until the rig passes keeps lanes open in case a second unit trails behind.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: On a four-lane highway with two or more lanes in the emergency vehicle's direction, how do you yield?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Leaving an open buffer lane alongside a fast-moving responder clears its path without abrupt highway stops.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: What must you do on that multi-lane highway if changing out of the adjacent lane is unsafe or blocked?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Never force a sideswipe into heavy traffic—slow smoothly and hold predictable lane control until the responder passes.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: How does yielding to an approaching emergency vehicle differ between an ordinary street and a four-lane same-way highway?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Ordinary roads require pulling right to a stop, whereas multi-lane highways open a non-adjacent buffer lane.
sec10-card-sec10-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Street pulls right; highway shifts lanes

visual_sync.text_span: Street pulls right; highway shifts lanes

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: What minimum following distance must you keep behind a fire truck answering an emergency?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Fire engines stop abruptly at hydrants or unroll hoses across lanes, needing a full five-hundred-foot cushion.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: What minimum following distance must you keep behind a police vehicle responding to an emergency?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Arizona sets a separate three-hundred-foot buffer behind responding police cruisers—a favorite exam contrast with fire rigs.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does Arizona's required following distance behind a responding fire truck compare with a responding police car?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Lock both numbers separately because MVD exams love mixing five hundred feet for fire with three hundred for police.
sec10-card-sec10-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred fire, three hundred police

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred fire, three hundred police

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: What restriction applies to the street block where an emergency vehicle has stopped to work an incident?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Sightseers crowding into an active incident block trap ambulances and block fire hoses.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: What primary action does Arizona's Move-Over law require when passing any stopped roadside vehicle with flashing lights?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: Opening an entire empty lane beside a shoulder stop shields officers, tow operators, and stranded motorists from mirror strikes.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: Under Arizona's Move-Over law, what must you do when traffic makes changing lanes impossible or unsafe?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: Dropping speed sharply cuts wind blast and gives stopping margin if someone steps beside their door.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: Does Arizona's Move-Over law let you freely pick slowing down when an open lane is available?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Slowing down is strictly the backup option when traffic or road width blocks a safe lane change.
sec10-card-sec10-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Move over first; slow if blocked

visual_sync.text_span: Move over first; slow if blocked

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: Which types of pulled-over vehicles with flashing lights are protected by Arizona's Move-Over law?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Arizona extends Move-Over protection beyond police, tow, and highway trucks to any stranded private car flashing hazards.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Why don't you need to check whether flashing roadside lights are red, blue, or amber hazards before moving over?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Treating hazard blinkers on a family sedan just like patrol strobes saves stranded tire-changers on busy shoulders.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: On which Arizona roadways does the Move-Over law apply?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: Drivers wrongly think Move-Over stops at interstate off-ramps, yet multi-lane city arterials enforce the same rule.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.question_text: When must drivers yield right-of-way to vehicles traveling in a funeral procession?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.teaching_text: Never cut into a gap between cars trailing a funeral escort car flashing red or blue lights.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.question_text: On an undivided roadway, which traffic directions must stop completely before reaching a loading or unloading school bus?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.teaching_text: Children cross across oncoming lanes in front of the yellow hood, requiring both directions to halt.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.question_text: What two visual devices show that a school bus is stopped to load or unload students?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.teaching_text: Alternating red lamps paired with the swing-out octagon turn the roadway around the bus into a stop zone.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.question_text: Once stopped for a school bus, what must happen before you may start moving again?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.teaching_text: Pulling out just because you stop seeing children misses late runners until the driver retracts the arm and lights.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: Which two events legally release waiting traffic at a stopped school bus?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Wait until either the bus drives off or both its stop paddle and flashing lamps shut down completely.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.question_text: Why must you scan carefully around both the front and rear of a stopped school bus?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.teaching_text: Young riders dropping homework or chasing friends step unpredictably from behind or ahead of the bumpers.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.question_text: When are you excused from stopping for a loading school bus?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.teaching_text: Students never walk across a physically separated opposing roadway during routine bus stops.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.question_text: What separates a truly divided roadway under Arizona's school-bus law, and what never counts?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.teaching_text: A center two-way turn lane or double yellow paint is NOT a physical barrier—you must still stop.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: If only painted yellow lines or a painted flush median separate you from an oncoming school bus, must you stop?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Without a physical barrier or unpaved gap between directions, painted center stripes still require every oncoming driver to stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F41.question_text: On a physically divided highway, how does the rule differ for a bus across the barrier versus on your side?
sec10-card-sec10-F41.teaching_text: A median never shields students stepping off right into your own side of a divided boulevard.

sec10-card-sec10-F42.question_text: What two ongoing duties govern your speed on every Arizona trip?
sec10-card-sec10-F42.teaching_text: Staying within legal limits while keeping foot and space ready lets you adapt instantly to changing traffic.

sec19-card-sec19-F01.question_text: What happens to your Arizona driving privilege after any homicide or aggravated assault involving a vehicle?
sec19-card-sec19-F01.teaching_text: Using a motor vehicle in any homicide or aggravated assault triggers outright revocation rather than a temporary hold.

sec19-card-sec19-F02.question_text: What licensing penalty follows committing any felony that involves using a motor vehicle?
sec19-card-sec19-F02.teaching_text: Turning a car into a tool for any felony crime strips your Arizona driving privilege through revocation.

sec19-card-sec19-F03.question_text: What happens to your driving privilege if you lie under oath about vehicle ownership or operation?
sec19-card-sec19-F03.teaching_text: Perjury on sworn statements covering who owns or drives a vehicle triggers mandatory Arizona license revocation.

sec19-card-sec19-F04.question_text: What licensing action hits a driver who fails to stop and render aid at a crash they were involved in?
sec19-card-sec19-F04.teaching_text: Abandoning a crash scene without stopping to help injured people triggers revocation of your driving privilege.

sec19-card-sec19-F05.question_text: What happens to your driving privilege upon accumulating two or more DUI convictions?
sec19-card-sec19-F05.teaching_text: While a first ordinary DUI brings suspension, picking up a second or later DUI escalates straight to revocation.

sec19-card-sec19-F06.question_text: What happens to your Arizona driving privilege upon a single aggravated DUI conviction?
sec19-card-sec19-F06.teaching_text: Even without waiting for multiple ordinary offenses, an aggravated DUI conviction revokes your license outright.

sec19-card-sec19-F07.question_text: What licensing consequence follows causing death or serious physical injury through the use of a vehicle?
sec19-card-sec19-F07.teaching_text: Inflicting fatal harm or serious bodily trauma behind the wheel strips away your privilege via revocation.

sec19-card-sec19-R01.question_text: How do two or more DUI convictions differ in licensing outcome from two or more reckless driving or racing convictions?
sec19-card-sec19-R01.teaching_text: Classic MVD exam contrast—repeat DUI wipes out your privilege via revocation, whereas repeat reckless or highway racing suspends temporarily.

sec19-card-sec19-F09.question_text: What can happen to your driving privilege if MVD orders a driving retest and you fail to take and pass it?
sec19-card-sec19-F09.teaching_text: Ignoring or failing a mandatory MVD re-examination gives Arizona grounds to revoke your driving privilege.

sec19-card-sec19-F10.question_text: What licensing action may apply if someone is found medically, psychologically, or physically unable to operate a vehicle?
sec19-card-sec19-F10.teaching_text: When medical, psychological, or physical conditions prevent safe control of a car, MVD may revoke the privilege.

sec19-card-sec19-F11.question_text: What may happen if your continued driving would endanger public health, safety, or welfare?
sec19-card-sec19-F11.teaching_text: Protecting everyone sharing Arizona roads lets MVD revoke privileges whenever continued driving threatens public welfare.

sec19-card-sec19-F08.question_text: What happens to your driving privilege after two or more convictions for reckless driving or highway racing?
sec19-card-sec19-F08.teaching_text: Picking up a second reckless-driving or highway-racing conviction triggers mandatory suspension of your privilege.

sec19-card-sec19-F15.question_text: How does Arizona define a license suspension, and what two triggers bring it about?
sec19-card-sec19-F15.teaching_text: Unlike revocation, suspension temporarily lifts your privilege either when a statute demands it or after MVD reviews your record.

sec19-card-sec19-R02.question_text: When repeat reckless driving or highway racing suspends your privilege, is that removal permanent or temporary?
sec19-card-sec19-R02.teaching_text: Remember what suspension means—repeat reckless or racing removes your privilege temporarily rather than revoking it permanently.

sec19-card-sec19-F16.question_text: Which two fees must you pay to get your license back after an Arizona suspension?
sec19-card-sec19-F16.teaching_text: Clearing a suspension takes two separate charges—the reinstatement fee plus the standard application fee for your age bracket.

sec19-card-sec19-F12.question_text: What must happen to the vehicle when someone drives while their privilege is suspended or revoked for any reason?
sec19-card-sec19-F12.teaching_text: Driving on any suspended or revoked status—regardless of the underlying reason—forces officers to impound or immobilize the car.

sec19-card-sec19-F13.question_text: When does driving without ever holding an Arizona license or permit trigger mandatory vehicle impoundment?
sec19-card-sec19-F13.teaching_text: If a driver never held a valid permit or license and cannot show a valid out-of-state license, the car gets impounded.

sec19-card-sec19-F14.question_text: What happens to the vehicle if an interlock-restricted driver operates a car lacking a working certified interlock?
sec19-card-sec19-F14.teaching_text: Borrowing or driving any vehicle without a functioning certified interlock violates the restriction and triggers mandatory impoundment.

sec19-card-sec19-F17.question_text: Which two outcomes on a moving traffic violation add points to your permanent Arizona driving record?
sec19-card-sec19-F17.teaching_text: Both court convictions and forfeiting bail on a moving violation post demerit points onto your permanent MVD file.

sec19-card-sec19-F18.question_text: How many points accumulated within twelve months trigger mandatory Traffic Survival School or possible suspension?
sec19-card-sec19-F18.teaching_text: Hitting eight or more points inside any rolling year requires completing Traffic Survival School to avoid license suspension.

sec19-card-sec19-R03.question_text: What exact point total and rolling time window trigger Arizona's Traffic Survival School requirement?
sec19-card-sec19-R03.teaching_text: Keep eight and twelve paired—accumulating eight points across any twelve-month stretch triggers the TSS order.

sec19-card-sec19-F19.question_text: Which six impaired, reckless, racing, or aggressive offenses each drop eight points onto your record at once?
sec19-card-sec19-F19.teaching_text: Because eight points triggers TSS immediately, a single DUI, extreme/aggravated DUI, reckless, racing, or aggressive conviction hits the limit alone.

sec19-card-sec19-F20.question_text: How many points does leaving the scene of a crash add to your Arizona driving record?
sec19-card-sec19-F20.teaching_text: Fleeing a collision scene tacks six heavy points onto your record right behind the eight-point tier.

sec19-card-sec19-F21.question_text: How many points apply when failing to stop for a sign or signal—or failing to yield—causes a death?
sec19-card-sec19-F21.teaching_text: Running a stop control or cutting off right-of-way jumps to six points whenever the resulting crash proves fatal.

sec19-card-sec19-F22.question_text: How many points apply when failing to stop for a sign or signal—or failing to yield—causes serious injury?
sec19-card-sec19-F22.teaching_text: When running a signal or failing to yield causes serious bodily injury rather than death, Arizona assigns four points.

sec19-card-sec19-R04.question_text: Which crash-related offenses carry six points in Arizona compared with four points?
sec19-card-sec19-R04.teaching_text: Leaving a crash scene or causing death by failing to stop/yield adds six points, while serious injury adds four.

sec19-card-sec19-F23.question_text: How many points does a speeding conviction add to your Arizona driving record?
sec19-card-sec19-F23.teaching_text: Every speeding ticket conviction posts three points—meaning three speeding tickets in a year pass the eight-point TSS line.

sec19-card-sec19-F24.question_text: How many points come from driving across or parking inside a highway gore area?
sec19-card-sec19-F24.teaching_text: Crossing or parking inside painted ramp gore triangles carries the exact same three-point hit as speeding.

sec19-card-sec19-F25.question_text: How many points do wrong-way driving and all other unlisted moving violations carry?
sec19-card-sec19-F25.teaching_text: Wrong-way driving sits in the baseline two-point bucket alongside every moving violation not given a higher score.

sec19-card-sec19-R05.question_text: Which violations sit on Arizona's three-point shelf versus the baseline two-point shelf?
sec19-card-sec19-R05.teaching_text: Pair speeding and gore areas at three points, leaving wrong-way driving and other unlisted moving tickets at two.

sec19-card-sec19-F26.question_text: Even without reaching eight points, what extra requirement follows a conviction for running a steady or flashing red light?
sec19-card-sec19-F26.teaching_text: Blowing through either a solid red or flashing red signal triggers mandatory Traffic Survival School atop court fines.

sec19-card-sec19-F27.question_text: What three options can MVD take if frequent serious traffic convictions show disregard for others' safety?
sec19-card-sec19-F27.teaching_text: A pattern of dangerous traffic convictions lets MVD step in with Traffic Survival School, suspension, or full revocation.

sec19-card-sec19-F28.question_text: Can MVD take license action for a single reckless-driving conviction or repeat negligent driving?
sec19-card-sec19-F28.teaching_text: Even one reckless conviction—or repeated reckless or negligent driving—gives MVD authority to act against your license.

sec19-card-sec19-F29.question_text: What happens if you commit—or let someone else commit—unlawful or fraudulent use of your driver license?
sec19-card-sec19-F29.teaching_text: Lending your card out or using it fraudulently exposes your driving privilege to direct MVD enforcement.

sec19-card-sec19-F30.question_text: Alongside alcohol and drugs, conviction for driving under the influence of what third substance triggers MVD action?
sec19-card-sec19-F30.teaching_text: Arizona's impaired-driving umbrella explicitly covers inhaling toxic vapors right alongside alcohol and impairing drugs.

sec19-card-sec19-F31.question_text: How long is your license suspended for a first chemical-test refusal versus a repeat refusal within seven years?
sec19-card-sec19-F31.teaching_text: Refusing or failing to finish an alcohol or drug test suspends twelve months—doubling to two years inside seven years.

sec19-card-sec19-R06.question_text: How does a second chemical-test refusal within seven years change the suspension length from a first refusal?
sec19-card-sec19-R06.teaching_text: A repeat refusal within the seven-year lookback jumps straight from one year suspended to a full two years.

sec19-card-sec19-F32.question_text: Can an unresolved traffic or court judgment from another state affect your Arizona driver license?
sec19-card-sec19-F32.teaching_text: Interstate reporting follows you home—leaving another state's judgment unresolved lets Arizona MVD act against your license.

sec19-card-sec19-F33.question_text: May MVD act against your license when you commit an offense that carries mandatory revocation upon conviction?
sec19-card-sec19-F33.teaching_text: Committing any crime slated for mandatory revocation authorizes MVD administrative action against your driving privilege.

sec19-card-sec19-F34.question_text: Even outside a car, which three alcohol acts can trigger MVD license action for someone under twenty-one?
sec19-card-sec19-F34.teaching_text: Underage drivers don't have to be driving—any conviction for receiving, consuming, or possessing alcohol invites MVD license action.

sec19-card-sec19-F35.question_text: What can MVD do to the license of a driver under twenty-one convicted of any illegal drug violation?
sec19-card-sec19-F35.teaching_text: Zero underage drug tolerance applies—any illegal drug conviction under age twenty-one lets MVD act against your license.

sec19-card-sec19-F36.question_text: What can MVD do if medical evidence shows you are unsafe behind the wheel?
sec19-card-sec19-F36.teaching_text: Whenever health conditions make driving unsafe, MVD holds authority to step in and restrict, suspend, or revoke.

sec19-card-sec19-F37.question_text: Which three crash outcomes allow MVD license action if you are convicted as a driver in that collision?
sec19-card-sec19-F37.teaching_text: Being convicted in a crash involving fatality, bodily injury, or major property damage empowers MVD to act.

sec19-card-sec19-F38.question_text: What can happen to your privilege if you are convicted of violating a restriction printed on your license?
sec19-card-sec19-F38.teaching_text: Driving without required glasses, outside permitted hours, or past any restriction code exposes your license to MVD action.

sec19-card-sec19-F39.question_text: What may MVD do if you fail to comply with a certified ignition interlock device order?
sec19-card-sec19-F39.teaching_text: Skipping installation, tampering, or breaking certified interlock rules prompts MVD enforcement against your license.

sec19-card-sec19-F40.question_text: How many moving civil traffic convictions—or certain criminal traffic offenses—let MVD act against a driver under eighteen?
sec19-card-sec19-F40.teaching_text: Graduated licensing keeps teens accountable early—MVD can step in on the very first moving violation under eighteen.

sec19-card-sec19-F41.question_text: What can MVD do if you are convicted of driving the wrong way on a controlled-access highway?
sec19-card-sec19-F41.teaching_text: Entering a freeway ramp or divided highway against traffic creates deadly head-on peril and triggers direct MVD action.

sec19-card-sec19-R07.question_text: In what two separate places does wrong-way driving appear in Arizona's penalty rules?
sec19-card-sec19-R07.teaching_text: Know both angles—wrong-way driving carries two record points and, on a controlled-access highway, authorizes direct MVD license action.

sec19-card-sec19-F42.question_text: After finishing a suspension or revocation term, what fee, review, and insurance filing can reinstatement involve?
sec19-card-sec19-F42.teaching_text: Restoring privileges requires paying the application fee and can add an MVD investigation plus an SR-22 insurance certificate.

sec19-card-sec19-F43.question_text: For up to how many days may police impound your vehicle if you are cited for driving while suspended or revoked?
sec19-card-sec19-F43.teaching_text: Getting pulled over on a suspended or revoked license can lock your car in an impound lot for thirty days.

sec19-card-sec19-F44.question_text: What limited credential might someone qualify for after a conviction for driving on a suspended or revoked license?
sec19-card-sec19-F44.teaching_text: Depending on eligibility rules, a convicted driver may apply for a restricted driver license covering approved essential trips.

sec19-card-sec19-R09.question_text: How does getting cited roadside for driving while suspended differ from what can follow a conviction?
sec19-card-sec19-R09.teaching_text: Roadside citations risk up to a thirty-day vehicle impound, whereas post-conviction rules may open restricted-license eligibility.

sec19-card-sec19-F45.question_text: What three items get suspended—and for how long—after a first conviction for lacking proof of financial responsibility?
sec19-card-sec19-F45.teaching_text: Driving without current insurance proof suspends not just your driver license, but your vehicle registration and plates for three months.

sec19-card-sec19-F46.question_text: How long are license, registration, and plates suspended for a second financial-responsibility conviction within thirty-six months?
sec19-card-sec19-F46.teaching_text: A second uninsured-proof conviction inside a three-year window doubles the suspension of license, registration, and plates to six months.

sec19-card-sec19-F47.question_text: What suspension hits your license, registration, and plates on a third or later insurance violation within thirty-six months?
sec19-card-sec19-F47.teaching_text: A third financial-responsibility strike inside thirty-six months sidelines your license, registration, and license plates for one full year.

sec19-card-sec19-R08.question_text: How do Arizona's financial-responsibility suspensions escalate across first, second, and third offenses within thirty-six months?
sec19-card-sec19-R08.teaching_text: Memorize the clean doubling ladder inside thirty-six months—three months first, six months second, and twelve months third.

sec19-card-sec19-F48.question_text: What happens to your license if MVD is notified that you skipped court or left a criminal traffic charge unpaid?
sec19-card-sec19-F48.teaching_text: Skipping your scheduled court date or failing to pay a criminal traffic charge triggers mandatory MVD license suspension.

sec19-card-sec19-F49.question_text: What exact legal promise are you making when you sign a traffic citation?
sec19-card-sec19-F49.teaching_text: Signing a ticket doesn't confess guilt—it simply pledges that you will appear or handle the matter in traffic court.

sec19-card-sec19-F50.question_text: Which three court-related failures can suspend the driving privilege of someone under eighteen?
sec19-card-sec19-F50.teaching_text: Teens under eighteen lose driving privileges for skipping court, leaving fines unpaid, or disobeying any court-issued order.

sec19-card-sec19-R11.question_text: Beyond missing traffic court or skipping a fine, what broader court failure can suspend a driver under eighteen?
sec19-card-sec19-R11.teaching_text: Don't narrow it to traffic fines alone—violating any court order at all can suspend an under-eighteen driver.

sec19-card-sec19-F51.question_text: What must MVD block when courts report delinquent traffic or boating fines or missed criminal traffic or boating cases?
sec19-card-sec19-F51.teaching_text: Unpaid traffic or boating fines and skipped criminal cases freeze renewal on every vehicle registration you own.

sec19-card-sec19-R10.question_text: How do missed criminal traffic cases and delinquent fines hit both your driver credential and your vehicle?
sec19-card-sec19-R10.teaching_text: Ignoring court hits twice—MVD suspends your personal driver license while freezing registration renewal on vehicles you own.

sec19-card-sec19-F52.question_text: What pressurized substance is someone under eighteen barred from obtaining using false identification?
sec19-card-sec19-F52.teaching_text: Arizona specifically bans anyone under eighteen from flashing fake ID to buy, receive, or obtain a nitrous oxide container.

sec22-card-sec22-F01.question_text: What two core duties explain why you must stay at the scene if you are involved in a crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F01.teaching_text: Remaining onsite lets you help anyone hurt right away and swap mandatory driver and insurance details.

sec22-card-sec22-F02.question_text: Which five identification, policy, witness, and vehicle details should drivers share after a collision?
sec22-card-sec22-F02.teaching_text: Trade license numbers, names and addresses, insurer and policy numbers, witness contacts, and license-plate numbers.

sec22-card-sec22-F03.question_text: What immediate action is mandatory whenever anyone is injured in a crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F03.teaching_text: Any bodily injury turns notification from optional to urgent—contact police immediately so medics and officers roll.

sec22-card-sec22-F04.question_text: If you are one of the first passersby arriving at a crash, where do you park and what lights go on?
sec22-card-sec22-F04.teaching_text: Pull completely clear of travel lanes and flip on hazard flashers so your car warns rather than blocks.

sec22-card-sec22-F05.question_text: What fire-safety step should be taken with the ignition switches of wrecked vehicles at a crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F05.teaching_text: Turning off ignitions cuts electrical sparks and electric fuel pumps before spilled gasoline can ignite.

sec22-card-sec22-F06.question_text: Which emergency number alerts dispatchers and emergency officials at a crash scene?
sec22-card-sec22-F06.teaching_text: Calling nine-one-one connects police, fire, and paramedics to the exact crash location right away.

sec22-card-sec22-F07.question_text: Where must you never stand or walk while dealing with a crash scene?
sec22-card-sec22-F07.teaching_text: Approaching drivers distracted by wreckage often clip people standing in live lanes—keep everyone off the roadway.

sec22-card-sec22-F08.question_text: How can other bystanders who have pulled over at a crash scene help prevent a pileup?
sec22-card-sec22-F08.teaching_text: Having extra stopped bystanders alert oncoming drivers up-road gives fast traffic time to slow down safely.

sec22-card-sec22-R03.question_text: How does the manual pair an involved driver's injury duty with an early-arriving bystander's scene role?
sec22-card-sec22-R03.teaching_text: Involved drivers immediately call police for injuries, while early bystanders park clear, dial nine-one-one, and rally traffic warnings.

sec22-card-sec22-F09.question_text: Under what injury condition must crashed vehicles be moved off the main traveled roadway?
sec22-card-sec22-F09.teaching_text: Arizona's quick-clearance rule kicks in whenever a collision involves neither serious physical injury nor fatality.

sec22-card-sec22-F10.question_text: Who is allowed to move a minor-crash vehicle off the road, and what three vehicle/safety conditions apply?
sec22-card-sec22-F10.teaching_text: Any licensed driver may move it if it drives under its own power without towing and adds zero damage or hazard.

sec22-card-sec22-F11.question_text: Does moving your car off the roadway before police arrive make you legally at fault for the crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F11.teaching_text: Drivers often freeze in live lanes fearing blame—Arizona law explicitly shields lane-clearing moves from implying fault.

sec22-card-sec22-R02.question_text: Why shouldn't fear of legal blame keep you blocking traffic after a minor fender-bender?
sec22-card-sec22-R02.teaching_text: Clearing operable vehicles off the main roadway before officers arrive cannot legally be used to assign crash liability.

sec22-card-sec22-F12.question_text: How soon should drivers relocate operable vehicles after an injury-free minor collision?
sec22-card-sec22-F12.teaching_text: As soon as traffic allows a safe pull-off, clear operable cars out of travel lanes without waiting around.

sec22-card-sec22-F13.question_text: Is clearing a drivable car after a minor, injury-free Arizona crash optional advice or state law?
sec22-card-sec22-F13.teaching_text: Arizona statute makes removing safely drivable vehicles from live lanes mandatory—not optional—in minor injury-free crashes.

sec22-card-sec22-F14.question_text: Which three safety benefits come from moving minor-crash vehicles out of active travel lanes?
sec22-card-sec22-F14.teaching_text: Clearing lanes gives you safe room to inspect damage, shields arriving responders, and prevents high-speed secondary crashes.

sec22-card-sec22-R01.question_text: Putting injury, power, damage, and hazard rules together, when must crashed vehicles clear the main roadway?
sec22-card-sec22-R01.teaching_text: Clear the main roadway whenever nobody suffered serious injury or death, cars drive un-towed, and moving adds no damage or hazard.

sec22-card-sec22-F15.question_text: Right after any collision stops moving, what is your very first priority?
sec22-card-sec22-F15.teaching_text: Before touching doors or phones, verify that you and everyone riding inside your vehicle are unhurt.

sec22-card-sec22-F16.question_text: If your car still runs after a highway collision, which three places can you move to before calling nine-one-one?
sec22-card-sec22-F16.teaching_text: Steer onto the emergency shoulder, into the median, or off the nearest highway exit, then dial nine-one-one.

sec22-card-sec22-F17.question_text: While waiting near a crash site, where do you position yourself and where should your attention stay?
sec22-card-sec22-F17.teaching_text: Stand well clear of live lanes and keep eyes peeled toward approaching cars in case another driver loses control.

sec22-card-sec22-F18.question_text: May an involved driver ever simply drive off and leave a crash scene?
sec22-card-sec22-F18.teaching_text: Driving away turns an accident into a serious hit-and-run offense carrying mandatory license loss and criminal charges.

sec22-card-sec22-R04.question_text: How does pulling onto a shoulder, median, or exit ramp differ legally from leaving the crash scene?
sec22-card-sec22-R04.teaching_text: Moving yards away to a shoulder or ramp clears danger legally, whereas abandoning the crash altogether is forbidden.

sec22-card-sec22-F19.question_text: Which three crash outcomes legally require every involved driver to stop and remain at the scene?
sec22-card-sec22-F19.teaching_text: Even property-damage-only fender-benders carry the same legal stop-and-remain mandate as injury or fatal crashes.

sec22-card-sec22-F20.question_text: How must an involved driver fulfill the legal duty to render aid when someone is hurt?
sec22-card-sec22-F20.teaching_text: Rendering reasonable assistance includes dialing nine-one-one promptly to arrange professional medical care.

sec22-card-sec22-F21.question_text: Which three identification items must you give police and emergency responders at the crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F21.teaching_text: Provide arriving officers and responders your full name, current address, and vehicle license-plate number.

sec22-card-sec22-F22.question_text: What license penalty follows a conviction for failing to stop at a crash that caused only vehicle damage?
sec22-card-sec22-F22.teaching_text: Even with zero injuries, fleeing a vehicle-damage crash suspends your Arizona license for one full year.

sec22-card-sec22-F23.question_text: What license loss hits a driver who fails to stop at a crash involving non-serious bodily injury?
sec22-card-sec22-F23.teaching_text: Leaving a crash with minor or moderate bodily injury jumps from suspension to a three-year revocation.

sec22-card-sec22-F24.question_text: How long is your license revoked—and how does prison time count—for fleeing a serious-physical-injury crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F24.teaching_text: Fleeing serious injury brings a five-year revocation clock that doesn't even start ticking while incarcerated.

sec22-card-sec22-F25.question_text: How long is your license revoked—and how does incarceration count—for failing to stop at a fatal crash?
sec22-card-sec22-F25.teaching_text: Abandoning a fatal collision triggers a ten-year license revocation measured strictly outside any time spent locked up.

sec22-card-sec22-R05.question_text: How does failing to stop at a damage-only crash compare with failing to stop at a non-serious-injury crash?
sec22-card-sec22-R05.teaching_text: Notice both the time triple and the upgrade—one-year suspension for damage becomes three-year revocation once anyone is hurt.

sec22-card-sec22-R06.question_text: How do Arizona's revocations for fleeing a serious-injury crash versus a fatal crash compare—including prison time?
sec22-card-sec22-R06.teaching_text: Serious injury revokes five years and death revokes ten, with neither clock counting days spent incarcerated.

sec22-card-sec22-F26.question_text: Which two national leadership groups approved the traffic-stop guidance in Arizona's manual?
sec22-card-sec22-F26.teaching_text: National associations of motor-vehicle administrators and law-enforcement executives jointly endorsed these roadside safety steps.

sec22-card-sec22-F27.question_text: What legal threshold prompts a law-enforcement officer to pull a driver over?
sec22-card-sec22-F27.teaching_text: Officers initiate traffic stops whenever reasonable suspicion points to a traffic infraction or criminal offense.

sec22-card-sec22-F28.question_text: How should both you and your passengers behave as soon as police lights flash behind you?
sec22-card-sec22-F28.teaching_text: Keeping everyone inside the cabin calm and cooperative lowers tension from the very first moment.

sec22-card-sec22-F29.question_text: What signaling and positioning steps belong to pulling over for emergency lights?
sec22-card-sec22-F29.teaching_text: Click your turn signal immediately to acknowledge the officer, then guide safely off or to the road edge.

sec22-card-sec22-F30.question_text: Which two things inside your car should you turn off once parked for a traffic stop?
sec22-card-sec22-F30.teaching_text: Killing the engine shows you aren't fleeing while muting music or podcasts lets clear instructions carry.

sec22-card-sec22-F31.question_text: During a routine traffic stop, when should you step out of your vehicle?
sec22-card-sec22-F31.teaching_text: Opening your door uninvited looks aggressive and puts you near passing traffic—stay seated unless instructed out.

sec22-card-sec22-F32.question_text: What cabin light should you switch on during a nighttime stop, and what cruiser light should you expect?
sec22-card-sec22-F32.teaching_text: Flipping on your dome light reassures the approaching officer, who will often illuminate your car with a bright spotlight.

sec22-card-sec22-F33.question_text: Where should your hands rest throughout a traffic stop?
sec22-card-sec22-F33.teaching_text: Resting both hands on the steering wheel—or another clearly visible spot—eliminates officer concern over hidden reaches.

sec22-card-sec22-F34.question_text: Whose roadside instructions apply to both you and every passenger in your car?
sec22-card-sec22-F34.teaching_text: Both drivers and passengers must comply promptly with every safety direction given by the stopping officer.

sec22-card-sec22-F35.question_text: Because officers sometimes walk up on the passenger side, which window do you lower?
sec22-card-sec22-F35.teaching_text: Freeway traffic often makes a right-side approach safer for police—roll down whichever side the officer approaches.

sec22-card-sec22-F36.question_text: At what exact point in a traffic stop should you inform the officer if a weapon is in the vehicle?
sec22-card-sec22-F36.teaching_text: Calmly disclosing any firearm or weapon right at initial greeting prevents dangerous surprises when opening compartments.

sec22-card-sec22-F37.question_text: When should you reach into your pocket, purse, or glovebox for your license and registration?
sec22-card-sec22-F37.teaching_text: Diving toward a console or pocket as an officer walks up mimics reaching for a weapon—wait to be asked.

sec22-card-sec22-R07.question_text: How do weapon disclosure timing and reaching for documents pair together at a stop?
sec22-card-sec22-R07.teaching_text: Speak up right at first contact about any weapon while keeping hands visible until instructed to reach.

sec22-card-sec22-R08.question_text: What is the default rule on staying in your car, and what two rules apply if the officer asks you out?
sec22-card-sec22-R08.teaching_text: Remain seated inside unless asked out—and if asked out, keep hands visible and stand exactly where directed.

sec22-card-sec22-F38.question_text: What will an officer normally explain, and which three documents will they ask to see?
sec22-card-sec22-F38.teaching_text: Officers typically state why you were stopped and request your driver license, insurance proof, and registration.

sec22-card-sec22-F39.question_text: What two-step courtesy applies if your registration or wallet is tucked out of immediate reach?
sec22-card-sec22-F39.teaching_text: Tell the officer where the papers sit and wait for their nod before leaning across the cabin.

sec22-card-sec22-F40.question_text: What must a non-uniformed officer display at a stop, and what may you ask if they haven't?
sec22-card-sec22-F40.teaching_text: Plainclothes officers should present official law-enforcement credentials, and you may politely ask to see them.

sec22-card-sec22-F41.question_text: If an officer instructs you to step out of the vehicle, how should you manage your hands and position?
sec22-card-sec22-F41.teaching_text: Keep both hands in plain sight as you exit and stand in the safe spot the officer points out.

sec22-card-sec22-F42.question_text: Which three enforcement outcomes can conclude a stop, and what may you ask if the action isn't explained?
sec22-card-sec22-F42.teaching_text: Stops end in a warning, citation, or arrest, and you may politely ask for clarification if unexplained.

sec22-card-sec22-F43.question_text: If you think a ticket is wrong, why shouldn't you argue roadside and where do you contest it?
sec22-card-sec22-F43.teaching_text: Arguing on the shoulder never helps your case—save every factual or legal dispute for traffic court.

sec22-card-sec22-R10.question_text: Where does Arizona law resolve disagreements over an officer's traffic decision?
sec22-card-sec22-R10.teaching_text: Keep roadside interactions brief and cooperative, bringing evidence and arguments before a judge later.

sec22-card-sec22-F44.question_text: Does signing an Arizona traffic ticket admit guilt, and what happens if you refuse to sign?
sec22-card-sec22-F44.teaching_text: Signing acknowledges receipt and promises court follow-up without admitting fault, whereas refusing to sign risks arrest.

sec22-card-sec22-R09.question_text: Contrast the legal effect of signing a traffic ticket with refusing to sign it at the roadside?
sec22-card-sec22-R09.teaching_text: Signing keeps your right to contest guilt intact, while refusing to put pen to paper invites roadside arrest.

sec22-card-sec22-F45.question_text: Whom should you contact—and when—if you believe an officer acted inappropriately during a stop?
sec22-card-sec22-F45.teaching_text: Reach out directly to that officer's law-enforcement agency and request a supervisor while details remain fresh.

sec22-card-sec22-R11.question_text: Where does a complaint about an officer's behavior go, and why act promptly?
sec22-card-sec22-R11.teaching_text: Routing conduct complaints promptly to a supervisor at the officer's agency ensures dashcam and dispatch records stay fresh.

sec22-card-sec22-F46.question_text: Which five vehicle ownership, testing, and coverage topics are covered on the ADOT website?
sec22-card-sec22-F46.teaching_text: ADOT's site centralizes title and registration rules, temporary/resident tags, vehicle inspections, emissions checks, and insurance info.

sec22-card-sec22-F47.question_text: Which eight hydration, fire, medical, light, warmth, battery, warning, and tire items belong in an Arizona car kit?
sec22-card-sec22-F47.teaching_text: Desert breakdowns make drinking water essential alongside an extinguisher, first aid, flashlight, blankets, cables, flares, and spare-tire gear.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Which children by age must ride secured in a child passenger restraint system in Arizona?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Standard adult belts ride dangerously high on small frames until a child reaches age eight.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: What specific crash injury are seat-back head restraints designed to reduce, and from which impact direction?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Getting struck from behind snaps an unsupported skull backward unless the headrest catches it.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: Against which part of your head — and even with what feature — should an adjustable head restraint sit?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Resting right behind your skull at mid-ear height stops backward hyperextension on rear impact.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: Why are 'top of the head' and 'base of the neck' wrong choices for setting a head restraint?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Leaving a headrest down at your neck acts like a pivot point that worsens whiplash.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: When must a motor vehicle's muffler operate, and which two problems does it prevent?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Rusted-out or disabled mufflers dump raw exhaust and illegal racket onto public streets.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: Does Arizona law allow installing a muffler cutout, exhaust bypass, or similar device?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Switchable exhaust valves that route fumes around the muffler break Arizona equipment law.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: Starting with which model year must motor vehicles carry an exhaust emissions system?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Removing factory smog equipment on nineteen sixty-seven or newer cars violates clean-air law.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: What must every motor-vehicle engine be equipped to keep from escaping into the air?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Worn rings or missing crankcase controls cloud visibility behind you and pollute cabin air.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: Contrast what Arizona's muffler rule regulates against what its nineteen sixty-seven emissions rule requires?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Mufflers run on every vehicle without bypasses, whereas dedicated emissions hardware starts on nineteen sixty-seven models.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: What two condition requirements apply to every vehicle's windshield and wiper blades?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Spiderwebbed glass scatters desert sun glare and dry-rotted blades smear sudden monsoon rain.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: When is window or windshield tint film legal in Arizona, and who should verify compliance?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Assuming a tint shop stayed legal won't stop a citation on your dark glass.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: Does the Arizona manual print exact tint percentages, or where does it place responsibility?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Don't fall for fake percentage traps — the manual simply tells owners to verify installer compliance.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: When your vehicle's build or cargo blocks the rear view, what mirror is required and how far back must it show?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Box vans or stacked camping gear blind your center mirror, requiring a two-hundred-foot driver-side view.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: From at least how many feet away must your vehicle's horn be heard?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: A weak horn fails to warn highway drivers drifting toward your fender.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: Which two Arizona equipment rules share the exact same two-hundred-foot benchmark?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Pairing rear sightline distance with audible horn reach locks both two-hundred-foot answers together.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: Which vehicles are the only ones allowed to carry a siren, whistle, or bell?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Banning novelty sirens on private cars ensures drivers immediately recognize genuine emergency responders.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: May a broken-down civilian car show forward-facing flashing red lights — and which three fleets are exempt?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Even during a breakdown, forward red flashers stay reserved for emergency rigs, school buses, and snowplows.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: In which two stopped locations should an ordinary motorist switch on hazard warning lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Pulsing amber hazards alert fast traffic instantly that your car is stationary.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: Contrast standard hazard warning flashers on a disabled car against forward-facing flashing red lights?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Drivers use four-way hazards for roadside stops, never unauthorized front red strobes.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: What two things does defensive driving protect, and which two habits start it?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Staying constantly aware of surroundings and thinking ahead shields both your body and your license.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: Beyond awareness, what two action steps let a defensive driver avoid hitting obstacles or vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Spotting trouble early only prevents collisions if you brake or steer before space runs out.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: Even when nobody gets hurt in a crash, which five hassles and financial hits can still follow?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Property-damage wrecks still drain time and money through body shops, traffic court, tickets, and insurance hikes.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Which two attitudes toward fellow road users does the Arizona manual rank as the most important key to safety?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Yielding graciously and sharing lanes defuses conflicts long before skill has to rescue a bad spot.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Alongside courtesy, which two mental-focus habits must stay switched on behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Training your mind not to wander keeps small traffic changes from catching you flat-footed.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: How does the manual's wording separate courtesy and consideration from concentration and alertness?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Multiple-choice questions ask specifically for 'the most important' attitude, where courtesy wins.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: How risky can driving while exhausted or emotionally upset become?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Tears, anger, or nodding off wreck judgment and reaction timing much like alcohol.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: How does the Arizona manual define foresight behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Reading a developing merge bottleneck in a glance lets you ease speed smoothly.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: How does foresight fit inside the broader concept of defensive driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Foresight is the quick situational read inside the wider habit of awareness, planning, and timely action.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: Regardless of years behind the wheel, which four mechanical, weather, and human hazards will every driver face?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Defensive habits prepare you for blown tires, monsoons, inexperienced novices, and red-light runners alike.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Which four visual, mental, speed, and restraint habits form the manual's defensive checklist?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Wide vision, sharp focus, legal speed control, and buckled belts work together on every drive.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: Where do a defensive driver's eyes keep moving to catch developing hazards?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Constant mirror sweeps paired with forward and side checks eliminate surprise merges.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Which three building blocks teach a beginner to drive — and who should coach if you skip formal driver ed?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Learning beside a calm, skilled licensed driver prevents picking up sloppy shortcuts early.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: Once your instruction permit is in hand, where should you practice starting, pulling out, and stopping?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Mastering smooth gas and brake feel away from live traffic builds calm confidence first.
sec05-card-sec05-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Quiet parking lot or open area

visual_sync.text_span: Quiet parking lot or open area

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: May a beginner practice behind the wheel in a public parking lot before getting an instruction permit?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Operating a car without a valid instruction permit in hand violates licensing rules.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: Which three traps — rather than lack of basic skill — trip up experienced drivers over time?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Years without a crash lull seasoned drivers into rolling stops, tailgating, and lazy mirror checks.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: Why is 'lack of basic skill' the wrong answer for what threatens experienced drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Veterans already know how to steer and brake — overconfidence and carelessness cause their wrecks.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: As road laws evolve and traffic volume climbs, what quality determines how safe you stay?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: New interchanges, wireless laws, and heavier congestion demand updating your driving habits.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: What three-part rehearsed strategy defines a 'driving skill' in the Arizona manual?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Real skill isn't flashy steering — it is continuously managing open space around your car.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: Which three changes show that a learner is genuinely progressing as a safe driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Maturing behind the wheel looks boring — fewer gambles, steady limits, and calm hazard recovery.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: Alongside phones and maps, which three everyday cabin tasks — including seat belts — belong off-limits while moving?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Fishing under seats, turning toward crying kids, or clicking a belt mid-roll yanks eyes off traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: Why does 'fastening a safety belt' show up on Arizona's distraction list, and what is the fix?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Fumbling for a latch one-handed down the driveway steals steering and visual attention.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: What must you do first whenever you need to handle a call or send or read a text?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Stopping completely off the travel lane lets you read or type without drifting into traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: Where should both of your hands stay while driving, and why?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Driving two-handed preserves instant leverage if a tire blows or a car cuts across your bow.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: Which two physical ways of handling a wireless device while driving are illegal in Arizona?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Pinning a phone between your ear and shoulder violates supporting rules just like holding it.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: Which two text actions and three video actions are strictly banned while driving in Arizona?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Scrolling messages or livestreaming behind the wheel blinds you completely to brake lights ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: What are the only wireless-device uses allowed while driving in Arizona?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Reporting an urgent crash or speaking hands-free keeps both eyes up on the road.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: Which two non-handheld ways of operating a wireless device stay lawful for Arizona drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Mounted Bluetooth audio and spoken dictation satisfy Arizona's wireless law while keeping hands on the wheel.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: Draw the exact line between what Arizona's wireless law bans and what it permits?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Physical holding or propping draws a ticket, whereas voice-driven hands-free stays legal.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: When may you use a wireless device while moving versus having to pull off the road and stop?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Anything requiring fingers on glass waits until you are safely parked off the roadway.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.question_text: What gaze distance and steering touch keep your vehicle tracking smoothly inside its lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.teaching_text: Staring right over your hood makes new drivers weave with jerky corrections.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.question_text: Because hands follow your eyes, where should you look while rounding a curve or turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.teaching_text: Aiming toward the outer lane arc keeps you from clipping the inside curb or drifting across.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: Contrast where your eyes focus on a straight stretch versus through a curve?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: Far horizon sight steadies straightaways, while tracking the outer lane edge guides clean bends.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.question_text: Which road users and animals may cross your path — and at which five busy places must scanning intensify?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.teaching_text: Intersections, crosswalks, shopping lots, work zones, and playgrounds pack sudden cross-traffic into tight spaces.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: Which two flying toys must children never launch near overhead light-rail power lines?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: High-voltage overhead catenary wires carry lethal current if a string or toy wing snags them.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: What rule governs skateboarding, rollerblading, and bike riding on light-rail tracks or platforms?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Rolling across crowded boarding platforms or grooved rail beds risks falls right into train paths.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: Which traffic laws bind bicyclists, and when do riders hold right-of-way?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Treat approaching bicycles at stops and turns under the exact same priority rules as motor vehicles.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: Why do bicyclists require active scanning and extra caution from motorists?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Narrow frames blend into parked cars, shadows, and mirror pillars unless your eyes look specifically for riders.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: What minimum lateral gap must you leave when overtaking a same-direction bicyclist in Arizona?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Buzzing closer than three feet creates wind turbulence and leaves zero margin if the rider wobbles.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: Why shouldn't you blast your horn while overtaking a bicyclist?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: An unexpected loud blast inches behind a cyclist can jolt handlebars sideways straight toward your fender.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: How should you adjust your headlights at night when approaching a bicyclist?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Glaring high beams blind oncoming riders who rely on street contrast to spot potholes.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: For which four legal reasons might a bicyclist move away from the right curb toward the left?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Expecting riders to hug broken glass or squeeze inside narrow lanes sets up preventable rear-end hits.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: Although cyclists usually ride near the right edge, when does Arizona law back moving left?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Exam questions check that taking the lane on narrow asphalt or dodging debris is a legal right, not jay-riding.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: Relative to motor vehicle lanes, in which direction must bicyclists always ride?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Salmoning against oncoming traffic surprises turning motorists who look primarily for normal-flow vehicles.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: What passenger limit applies to riding a bicycle on Arizona streets?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Balancing extra riders on handlebars or pegs ruins braking stability and violates Arizona equipment rules.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: What is the maximum number of bicyclists allowed to ride side by side?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Spreading three or more bikes across a lane blocks overtaking sightlines and violates state law.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: Under normal conditions without hazards or turns, where on the roadway should a bicyclist ride?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Staying near the right edge when safe lets faster vehicles pass cleanly with a three-foot cushion.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: How should bicyclists communicate upcoming turns or stops to nearby traffic?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Recognizing left-arm hand cues tells trailing drivers whether a cyclist plans to turn or halt.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: How does Arizona law treat riding a bicycle under the influence of alcohol or drugs?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Intoxicated riders lose balance and judgment in live traffic, making impaired biking unlawful.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: Which two lighting items are mandatory on a bicycle ridden at night, including visibility range?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Unlit dark-clothed cyclists are nearly invisible until headlights catch a bright front lamp and rear reflector.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: Beyond mandatory equipment, what rear accessory helps motorists spot a nighttime cyclist sooner?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Pulsing red LEDs stand out sharply against steady urban taillights and streetlamp reflections.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: In Arizona bicycle law, what do the three-foot and five-hundred-foot measurements each govern?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Keep lateral passing clearance separate from nighttime front-headlamp visibility range on test day.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: How does the two-abreast bicycle rule differ from the bicycle passenger rule?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: One caps side-by-side bikes across the lane while the other restricts riders to built-in seats.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: Which nighttime bicycle visibility items are required by law, and which rear light is optional?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Every night bike needs a white front lamp and rear reflector, while a blinking red taillight adds extra safety.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: Between a car driver and a motorcyclist, who faces far higher odds of injury in a collision?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Lacking steel crumple zones, seat belts, and airbags leaves riders directly exposed to impact forces.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: What driver mistake causes the majority of collisions between cars and motorcycles?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Drivers overlook slim oncoming profiles or underestimate closing speed before turning left across their bow.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: How does a motorcycle's compact size trick a motorist's eyes regarding distance and speed?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Human brains scale closing speed against wide car grilles, making narrow bikes seem deceptively unhurried.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: Why is judging a motorcycle's distance at night tougher than judging a car's?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Paired car headlights spread apart visually as they close, whereas a solo lamp hides closing rate.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: Which two weather conditions noticeably reduce a motorcyclist's stability?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Wet slick asphalt and crosswind buffeting hit two narrow contact patches harder than four wide tires.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: What maneuver does Arizona call lane filtering for motorcycles?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: Filtering applies strictly when surrounding vehicles have come to a halt, never weaving through fast traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: What minimum street layout is required before a motorcyclist may legally lane-filter?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: Two-lane undivided roads with only one lane each way never qualify for motorcycle lane filtering.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.question_text: What is the highest posted road speed limit where motorcycle lane filtering is legal in Arizona?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.teaching_text: High-speed freeways above forty-five miles per hour remain off-limits to lane filtering.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.question_text: How fast may a motorcyclist travel while actively lane-filtering past stopped cars?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.teaching_text: Capping motorcycle speed at fifteen miles per hour gives everyone time to spot opening gaps or doors.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: How do the forty-five and fifteen mile-per-hour caps divide Arizona's motorcycle lane-filtering law?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Exam distractors flip these two numbers constantly—forty-five caps the street sign while fifteen caps the bike.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: Which traffic state and lane-count requirement must both hold true for legal lane filtering?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Both halted cars and side-by-side same-direction lanes must exist simultaneously before a rider filters.
