sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: How does the small-profile illusion directly trigger the most common car-and-motorcycle crash?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Thinking an oncoming bike is distant and unhurried tricks drivers into turning left right into impact.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.question_text: Where do car-and-motorcycle crashes cluster heavily, and why?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.teaching_text: Double-checking oncoming lanes at every corner stops left-turn cutoffs before they happen.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.question_text: When a motorcyclist shifts toward one side of a lane, why shouldn't you assume a turn is next?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.teaching_text: Riders routinely change lane thirds just to stay visible in mirrors or steer clear of slick patches.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.question_text: Which three surface hazards can force a motorcyclist to swerve unexpectedly toward your lane?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.teaching_text: Leaving generous side and following cushions protects riders when grease or broken pavement forces instant dodges.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.question_text: Why must you confirm a motorcyclist is genuinely slowing to turn before pulling out in front of a blinking signal?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.teaching_text: Many motorcycle switches stay flashing after an earlier corner until the rider presses them off manually.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.question_text: How much lane width belongs legally to a motorcycle, and what does that forbid?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.teaching_text: Sharing a single lane beside a motorcycle crowds out the space riders need to lean and dodge hazards.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.question_text: What danger do you create by cutting back into a lane too quickly after overtaking a motorcycle?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.teaching_text: Clipping a rider's front buffer can spook or push two wheels off the pavement or into adjacent cars.
sec15-card-sec15-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Forces rider into traffic or shoulder

visual_sync.text_span: Forces rider into traffic or shoulder

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: Why can both a rider's lateral shift and a flashing motorcycle blinker fool an impatient driver?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Wait until speed and lean confirm an actual turn rather than betting a rider's life on ambiguous cues.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.question_text: Why are heavy commercial trucks vital across Arizona's highway network?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.teaching_text: Sharing corridors patiently with freight haulers keeps essential food, fuel, and supplies moving safely.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.question_text: How does a heavy truck's stopping distance compare with a passenger car's?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.teaching_text: Massive cargo momentum means a semi cannot match four-wheel sedan braking if you dart into its nose.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.question_text: What happens to a truck's safety margin if you merge closely ahead and slam your brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.teaching_text: Stealing half a rig's stopping cushion leaves the truck driver mathematically unable to avoid rear-ending you.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.question_text: What name describes the large blind spots around trucks and buses, and where do they sit?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.teaching_text: Hanging out near a rig's front bumper or rear flanks hides your car completely from cab mirrors.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.question_text: Why does following closely behind a wide semi-trailer erase your reaction margin?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.teaching_text: Tucking behind a lane-wide trailer blinds you to stopped traffic or road debris until too late.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.question_text: Why must you never sneak into the open gap on a truck's right when it prepares to turn right?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.teaching_text: Long trailers swing wide first before cutting sharp across that right-side gap toward the curb.

sec15-card-sec15-F38.question_text: If mechanical trouble forces a breakdown, how far off the highway should you pull and why?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.teaching_text: Stationary vehicles parked tight against fast highway lanes suffer devastating impacts if clipped.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.question_text: Measured in passenger cars, how much can a single loaded truck weigh?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.teaching_text: Twenty-five cars' worth of kinetic energy explains why shoulder collisions involving semis turn tragic.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: How do the phrases twice as long and half the distance pair up in Arizona's truck-safety rules?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: A rig already needs double your stopping space, and braking right ahead slices that needed room in half.

sec15-card-sec15-F40.question_text: How should you set your following gap behind farm machinery or other slow vehicles?
sec15-card-sec15-F40.teaching_text: Hanging back lets you scan oncoming lanes cleanly while giving wide implements plenty of room.

sec15-card-sec15-F41.question_text: What typical speed, width, and lighting traits should you expect from farm machinery?
sec15-card-sec15-F41.teaching_text: Wide plows and harvesters straddle lanes slowly and may turn without electric blinkers.

sec15-card-sec15-F42.question_text: What deceptive move might a farm-machinery operator make right before turning right?
sec15-card-sec15-F42.teaching_text: Mistaking a tractor's wide left setup for a left turn can tempt a passer into a crash.

sec15-card-sec15-F43.question_text: What top speed applies to any vehicle wearing a slow-moving emblem, and what must you do?
sec15-card-sec15-F43.teaching_text: Spotting that reflective rear emblem warns you to shed highway speed right away.

sec15-card-sec15-F44.question_text: Do slow-moving vehicles hold a legal right to use public roads, and how should drivers respond?
sec15-card-sec15-F44.teaching_text: Rushing a blind pass out of frustration turns a brief delay behind legal farm gear into a head-on risk.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.question_text: How does the trap around a semi-truck's wide right turn compare with a farm machine's wide right turn?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.teaching_text: Never sneak right beside a turning semi, and never assume a left-swinging tractor is turning left.
sec15-card-sec15-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Truck opens right, tractor swings left

visual_sync.text_span: Truck opens right, tractor swings left

sec15-card-sec15-R11.question_text: How does farm machinery's typical pace compare with the strict cap on a slow-moving vehicle emblem?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.teaching_text: Tractors normally run twenty-five or slower, while any vehicle sporting the emblem cannot exceed twenty-five.

sec11-m05.narration_text: Final sprint over round railroad warnings, fifteen-foot rail stops, lowered gates, and stalled cars. Any single rail warning stops. Chapter eleven is yours from speed limits to railroad tracks, so finish strong.

sec12-m02.narration_text: Time for a rapid-fire pass on permanent versus portable work zones, orange warnings, and doubled speeding fines. Drive slowly, stay alert, obey. Work-zone speeds and doubled fines are locked down, so crush this quiz.

sec12-m05.narration_text: Final sprint over broken versus solid white stripes, ONLY arrows, bike symbols, and painted curbs. Broken allows changes; solid holds. Chapter twelve is yours from mileposts to lane arrows, so finish strong.

sec13-m01.narration_text: Let's lock in white, yellow, and red painted curbs plus center-lane cruising on one-way streets. White riders, yellow loading, red nothing. Curb colors and one-way lanes are sharp, so jump straight into the quiz.

sec13-m02.narration_text: Time for a rapid-fire pass on broken, single solid, HOV, and double solid white lane lines. Signal first, cross when safe. Every white-stripe rule is dialed in, so crush this module quiz.

sec13-m03.narration_text: Let's recap left-edge yellow stripes and Arizona's double-dashed yellow reversible lanes. Divides opposite-direction traffic lanes. Yellow edge and reversible-lane markings are solid, so step into the quiz.

sec13-m04.narration_text: Quick-fire check on driveway turns, checking for bikes and mopeds, and right-on-red rules. Signal, slow, turn smoothly. Right-turn positioning and red-light stops are down cold, so tackle the quiz.

sec13-m05.narration_text: Final sprint over two-way versus one-way left turns and Arizona's one-way-to-one-way left on red. Two-way near center; one-way curb. Chapter thirteen is yours from painted curbs to every left-turn setup, so finish strong.

sec14-m01.narration_text: Let's recap turning just right of the center line from one-way onto two-way roads, signaling right shifts, and never turning on red there. Just right of center line. Jump into the quiz and lock down one-way-to-two-way left turns.

sec14-m02.narration_text: Time for a rapid-fire review on broken-inner solid-outer yellow lines, driveway entries, pulling all the way in, and zero passing in shared turn lanes. Left-turning vehicles either direction. Hit the quiz and prove you own two-way left-turn lanes.

sec14-m03.narration_text: Quick check on Maricopa Valley Metro corridors, six-inch curbs, signalized turn bays, flush platforms, door interlocks, and padded couplers. Signaled turn bays, controlled crossings. Step into the quiz and crush Metro light-rail design.

sec14-m04.narration_text: Let's review flashing Train Approaching signs, signalized U-turns, quiet electric trains, and white approaching versus red departing lights. Never stop or park there. Take the quiz and master driving safely near light rail.

sec14-m05.narration_text: Final rapid recap on staying off tracks, holding small children's hands, stop-look-listen habits, and walking bikes and skateboards across. Off tracks, back from edge. Finish Chapter Fourteen strong in the pedestrian light-rail quiz right now.
